**TOP NEWS**
**Ken Paxton finalizes divorce from state Sen. Angela Paxton days after his U.S. Senate loss**
Outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton’s nearly 40-year marriage to state Sen. Angela Paxton ended this week, according to his attorney and reporting from The New York Times. Angela Paxton, R-McKinney, filed in July 2025 on “biblical grounds,” citing recent discoveries; the couple had not lived together since mid-2024. Terms remain private. The personal issues featured heavily in the Senate race that Democrat James Talarico won by double digits on Nov. 3. ([KERA](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [USA Today](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Chron](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [The Hill](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Democrats chart course for 2027 session after historic sweep; House majority projected**
Democrats won every statewide executive race on Nov. 3 (governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, comptroller, land commissioner, agriculture commissioner, railroad commissioner) for the first time since the early 1990s, plus the U.S. Senate (Talarico over Paxton) and a projected Texas House majority (roughly 83–67 after flipping about 21 seats). Republicans retain the Senate (19–12). Bill filing is underway for the January 2027 session. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (first Latina governor; first Democrat since Ann Richards) is assembling a transition team and has pledged early action on education, including reviewing the school voucher/education savings account program. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [CNN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Reuters](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Washington Post](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Parents of students with disabilities and voucher advocates watch Hinojosa plans closely**
More than 18,800 students with disabilities currently use the state’s education savings accounts. Democrats have vowed to end or defund the program; Hinojosa has line-item veto authority over funding even if full repeal requires legislation. Senate confirmation of a new Education Commissioner (she has pledged to replace Mike Morath) faces hurdles with a Republican Senate majority. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Talarico stresses bipartisanship as Hinojosa sets Jan. 19 inauguration**
Talarico has emphasized unity in early comments. Hinojosa’s inauguration is set for Jan. 19. Nathan Johnson (attorney general-elect) has said he will review ongoing Paxton-era investigations and lawsuits. Comptroller-elect Sarah Eckhardt has sought early input on the revenue estimate. Four women are expected to lead major statewide offices for the first time. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Statewide Democratic wins reverse recent South Texas gains by Republicans**
James Talarico carried most predominantly Hispanic South Texas counties by large margins, including Hidalgo County by 46 points after Trump had won it by 3 in 2024. Similar swings appeared in Cameron County. Analysts noted the results erased multiple cycles of Republican gains with Latino voters. ([CNN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Washington Post](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
|
---
**STATE GOVERNMENT / #TXLEGE**
**Democrats set to control Texas House; Senfronia Thompson seeks speaker**
Democrats will control the House and elect the speaker (Rep. Senfronia Thompson of Houston has announced a bid and claimed majority support). The Republican Senate remains a check. Proposals already circulating include expanding Medicaid, marijuana legalization, abortion changes, data-center limits, and property-tax measures. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Dallas Morning News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**More than 1,200 bills filed as lawmakers outline 2027 priorities**
Lawmakers filed more than 1,200 bills in the opening days of the pre-filing period, with the bulk from the new Democratic House majority. Priorities include expanding Medicaid eligibility under the ACA, repealing the $1 billion education savings account program, ending sales-tax exemptions for data centers, legalizing adult-use marijuana, and rolling back certain border-security and immigration statutes. Republicans have filed measures focused on further property-tax relief and restrictions on local-government lobbying. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Dallas Morning News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [KERA](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [NBC DFW](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Divided Legislature convenes Jan. 12 under Democratic governor and House**
The 90th Legislature convenes Jan. 12. With a Democratic governor, Democratic House, and Republican Senate (led by Lt. Gov.-elect Vikki Goodwin), most major legislation will require cross-chamber compromise. Goodwin has signaled interest in THC regulation short of a full ban, clean-water issues, and affordable housing. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [USA Today](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Johnson and Eckhardt prepare to take AG and comptroller posts**
Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson (Dallas Democrat) will succeed Paxton and has indicated he will examine ongoing litigation and investigations from the prior administration. Comptroller-elect Sarah Eckhardt (Austin Democrat) will oversee revenue estimates, tax collections, and the education savings account program and has pledged scrutiny of the latter. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Dallas Morning News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Medicaid expansion, data centers and school vouchers among early bill topics**
Multiple measures address Medicaid expansion under the Affordable Care Act. Others target the education savings account program for repeal and seek greater oversight or tax changes for data centers. Some Republican filings focus on property-tax relief and limits on local lobbying. ([NBC DFW](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
|

**LOCAL GOVERNMENT**
**Austin voters approve $295 million parks and libraries bond package**
Austin voters approved a $295 million bond package on Nov. 3: Proposition A ($260 million for parks, recreation facilities, trails, and land acquisition) and Proposition B ($35 million for public libraries, including renovations at the Hampton at Oak Hill branch and planning for a Colony Park branch). Both passed with roughly 60% support. Voters also approved seven of ten proposed City Charter amendments, most of them technical. ([City of Austin](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Austin Free Press](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Austin Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Proposition I independent-audit measure fails**
Proposition I, which would have required independent outside audits of city spending every five years and conditioned future tax-rate elections on completed audits, failed with about 44% of the vote. The measure had drawn significant spending and opposition from city-employee unions and most of the current council. ([Austin Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Texas Scorecard](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Austin Free Press](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Austin City Council results force three December runoffs**
City Council results were mixed. District 8 open-seat candidate Selena Xie won outright (roughly 64%). District 9 incumbent Zohaib “Zo” Qadri narrowly cleared 50%. Incumbents José Velásquez (District 3) and Ryan Alter (District 5) advanced to Dec. 12 runoffs against Neha Shah and David Weinberg, respectively. District 1 (open seat) is also in a runoff between Amber Goodwin and Misael Ramos. ([Austin Free Press](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Austin Bulldog](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Ballotpedia](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Proposed Congress Avenue tower seeks zoning for up to 1,200 feet**
A rezoning request is pending for a proposed Congress Avenue project (“Project Bolo”) that would allow a hotel/condo tower up to 1,200 feet—potentially taller than the current Waterline. The application seeks density-bonus zoning in exchange for community benefits. ([Austin American-Statesman](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**City Council to canvass election results and order runoffs this week**
Austin City Council agendas include resolutions canvassing the Nov. 3 bond and general election results and ordering a Dec. 12 runoff for Districts 1, 3 and 5. A work session is also scheduled. ([City of Austin](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [City of Austin](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
|

**TEXANS IN WASHINGTON (ADMINISTRATION / U.S. CONGRESS)**
**James Talarico wins Texas Senate seat by double digits**
James Talarico’s double-digit Senate victory ends decades of Republican control of the seat and pairs him with Ted Cruz in the Texas delegation beginning in January. Early post-election comments from Talarico have stressed bipartisanship. ([CNN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Reuters](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**GOP mid-decade redistricting backfires; delegation set for 24-14 split**
Republicans’ 2025 mid-decade congressional redistricting, intended to produce a 30–8 GOP majority in the Texas House delegation, largely backfired. Democrats held or flipped most targeted seats; the projected result is 24 Republicans and 14 Democrats—one net Democratic gain from the prior map. Notable outcomes include Bobby Pulido defeating incumbent Monica De La Cruz in TX-15 and Katy Padilla Stout defeating Brandon Herrera in TX-23. South Texas Democratic incumbents Henry Cuellar and Vicente Gonzalez also held on. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Houston Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Houston-area delegation includes multiple freshmen after midterms**
Half of Houston’s 10 U.S. House seats will be held by freshmen. Democrats held their seats despite the new map; Republicans retained six. Statewide, the outcome left Republicans with one fewer seat than at the start of the prior Congress. ([Houston Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**New map used after earlier court challenges; national House implications limited**
The new map was used for the 2026 elections after earlier court challenges. National implications include a smaller-than-hoped Republican gain in the U.S. House from Texas, one of the largest states. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Ted Cruz remains as Texas’ senior senator alongside Talarico**
With Cornyn’s seat flipping, Ted Cruz becomes the state’s senior senator when the new Congress convenes. The delegation shifts from 25 Republicans and 13 Democrats to a projected 24–14 split. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
|
---
**BUSINESS NEWS**
**NRC greenlights first advanced nuclear project at U.S. industrial site in Texas**
Federal regulators issued a construction permit for the first advanced nuclear facility at a U.S. industrial site: four X-energy Xe-100 small modular reactors (up to 320 MW electric plus process heat) at Dow’s Seadrift Operations complex on the Gulf Coast. The Long Mott Generating Station is a Department of Energy Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program project; construction could begin later this decade if Dow proceeds, with power possible in the early 2030s. ([Department of Energy](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Inside Climate News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [TechCrunch](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**SpaceX seeks tax breaks from Starbase for $24 billion data center and gas plant**
SpaceX is seeking tax abatements from the city of Starbase and Cameron County for a proposed $24 billion data-center and associated natural-gas power plant (roughly 750 MW, 35 turbines) on recently annexed land near the Port of Brownsville. Site preparation has begun; the project has drawn attention amid broader state debate over data-center energy and water use. ([San Antonio Express-News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Data-center bills already filed as lawmakers eye incentives and water use**
Data-center regulation is already a focus of early 2027 bill filings, with measures from both parties addressing tax incentives, water-use disclosure, and local oversight. The sector’s rapid growth has become a bipartisan campaign and legislative issue. ([Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Dallas Morning News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))
**Dow and X-energy project marks several nuclear firsts for the U.S.**
The NRC construction permit is the first for a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor in more than 50 years, the first for a pebble-bed design, and the first advanced reactor approved at an industrial site. Each Xe-100 unit is designed for 80 MW electric or 200 MW thermal. ([Department of Energy](https://link.mail.beehiiv.), [Inside Climate News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.))

## **RISE UP AND FIGHT HATE**
Folks, in an age when social media has become a weapon to destroy reputations and even lead to very real threats IRL (in real life) - as the kids say - it's never been more important to know who it is you're watching, reading, gaming with, or listening to as "influencers."
Some of these figures build huge audiences, and exert considerable influence. And some spread heinous views as their audience grows.
Lately there has been a lot of controversy around Hasan Piker, and rightfully so. There are many others who've inspired similar reactions, from Tucker Carlson to The Tate Brothers.
Well, I just recently came a new one (at least to me). Ever hear of Nick Nemeth?
Nemeth is an aspiring social media influencer who writes a newsletter about markets called "Mispriced Assets." He's been making the rounds on financial podcasts and starting to show up in more mainstream media. Content from his blog was cited and praised on a recent installment of Chuck Todd's podcast, the _Chuck Toddcast._ Obviously, Chuck, having sat in the main seat at Meet The Press, for what seemed like millennia, has a large audience watching and listening.
[In September, Capitol Forum hosted an hour-long conversation with Nemeth](https://substack.com/redirect/4dc60ea6-3a25-418e-a276-9d3453496490?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "Today, I am extremely pleased to be joined by Nick Nemeth," exclaimed Capitol Forum's Executive Editor. "What I love, when I'm reading your stuff or listening to you, you've done a lot of homework, you've done a lot of due diligence, you have a lot of rigor with your investigating..."
Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Kspf5pHk17fr6ICydsiBKCmN2GgxfjBzZCwoyAY-I0I?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=225289806)
Huh? Has anyone done this kind of homework on Nemeth? Given his growing profile, understanding an individual's views and public behavior would seem to be quite important, and I've grown weary of all the free passes given out. Look, influencers have no gatekeepers except their conscience, compassion, and common sense--or a lack of all three in some cases.
So when I heard him say something demonstrably gross about women, I decided to listen more. And, it wasn't good. _At all_.
Here is one example from a video he himself posted:
"Yesterday, I was at a conference; I won't say which one; I won't say who I was talking to, but it opened up, and this woman, huge sales pitch, you know," he said. Then he recounted an exchange with her after his introduction and moved onto,
> And I sat there, and I go, that fucking bitch.
Wait, what?!? It took me a minute, as I was kinda shocked, to realize that this person people take seriously just up and outta nowhere, heads straight to the b-word. He's a financial podcaster, and he just openly talks about women this way.
_Was he an apprentice to Lou Dobbs?_
You know what, let's put the jokes aside, it's time for us all to rise up to take on this kind of hate.
Nemeth has also said some incredibly dehumanizing things about Jews, using age-old tropes. Here's an[ excerpt from one of his newsletter posts](https://substack.com/redirect/e9ffcc08-9ea3-4faa-bb0e-699deabef616?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from April:
> _Israel 's grip on the United States looks weaker today than it did a week ago...I am very critical of private equity guys, insurance commissioners, and the assortment of financial **vermin** who lie for a living. I think most of them are **parasites** , but I do not usually call them evil. I am much closer to that word here..._
Here's the thing. One can offer valid critiques of Israel. But that's not what this is. Isarel has no "grip on the United States." Nemeth plays into an age old stereotype of Jews as "all powerful" and controlling others, not to mention as financiers and borderline "evil."
This is when rhetoric around Israel can be dangerous and cross the line into antisemitism.
Nemeth also uses dehumanizing language--literally rhetoric right out of the Nazi playbook. Language employed by autocratic regimes from Pol Pot ("microbes" and "worms") to the genocidaires in Rwanda ("cockroaches"). Here, it's "vermin" and "parasites."
This is like a formula for stochastic terrorism. The very real concept that you can't predict where or when violence will happen when you share conspiracies, and _make others less than human_. But you can predict _it will happen_ , as its _likelihood statistically increases because of these very words_.
It's much easier to commit violence against those whom you see as subhuman.
This is why we need to call out this garbage, and why this guy should not be amplified by Capitol Forum, Chuck Todd or anyone else. It's why many of us don't want Tucker Carlson on our TVs or Hasan Piker anywhere near a campaign trail.
Nemeth added the following in a[ social media post](https://substack.com/redirect/8c2ba4ec-e5b4-454a-bf92-5ee62cd28730?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> _If you read the article, the biggest win is_
> _Bibi is sent back to the Stone Age_
> _Iran is now a superpower lol_
**I have criticized Benjamin Netanyahu plenty** , but advocating murder is revolting, and wrong, and the destruction of a society--which is what sending it back to the Stone Age means--is beyond gross. _Are we good with nearly eight million Jews and over two million Arabs --being sent to the Stone Age_?
That statement is incredibly irresponsible, one of the reasons when I launch my harshest criticisms, and say someone needs to be "taken out" or we need to "get rid of them" **I 'm always careful to say "rhetorically" or "politically" and make clear I'm not advocating violence**.
_[Those of us with larger platforms have this responsibility](https://substack.com/redirect/1b17ed8e-95eb-4f33-be4a-72da541b55ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[.](https://substack.com/redirect/1b17ed8e-95eb-4f33-be4a-72da541b55ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And of course, the government of Iran is not only a state sponsor of terror, where human rights groups have documented scores of executions of democracy activists, of women not *appropriately dressed* or who speak out. The LGBTQ community and independent journalists are targeted. Per the same human rights groups, **Iran has killed up to 36,500 of its own people in 2025-2026**. So, "Iran is now a superpower, lol?" Not funny. Particularly to their families. It's ghoulish.
Maybe there needs to be a professional organization (like journalists have) for influencers with a code of ethical behavior. Though journalists haven't been doing the best job themselves these days. So perhaps we all need to police this kind of irresponsible language, and let the guilty party know what we think of them.
Which is why I'm writing this.
Support those of us who take on the hard fights. You power this Substack. Please consider a paid subscription
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Kspf5pHk17fr6ICydsiBKCmN2GgxfjBzZCwoyAY-I0I?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=225289806)
Because as I've made clear before, this is much closer to inciting riot than it is to free speech. It shouldn't be tolerated. And people should know about it, particularly when someone like Nemeth is cited by legacy journalists like Chuck Todd and praised by publications like Capitol Forum.

Look, I can be incredibly harsh in my writing, using sarcasm, over-the-top metaphor and mockery to make my points. But you won't catch me utlizing terms Nazis used to turn human beings into easily discardable creatures.
We are in a time when the public discourse is filled with misogyny, antisemitic rhetoric, and outright hate. You don't have to look too far on social media to find it. And it has led to very real IRL consequences, including political assassination.
As a society, we need to reject this behavior. And when we see it we should call out those responsible.

Mark

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Desert Rose
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
It’s known for its ability to bloom even in the most challenging environments.
#

Team,
Can I tell you a story? It has to do with this brooch:
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261117-1-b&t=1&akid=12082%2E3935704%2Ec3kTQn)
I grew up in Tucson, Arizona, on the edge of the Sonoran Desert. The desert covers 100,000 square miles and is unforgiving — temperatures often reach 118 degrees in peak summer.
The brooch on my dress is a silver desert rose. It’s known for its ability to bloom even in the most challenging environments. Mark gifted it to me to represent strength and determination, and I’ve worn it ever since.
The trajectory of my life changed in an instant when a gunman shot me in the head. The bullet damaged the left hemisphere of my brain, where the language function sits, leaving me with aphasia.
The gunman tried to silence me — but like the desert rose, I persevered.
We never know what life hands us, but what matters most is what we choose to do in the difficult moments. I chose to channel my pain into purpose.
Some days, I feel like we are fighting a similar battle for gun safety. I know sometimes the challenge of ending gun violence in our nation can feel overwhelming. When we see the headlines after a mass shooting — or when we remember the countless tragedies that don’t make the news every day — I know how hard it is to keep fighting.
But we cannot give up. We cannot lose hope. Not when so many lives are on the line.
And this is the part where I ask for your help:
[**Will you make a contribution to GIFFORDS PAC today? We’ve got goals to reach before the year ends, and we have to hit them if we want to maximize our impact next year.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261117-1-b&t=2&akid=12082%2E3935704%2Ec3kTQn)

name: Chris Deluzio
subject: Should someone run against Fetterman? Should I?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Deluzio for Congress
body:
At the time, I said that was an after the election question.
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=170%2E42639%2ER8w60k)
In the weeks before the election, I was asked in almost every interview whether or not I will run for the Senate seat in 2028 that John Fetterman currently holds.
At the time, I said that was an after the election question.
At the time, we thought maybe there was a chance John Fetterman would be the 51st Democratic vote in the Senate.
Well, the election is over and Democrats have a healthy Senate majority -- if John Fetterman had designs on holding every vote hostage with a threat to switch parties, that ship has sailed.
Although just this weekend he was threatening to switch parties if Democrats elected Chris Van Hollen as majority leader.
But I did want to put the question to you. Two questions, actually.
**Should a Democrat run for the seat John Fetterman currently holds?**
**Should I do it?**
No doubt I have been thinking about it. Pennsylvania needs a Senator with the guts to stand up to corporate power, someone who rejects corporate PAC and AIPAC money, someone who has earned the support of everyone from Bernie Sanders to Elissa Slotkin and has won the state's toughest district.
I want to hear your thoughts. This is important to me.
**[Please answer a few short questions about Pennsylvania's 2028 Senate race. Should a Democrat run against John Fetterman? Should I do it? What about John Fetterman upsets you most? We will review all responses.](https://act.chrisforpa.com/signup/fetterman_survey/?source=em-261117-fetterman-survey&t=2&akid=170%2E42639%2ER8w60k)**
**[TAKE THE FETTERMAN SURVEY](https://act.chrisforpa.com/signup/fetterman_survey/?source=em-261117-fetterman-survey&t=3&akid=170%2E42639%2ER8w60k)**
I look forward to your response.
Don't give up the ship,
Chris Deluzio
**[TAKE THE FETTERMAN SURVEY](https://act.chrisforpa.com/signup/fetterman_survey/?source=em-261117-fetterman-survey&t=4&akid=170%2E42639%2ER8w60k)**

Peter Willis,

Majority Leader — and now we need to make sure Senate Democrats hear us

they expect it to fight for them. Chris Van Hollen has stepped up to
challenge the status quo, and we’re urging Senate Democrats to vote for
him.

We're not just issuing an endorsement and hoping senators listen. We're
organizing to make this happen, taking that message directly to the people
who will decide this leadership race.

We’re not alone. Two unions representing 700,000 members just endorsed Van
Hollen. We’re working alongside a growing coalition going all in to win
this fight — but we have just two weeks to do it and need you with us.

Together we’re racing to:

* Take our message to the media: Our endorsement is already making
headlines. We're working to raise Van Hollen's profile and make the
case for new leadership across the media landscape.
* Mobilize the grassroots: We're organizing supporters across the
country to demand that Senate Democrats choose a leader who will
actually fight for working people.
* Put pressure directly on senators: We're reaching out to senators and
making sure they understand that grassroots Democrats are watching
this decision — and expect them to support Van Hollen.
* Deliver our voices: We're bringing our supporters' demands directly to
the Senate.

We need a Senate leader willing to challenge the establishment, take on
corporate power, and fight for the policies working people actually want —
from Medicare for All to getting corporate money out of politics to ending
U.S. military aid to Israel.

Chris Van Hollen has stepped up to challenge the status quo. Now we need
to make sure Senate Democrats step up and elect him.

Chris Van Hollen the next Senate Majority Leader?

For ten years, Our Revolution has been building the grassroots power to
transform the Democratic Party from the bottom up. This leadership fight
is exactly why that work matters.

But we need resources to keep up the pressure — to amplify our message
online, mobilize supporters, get our demands into the media, and make sure
senators hear from us before they cast their votes.

We fought to win this majority. Now let's fight to make it deliver.

When we organize, we win.

body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, did you see
Josh Shapiro’s message on what Democrats can and must be for the next two
years?

Please, take a moment to read Josh’s full message below — [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23736?t=1001&akid=962%2E245147%2EejOM-d ]then chip in
just a few dollars to make sure he has the support to Get Stuff Done once
our historic Democratic trifecta is sworn in. We need at least 41
individual contributions before midnight to stay on track toward our
November fundraising goal, and we’re really hoping yours will be one of
them.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23736?t=1002&akid=962%2E245147%2EejOM-d ]Donate →

– Team Shapiro

–––––– Begin Forwarded Message ––––––

I’ll be honest,
Derek: This email is going to look
a little different — and it’s going to be on the longer side. [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23736?t=1003&akid=962%2E245147%2EejOM-d ]So if
you’re short on time, please consider chipping in just a few bucks to make
sure we can keep moving our Commonwealth and country forward.

But if you have a few minutes, I hope you’ll keep reading.

Look, I’ve always tried to be the kind of Governor who looks toward the
future instead of the past. But I’ve been thinking about the state of our
country right now, and what history — in this case, ancient history — can
tell us about it.

Back in Caesar’s time, the wealthiest man in Rome was a guy named Crassus.
He created the first Roman fire brigade.

Whenever a fire broke out, they hurried to the site — but they didn’t put
the fire out.

Instead, they stood there, doing nothing — all while Crassus offered to
buy the burning property for pennies on the dollar. If the owner said yes,
they’d put out the fire. If they said no, they’d let it burn to the
ground.

Sure, this story is pretty ancient. But I think you can see the parallels
here in the present day just as clearly as I can.

Not only do we have our own Crassus in the White House. We have laws and
courts and a whole brigade of enablers and grifters allowing the fire to
spread.

Elected officials who do nothing while our economy’s in flames.

Tech companies that track where we go and what we do, so they can lease
our lives back to us for profit.

Private equity that sucks up our hospitals, daycares, even kids’ sports
leagues — extracting profit, and leaving us with the damage they leave
behind.

No, we didn’t quite extinguish the fire earlier this month on Election
Day. We’ve still got two more years of an arsonist in the White House. But
we did call in a new brigade — one that won’t just stand around, waiting
for orders from Donald Trump.

This moment calls for more than just strongly worded statements or
toothless half-measures. Leadership today has to be about how big we can
think. How tough we can fight.

That’s what we’ve done here in Pennsylvania.

Rebuilding I-95 in twelve days.

Standing up to energy companies that try to hike rates.

Criminally charging contractors that steal workers’ wages.

Stopping data centers from running roughshod over communities.

We cannot be limited by the status quo. Laws will need to change. And if
we have to amend the Constitution to make it happen, so be it.

That’s the kind of leadership the good people of Pennsylvania — and folks
all across the country — voted for earlier this month. But make no
mistake: The grifters and arsonists aren’t going to pack up and go home.
They’re going to fight us in every way they can. [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23736?t=1004&akid=962%2E245147%2EejOM-d ]And
Derek, that’s
exactly why I need to ask: Will you chip in just a few dollars to help us
keep up the fight for progress here in Pennsylvania? Every dollar counts
at an inflection point like this.

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23737?t=1005&akid=962%2E245147%2EejOM-d ]Donate $5 →

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23736?t=1010&akid=962%2E245147%2EejOM-d ]Other →

Thank you,

Josh Shapiro

## Ocala Couple Charged in Fentanyl Ring
Agents searching an Ocala couple's home seized [about 6,000 suspected fentanyl pills](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkT2P3CAQhn-N3bEC_F24SOPu0qa0xjDYc4thBWOf9t9Hvqw2Sp32gXkfvTO_PuYPIE9h_Qk7ji66OeBX9siMad4QzmcCChk2BAsW0n2HlcyspW6FUkJ1MximE-caSjt2dQ9yKXFU3VAPSg9DU27joGTfuGowi-wH2zRWVX0z9J1q66VxOJQ0XnlKqU7Jpq2amwEJLerKOmNaY-qilmiJY7p9RgrOP-OJyfmYyMLNxL3048b8yEX1o9BToSezZKWvl0JPV6FCTz4a8IWe7mSzaKWUwmFgCE8vHuR9FhCsyBw9BrEeQRzBXBa0goLYIWc6UbycwqZjFcuR-U3eYd_0coH4hB2zOHjbkTC9vwJzTAGfYsWACfzfWU7gHJk7hfWP4h-ALy8GF5PBHQMLsDsFypyAKQZh4hEYk0PiVysHdyzTaB9f5D3ltitque5A_ntv_J8nP0f9OwAA__9BCssM) and a press that could stamp out 2,500 fake pills an hour, Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Monday in Tampa. JaMaries Johnson and Jerniesha Walls, both 26, are charged with trafficking 28 grams or more of fentanyl, which carries a 25-year mandatory minimum. Uthmeier said they pressed fentanyl into fake oxycodone pills and [sold them across Tampa Bay](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykULFuhDAU-xrYQCSE5BgydGG7rh3RI3mB1wvJKUlB_H1Ff6GLZcmWZfvrOT-BPIX1E3bULro54Jk9loJp3hCOKwGFDBuCBQvptcNKZuYdlw1jDVMzmEIHzgJqq5V4QLfUqJkaxcj4OA71pvu-t0o5K-TiRmvdIhbppGQdjoDAsCZ95zHGFOsG2Q-tgQ4k8t46Y6QxohIdWioxtd-RgvNXPDA5HxNZaE3ca6-3Ut656j8qPlV8Os-zvWCL8VYrPt2jKj793ACpkPF40-gcGQKfm7xBwsZiAfK5cRgKhMs3JcFteVFYGzYMsh-ZerRb2X2dtH2f5D1lqSrRrTuQ_-tS_nnjoflvAAAA__8fOol5) and Central Florida. Investigators made undercover buys in Sumter and Pasco counties in September and October. During one deal, authorities said, Walls drove with her child [unrestrained in the back seat](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL_ypCAMx58GOxxB1LWguMZur73SyULQ7CI4yOr59jfcK_yazCd_Jsn3--c5P4E8heU3bKhddHPA6_CYM6Z5RTjvBBQOWBEsWEifDRYys2xkz4XgYpjBZDpxVlBZPagHNK8KtRhGNQo5jl216nZ4CGhfSrnOjLIdX8p1rRDOGQWdbfqKdNknhBhE0_VtVxtooEfZWmdMb4xiqkFLOab6HSk4f8cTk_MxkYXaxK3yes15P1j7i8mJyem6rroIUW_4WwaYnErK5OSjAc_kVC4yOQlRQqFSB27id_fIzQppQcspcPAeC25fn6n0Q765w5Ah3J7nBM6R-VBYeNwxQaYYmJyqpO1-kfd09ANTzbIB-f-v5h-6fGr5LwAA__8qv5Ks), and she now faces a felony neglect charge. Johnson's young child was within reach of the pill press and drugs when agents searched the home, the DEA said. Johnson, a convicted felon, also faces a gun charge, and Uthmeier said [more charges could follow](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0DFvgzAQBeBfA5sjfBhTBg9d2NK1I7rYZ7jG2JHtEOXfV_QvdH7S0_ve93W5IgeO6xfuZHzyS6RXCVQr5WUjPN4ZORbcCB06zPcdV7YLdKCFlEKOC9rKBy0KW2dG9YHdrSUjx0lNEqZpaDfjAAH9rXdaKlKTAwWkPEk1DqDJuZbN2SelHGU36H64WOxQE_TOW6utVY3qyHFN-fKTOPrwTgdlH1Jmhxeb9jaYrdZHafrPBuYGZh-OxJZOy5k3MD_rthNTFhhjekZLRXiKFeM7iJrRe7Z3jquwG-aVisD1dFdRX0kkiwFFpsKOYi0NzG027vHiELjosVHduiOHvyX1nyceBn4DAAD__wdqiwE) lab testing.

Bands of heavy rain will start rolling in off the Atlantic today, kicking off [a wet, windy stretch](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0MFu1DAQBuCncW5exZOs0xx8qIAIqHZRD5Sql2g6HmcNXruy3UT79iiIN-h5Rp_-__91mk_og4_LGa9sXHJz5K0ErpXzfGFcbxl9LHhhtGgx_7ni4mmGFrRUSqphRqp-5bnHxpqhv8P2tWGjhrEfFYzjsbkY0DQCO257YATniEjrV9fRMCrbqbvGm91TSg2qPerueCBsUTN01hFpol70LVtfUz78Tj66cEsrZxdS9hYPlK5NMJda34ro7gVMAqZt2w6bq-t-FDDtnQRMIREGARNxrBmD_C8UiTVgrJ4kJSxVOiQu0mJcOKf3sv8l6-MiKaTynnm3Pj39mD4_HB-Hp_vn7-fTCzy__Hz8dn74-kXA1GRj3zYfgi96EH27XNGHf0HrBzdeDfwNAAD__yLoky8) on Florida's east coast that forecasters expect to peak midweek, with gusts up to 35 mph and rough surf at the beaches. ## UF Team Finds 'Dark Magic Mushroom'
University of Florida [researchers have identified](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLFywyAMhp8Gb_YBxqYMDF28pWtHnwJyrBSbHBC7efseeYUuOulO93_69H2ZL0CB9tsXbGiXuMw7njlgKZjmFeF4JaA9w4rgwUP62eBGbpZcjq0QrdAzuEIHzgoab7X6AH5t0AptlBHSmKFZrTNXBV4oDUr3g1IKvDODFFwaPSBAQ7bmCSG04MPYD50DDiPK3i_Ojc4ppjh6KjF190j7El7xwLSEmMhD5-LWBLuW8sis_2RyYnI6z7OrIuoOv3WByamOTE4hOghMTpXI5CRELbV7Lm0uT497ya2n7CqircbtW7ndnnlN8R3VJOsfJ4VAedRM8dsGFN53lH--8LDyLwAA__-tV4VC) the "dark magic mushroom," a tiny fungus that's the first known species to contain both psilocybin, the psychedelic in "magic" mushrooms, and amatoxins, the toxins behind fatal mushroom poisonings. Andrew Kunik, then an undergraduate, found it while documenting fungi at a UF research station in Melrose. The small brown mushroom belongs to a genus that includes deadly species, but it [stained blue when handled](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL1u7CAQRp8Gd1iAAV8XFLdxt2lTWmN-1pNgWAFra98-8ipvkHp0zuh8n7flBhgx3T9g9ybksCR_1uhb82XZPByvApgqbB4cOCjfO9zRLoIJTTmnfFzANjz8IqFzZpT_gK2dN3yc5MTFNKluM0pqywbBtFYDt-OqreKBiymsQbtV-Q7N5eOcj5wpPajeAgPtxeCCtdpaSSTzDlsu_VfGFOIrH76EmAs66G3eu2i21h6VDP-JmImYz_Psa0rtuK5EzFcUEfMvQmt7Op9apQ6rvVz0SqPvNro_61Zy3i-gK8Y9TowRqx6JZPcdML4_tj-OdRjxEwAA__8ulICx), a trait associated with magic mushrooms. The largest specimen stood about 0.2 inches tall and grew on mossy palm trunks. Testing turned up an [amatoxin never before documented](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ_GdKC1MXAuXPwN3f1tSrSYBTax8cl2QPf20UVRXiDtjPRp5nu7T3dkz8f2HwPZNa7TQVf2VAqlaSc8nwn5yLgTLrhg-gi4sZsUqL6WspbDhK7wSZPGarGDviHMFVk5GG2kMqardtvSPEPb6gFX6AHNrZMA8zwjIGjUWLF98aSUg4Sub7vGIWBPql1W53rntNBAC5eYmvfIx-qf8aS0-ph4wcbFUHm7l_LIov0n1CjUeF1X88Q9xlcr1Pg6JdSYHdPhSKgRU2Hn6TcsnEuuC-XCx1b_oOt8YXjU4TPvKcaQazCdAeiUafYSfJXs8rjYe879IDRsAdl_zyl_NHla9RUAAP__KcyKSg) in mushrooms, and the team believes the fungus borrowed its psychedelic genes from another organism. Amatoxin poisonings [kill 10% to 20%](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkDGOwyAQRU-DOyIYY4gLim3cZdstrQkMgQ02ESaOcvuVc4VtZoovPf33fy7zBVNO6-0bF7KhhHml15apNapzJNzfFdO6YST06LHeF7wlN4MAzaXk0szoWtppVth5a9QZxbUjK82oRgnjOHTRGnN2Ygigeq1lH4zUV2egBzkKPwRHXbIHT0pppBh0P5wcCtQEvQ_OaecUU4J8aqWefktaQ36XnWrIpSaPJ1eWLtvY2mNj_ReDicG0vh9la0fEYDrgDCYpj6MYTJEwt8hgOoT4x4gvzy3WUpaNh_JcPW-FR9yJV1qw3vGaifvyPB6FQK4xmLpq_eOVck6bNkyJ24Ipf-q0fy65W_gLAAD___r4h8k) of patients, mostly by shutting down the liver and kidneys. Matthew Smith, the study's senior author and Florida's state mycologist, said even experts struggle to tell the species from other small brown mushrooms.

## Charlotte Banks Hit by Nationwide Outages
Customers of major banks, including Charlotte-based Bank of America and Wells Fargo, which maintains a large regional presence in the city, reported widespread [_online and mobile banking outages_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkL1y7CAMRp_G7vBYYJuloLjNdnvblB5-1yQYOcCuJ2-fYZM3SCVpNNJ857zd1psKMaT7f7U76ZNZkztLdLW6vGqVPvBR1d3h4bKqAVPZlMVzpSNdCAABvh4Zy-FMXaG3knO2CNs7CVxMAtiF0X6TlCqYYdYL07MGsMLzeTFGcKuNHyntg2wPAYADjBfGBjrNyngjhNeMagvdNDobKubBxy98upww182ojDEkNRjc-yi3Wo_SsX8dvXb0ep7n8GkaTVt39NraVl4cKpLf2TxKxd3lQtCTXb1jJo9CGnoh2R2YK8EUQ3LkR0W76bO0xxliDGXh3TTedxXiK0X9q8OnpN8BAAD__x-VigQ) Monday as technical issues disrupted access for thousands nationwide. Users said they could not check balances and that some transactions were delayed. Chase led the complaints with thousands of reports on Downdetector, [_followed by Bank of America_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkMFutSAUhJ8GdxgBL-qCxb9xd_9tl-Z4PCgtggF6Sd--sX2E7iaZyWS-eXsuT3Dehf0_nGRswCVQzZ5KobSsED7iZ4Gd4kUJioshH7DFushOai4EF8NypZgvwrKIZjPDoPS0NWTEMPWTUKOSzWFGolWPegKNiGAfFuyqHgPqbcVJj9g4cxcKIQYhulGpVvYPQIvTZFcl102wvqPNlZha67_ii1KIqRwIKXoXoMV4Nt4cpVyZqX9MzkzOtdYW13zj3D6T8y2ZnG-qzGPwLhDPlF4Oif9iZv5-nTHtEDgekInfWR4th5OSQ-CVvM_cQtojk3OTzHZV573LemB9t5_g_M-Y8tcrX0Z-BwAA__9yno3J), Wells Fargo, and others. Payment app Zelle said the problem on its platform originated with Chase. A Chase spokesperson [_called it a “technical issue,”_](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLGu5CAMRb-GdIxiyIakoNgm3Wy7ZWTAJGgJRMBMNH-_ynuf8BrLkuWje-7f5_rEEEPa_uBB2ie7JrpqpNaorAbTv_xquFE-qWALOdUdXb5W0YuRA3BQ61lyPcm2FTqnlZLj7DrSoOZhBjlJ0e3amN5JbxCtHEbTO-8U4gjTNMtBTUp2Qd9AAFAA_STlQwy_0Ho7z95IYRywoScXWi4PHz_5TSXl0naLJceQ8GHz0UW9t3ZWJn8zsTCxpM-Za7tPTCw3nokF4B73Zl41JKqVieXbsPI9NG53rMRvb549x4NKsMgxOX5RjJV7LFvm9lVbPqjc313R7rxCjKGOig39dmCIX4HaT-t8a_E_AAD__7JEi3s) not a cyberattack, and said customers still had access to funds while the bank worked to restore full service. The problems came days after other major tech disruptions, including a Microsoft outage and a nationwide FAA ground stop.
## Audits Find 4 Universities Broke P-Card Rules

## $4M SNAP Card Scheme Prompts Changes
The state Department of Human Services [added](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O3DAMhU9jdxqYssbyFCrSuNu0KQ2ORMlC9GNI3DX29oGD3CANwYL4-L7362P_wJhiCT8xk-Hg90JXT8RMbQ8Nc_4u1XWV6c0Wm_MNPx3ucpKLABCg97PVfpLlHUZn5skRqHUkA_qlXjC_YBkP43HybrJvPyuNi3aEtE74Jnyuy6ysH6O5iQCgAQCez8eilNSwumVVWpKWg5rIRa7twQcFqi1E9Om7flF72JrHZA7msw_zj0Fug9yu63ogJyyMt5CPrfN9OMjt_jTIDeAe9_YPJzL-pi7sgSVQF73gKejN4tbuwteU6hVLEL3aiElkchFFLD59UrHUuojFRcuZCg9yG5tx5xVTin3Rg5pCxpj-RuX_rfnLyD8BAAD__0trlH0) new EBT card security features after federal prosecutors indicted a social media influencer for allegedly using stolen IDs to obtain more than 500 EBT cards. Prosecutors say Mercedes New, known online as Shawty Dred, collected more than $4 million in SNAP benefits by [contacting](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2ynSAQx59GO864iKgFRRq7mzalsxdWJAPowOY45-0z5BXS7Gzx2_1__PravzDEkP1PTGTYH3ump0ZiprL7gil98uWqSvTNFos7Cv5xuMtBagEgYN7vctWbLO_QOzMOjkAtPRmYV7XCuILuTwPrsaD6luiQJlgGsJNax3WZrJ5Q26EPpn0EgBkAYJpeWik5w-L0omZJs-zUQC7wVV58kqer-IBH_FxvKi97pT6ak_mu3fijk1snt-d5XsgRM2MLdIRSuYGd3JpSJzeANtp2l_BGJvGbuIo7RKrCYj0FZoExkicnlBYpxBiuLGrGW1R7UiIRcg2OGk0CPYZcWdQTH_4IV8h1cuuLcffTTqueOzX4hCH-c8z_2_bbyL8BAAD__0iflNk) the state's EBT phone line more than 9,000 times using various telephone numbers as part of the scheme. Last month, the state [began blocking](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOpSAYBeCnwQ7j_4uiBcU2dnfbLQ3Kj5JFMYCX3LefOJk3mO4kJ_lycv695pd23p3bX32QypudTyrJU84U5y3q4_icwSRx0JJXHY2N-jZ6xgZ7DsBBzlcM6aI1z1AZ1TaGQAwVKZCjGKEdoa92ZTU2IAcB0JqhXboOV-iFHUc50DgAVU49IgBIAICuq3shUMJg-kFIJIlMNGRcDrHOO20U4ua09Z_wpliv4ai82nO-Emv_MJwYTqWUukRTnpLh9OgMJwCGU_OkH4LTknk4vTuJhzvzYLmOpPl1x3XXiRJffFj_k-HLhxuy-vaZ4VRFZa7ivHepl0w026Gd_96Rf_vhW-FXAAAA___YoIRp) online EBT purchases and purchases outside Georgia and its five neighboring states by default, requiring cardholders to unlock their cards for those transactions. The state now also mails new and replacement cards as inactive. Haywood Talcove of LexisNexis Risk Solutions, which sells fraud tools to government agencies, called the changes positive but questioned whether the state has fixed enough gaps in identity verification.
## Flat Holiday Traffic Forecast
AAA [projected](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SnDAMx5_GdGaQ8RooXKSh27QpGS0SxhODiXHg9u1vfHNvcI1GhfT7f_x5Tk_0we_uN25ss1umne8zcM6cJpdw2957pFNv_MozJloS_iecVKOMBJDQTUeK58FznqAi2zbEoPuKLXSDHqAdwFSrpdeApPuWSS8DmFmDaYjUo9FG6XleKm8LEQA6AIDHozZaqw56Mr3uFHdK6IbJ55jqvLLjmJzHJbzjxame41YFu-Z8nKL9JdQo1Hjfd30H_AcamnIg1FgUhBoByigbIkolW7n5EHzc5Td2PyV_lERMMkeZE14c5BKTzCvuf0_nL787ocYqWTru8nyaTujGbejDl5v80yYvqz4DAAD__1Oyhow) that nearly 2.36 million Georgians will travel at least 50 miles from home between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30, virtually unchanged from last year. Air travel is expected to dip slightly, with the average cost of a round-trip domestic flight up 17% to $800 nationally from a year ago. More than 2.1 million are expected to drive. Transportation analytics firm INRIX expects the Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving to be the busiest departure days, and [AAA](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGupDAQBNDTmAxENwZD4GATstl0Q9RjN8ZaGyPby2huv5qvf4OfP1Wp6s9je5AP_nS_KbKubt9OfpXAtXLeXKYY32eyRUZ-VkPZ7pn-Wdqwx6kFaEFtV07lYlM3aKweessg54Y1qEUuMCwwNYdWtDAq0_fS7DAPDKNimuRzMNY-wcjG608iACgAgHHsJilRwWynWSpkhUL2bH1NuasHO07ZedrDO92cO5NiE_RR61XE8EvgKnD9rMgpxY6IPkDgij2OAlcAgSsRtfWg829x_vana2umm0O7p8yGSm2_cZO1vV4-BF8mJWTvIvnwVVh_etat8X8AAAD__3nCfRc) said it doesn't expect Friday's nationwide ground stop to affect holiday travel. Atlanta [ranked](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSpCAQhJ8GM7cYRFgDgkvM9tILrVkZkToUC2bd8u2vvFf4867u_r4_r-mFMcU9_MaNHIdl2ulbEzFTmULBbbv27Kve6M0zFr8U_HiclFSmBWjBTkfJ9aCZJ2i866Qn0M-GHNhBD9ANYJrV9e9Fy0Vpg96TMr20vZY9mhnlAN3SN9HdjQBgAQD6_mG0Vhae3jy1VWSV0JJ85FwevFKgXELEJV35pPKY89YktzIfVXS_hBqFGnP9Ushz_ux8cfZ43SmhxptOqBERW15x_1tDPOMeWi54UmqXXGjGyu2eT9reVNr7l1BjU5w_vjGlWI0VWoYNY_q_zD-1djr1LwAA__8PqoKT) ninth among AAA's top domestic holiday destinations, behind Detroit, Michigan, and ahead of Dallas/Fort Worth, Texas. Orlando, Florida, ranked as the top choice.
## Georgians Land Grammy Nominations
Zac Brown Band earned a nomination for Best Country Duo/Group Performance for _Butterfly_ with Dolly Parton on Monday, while another Georgia artist, Megan Moroney, [received](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOtCAQhJ8GbxgbUeTA4b94m_-6R8NIqyQgBnqHzNtvnH2EvXQ6qdRXqfp6LA_rgz_3_zaioX1bTqwlIBHmZc82xveZXJERn7Ta7LZsv51dRCdGDsBBLVdO5cKVFmic6TuHIKcGDSgtNfQaxuYwupcKNlifaHsBA-hu03KdnhaGzQ26b7y5iQCgAACGoR2lFAomN05SCVSCyQ6dp5RbOnDHlHdvt_BOL8ztmmITzEF0Fdb_Y2JmYq61tpXSeotMzDediRngPveX7Rt5QOsKF51Q_LcqP1P0pyWfzsKrp4N_HE027qo-BF9GxWS3R-vDJ5b-OtnLiJ8AAAD__ybQfXY) two nominations. _"She sang her heart out on_ Butterfly _, and I will never forget the first time that I heard what she sang on it and how much she loved that song,"_ the Atlanta-born Brown [said](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAQBeDTmMwtV7UbQ-BgE7LZdENkcAGW_INM0Yjbr3rmCJN_VXrv_fsav1yIIa9_XSLL6zJmuo5IzFTHtbqU7lz8oRNNPLvql-pO70ZU2EoACWbcazl2mnmExtun8gS6a8iC6XUPzx7aZrPgn2ryynU4vVSPeupda8zUzj11HWrdBPv5CAAGAOD1erRao4HOt502SAaFVuQDl_rgjVYqdQ1uiXd5U33MJTXRbsz7IZ5_BA4CB6PUFa9H2MhV_giBw0KOz0pe4HCVRFmWRf6AuZyZ6y1wmEtmyixw-K6oOokv6UuMt9xd5ZJlKmfN5GXIkmuYTqZDXiSvEKN08XL3IWN5k7zL-XMocGiq9ftHhKM1Qqs1uRC_c_NvN39b_B8AAP__AS6XfQ) of Parton following her death in August. You can watch the music video [here](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnwVssHxCwB4ZWbbZ07YiI72xTQbDwJVbevnJfoev3Sb_h_3311xBTvM9fIZPjefJ32rdEzFT9XEPOr3vBTWe68RgqTjU8MHjZSXMCOIH1ay3bSiN7aNCpDgl035ADO-gB1ACmWZzBCbtp0HoEi7o3iKafrB6kulkbFDTRHSIAWACA87k1WksLPZpeW0lWCt0RRi615YVmKnWOYUqv8qTajiU3yS3M6ybUm5AXIS_7vrev8uDHjY7_WAKPi1CXp1AfBf3754_i5TQ21eG6x5TiZqzQ3ZxDTH8k_zfH08nfAAAA__-nJnNw). ## COVID Smell Loss Lingers, VCU Finds
More than half of respondents who lost their sense of smell to COVID-19 [still have problems](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOhCAQBuCnwQ7jAOpSUFxjt9deaVgc1klQNoCYffuLm3uDKyeT_H--_-c-3y0F2p_fdkNTqp93PHPAUjDNLlZa8oYhhJhzLsfyBtVv5ZhFJwYOwGGcrStUcVa2WYy3Cq1u0MColQap-1uzGuVlL20vnVZ6HOWAsnfQPSw8vOz8IBsyVx4AjAAg5Nj6h0e9yE5L7fVNCKY6XKjE1JYVK6Un7WR9eMeKqXVxa4JZS3llJr-YmJiYzvNsz0TuejIxXSYmphCdDfzvSOTWLe4LE1N1B89HqvjmHzIHzT9sfrmZmJpkltdJIVAeRqa652YpfIrLPzerRvwGAAD__9AXgVU) five years later, according to a preliminary VCU-led study. Among 419 respondents to the [latest survey](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGuqzAQheHVmM6IMQ7EhYvX0OW1t0QTexxGMiGyjVF2fwVbuBv4j77z85gfyJHfr_-4ki01zG86cqRSKM1uq-zzSjHGLedcdv8FfVvLPqtODRJAwjijK1xp1th4G1ATmoYsjEYb6M3t3izW0OD0oAFRB8DhqcmB6Z5I2o0aOt2wPXsAMAKA6sc2PAMZ33emN8HclRK6I89lS21ZqHJ68ZsxxO9WKbVuW5tol1I-WfT_hJqEmo7jaE9IW93ekt-FmjAVdpGEmi6WBCMvmjxtMpE7Y1-ZKBMmtzTJ-s_BMXIeRqG714ocr63yx5uqVb8BAAD__z-AfiM), 44.2% reported full recovery, 48.4% partial recovery, and 7.4% no recovery. Researchers say the odds of regaining smell largely plateau after two years. The VCU School of Medicine team, which has tracked a national patient database since 2020, calls lingering smell loss a [chronic condition](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu4yAQQE-Du1jMmBhTUGzjLttuaWEzxLPCEAFx5Nuvslf4B3jvSe_PY3k4jpyev91Btp1hSfSpkVqjsmz5ZF8PijHmWmt7-wvU_WjvBSWON4Ab6MVtjU9alOu8DU6RMx1Z0EYZGMx96nY7jFJhGAOuSt9BrRutnkY_bpucaPRTx_brAwANADjoPqyBjB-kGUwwE6JQkjy3XPq208nlyYldiFc-qfRbPrpo99ZeVQy_BM4CZ-fybU81_M3vklysfU6RE0VeiytX_-FI1xcUOPvMAmeQPUiJAue8p15LhbIr1r8-HCPXUQsln4fj-L_WfjjqtPgvAAD__7WtfNM) rather than a passing symptom. Younger patients recovered at far higher rates. Dr. Evan Reiter, medical director of VCU Health’s Smell and Taste Disorders Center, said patients often worry about missing hazards like gas leaks, smoke, or spoiled food, and some experience appetite loss and depression.

Among 419 respondents to the , 44.2% reported full recovery, 48.4% partial recovery, and 7.4% no recovery. Researchers say the odds of regaining smell largely plateau after two years. The VCU School of Medicine team, which has tracked a national patient database since 2020, calls lingering smell loss a rather than a passing symptom. Younger patients recovered at far higher rates. Dr. Evan Reiter, medical director of VCU Health’s Smell and Taste Disorders Center, said patients often worry about missing hazards like gas leaks, smoke, or spoiled food, and some experience appetite loss and depression. McLean Parents Charged after Teen Party A McLean after a party they organized for their 13-year-old sons drew an estimated 100 to 300 people to their home, according to 911 callers. Police said the Nov. 6 gathering in the 1400 block of Woodacre Drive turned unruly, with fireworks, alleged underage drinking, and disorderly conduct. Lisa Vaughan, 45, and Aubrey Vaughan, 55, each face charges of and maintaining a common nuisance. Both turned themselves in and were released on $1,000 bonds. Fairfax County police released bodycam footage on Nov. 13. The couple’s attorney said an invitation meant for 10 to 20 eighth-grade classmates spread via Snapchat to older high school students. Aubrey Vaughan , said the family was “embarrassed,” and maintained the event was intended as a supervised, alcohol-free backyard gathering. Police described it as an underage drinking party. Amazon To Cover Community College Costs Amazon will cover the full out-of-pocket cost of community college for Virginians pursuing credentials in at eight of the state’s 23 community colleges. ## Chase Software Bug Snarls Bank Apps
Customers of Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and U.S. Bank [reported outages](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uwzAMhU8jbwpM-S8eNHTxlq4dDVqibTWyFEiMg9y-UNEbdCEIEPzwvvd1m2_ovAvbJx6keY1zoFf2xExpXjDc45Nxo8w7hnve3OnCxmlWteolgIRhRsPupBkqq1ciRU1FGoaxHaGDYax23cO1A7Bdb2qDVvXNUFvADhq71IDYVU4XHAAMAI3qrhfTL9elGbqxJVWjIdHWZB3HdPmOLvBOq3_Hk9LFxKPyemd-ZNF8CDUJNYX3I2YuJ6GmAhZqAiijbMszu0A5CzX9mcndsTQ7ZpLFV8ZV4kHJGZQYrHyR91mumLYozTNzPCiV7ypp-3g5713uB9HW24HO_wbi_9V4avUTAAD__3DhhwY) yesterday, with thousands saying they couldn't log in, check balances, or move money. Chase [drew the most complaints](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OrSAQgJ8GOwwgihYUt7E7t72lGXFQ7kE4wVnNvv3G_XmCrSaTL5nM9_17TA8IMaT1L-xoyecp4XVEJMIyzZCe-Y1gxYM2SM9jDWdIK5VJCdVxKbk0EzgKJ06yWqxHVNhUaKUZ9CBbaYZqs2p22PUgdOuNwEUa7PXcdn3bKSnE4qtg73NSSiNlo9q-dt3cz41pB41KgEOmBS6Bcqn_55BoQx_f84mldnmvot2IXgdr_jA1MjVe11Wn2S3-ujFT4y10D6CQE0QeEmH52Zga3QYH8tuVZ89hxxIc8AtjPLiHsuZv9hWCF3zlQrgwNWopul4PTI1VscvrCjGGozNMi3WHED_fo99FPa36CAAA__-o_o2E), more than 5,000 on the tracking site Downdetector by early afternoon. Users also reported trouble with ATMs and the Zelle transfer app. By late afternoon, JPMorgan Chase blamed a software bug in an [in-house hardware system](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkb3unEAMxJ8GOp_Y5esoKNJc90-bEpnFgO-W9WnXgJKnj8ilSJ_Klj0a6-f58TV8IXsOy3fcqNdZhkBn8qRKcRgxvGRXXCjpiuGVFj44LBoHW9gGjAHTDuiUDxpMPvUzkaUyp960XdWZ2rRdvvZli42ti8JSR9VYk-2wc6ap71VN97Focu4vO2NMa0xp6_vNNeN9LNu6q8gW6CirCppYJd6ewkFXmv1POSjenGy571fVd8rKb5l9ZPbxkk0uhmuZ2cfVXgWVJcAp0U-Zfbg9qWwUE0R6S1SQ4DkQXMQcFuCUdkqACm7F9JmDzIAbRXYIJ3mfYMa4CIiul9HzDZvEBQPs6aP_V_SLvCeY5AwTKTmVCEpuDezQw7j_vQgbuyhJZoWyqeHz-zz20_tk7zk1bVYVy4bs_6Dr_wV29PZ3AAAA__--1bI4) and said it was not cyber-attack related. Customers kept access to their funds, the bank said. Other banks were only affected when transacting with Chase, which called it "not a systemic issue." Hours later, United Airlines confirmed a [widespread system outage ](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMiPahvEQOLiEbC69EBncNn1jzMjuAc3fr9j9hM1KKlWVXv17TA9LkVL4azc07Pcp4VkiMmOeZpue-5ttwMKrTc8S6KAUOE-ylTcBIEBPdmE6cILaGY8oUdVoQA_dAD3ooV7N0tp5vqsB3NB6p7TvvHIoAXqlQfa2JnPVAYAGULK_N8ttvs9K90OHsrULVl2LjnjPzf-dEq_o42c_MDfLvtXRrMyvUqk_lRwrOZ7n2SxzuTAuv5LjJSs5vhMxOmEpR0pYRPkUxk38AAqHL5uZUhA-Ulj5StTZuNdJMVK56aprw2Ypfo_y7646jPwKAAD__0w-gEI)of its own, days after the FAA's nationwide ground stop. ## Judge Warned Over Courtroom Conduct
The State Commission on Judicial Conduct has [publicly warned Judge Nathan Milliron](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGyozAMRb_GdM4gh4FQUGxD97bdkhG2iPXW2BlbQPL3O95feI1GheZcnfvna_lCDhyfv3GnSd5bWiJdJZAI5QWPIhx3FC-E1lMu35RemN1iWtNrAA3Dglb4pAUaN62tG6GhCYaxG6F_dH3jpzs8thHNNhKuI6HrYXXWAWyAq8OHaXiqNAAYwLRtB7ehdaNr7b0fV9M7dKprybGkfBNPQm8sW_ikk_LNpr0Jkxd5FXX_pcyszHxd180Gtn-NT0eRFOuVMnP1UmYOyWJQZq6ZyswAddTNY85ctE1HlI92XCSzFf19uCfpiOIx6p1D4Jyifh1rYBs--sIcyen6jT45Y6iALDmlXdsUt5yioHCKNbvJk3tdlVH6QXXtc0cO_yXkh92fk_kXAAD__wdLndM), the Harris County district judge whose courtroom run-ins drew attention earlier this year, following its review of several complaints about his treatment of attorneys and county employees. The warning covers three incidents, including a March video that spread online showing Milliron [berating an IT technician](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O5CAQBOCnwRkjwKx_AoJLnO2lF1ptaMa9wjCCtmfn7U-zr7BxqUqf6t_n-gmUKN__woGOv2NZMz5bQmasK5yNKR_AOyP4HWv7wvKAGlajzCC1lnpcwTNduOouuE2FWXfo9DjbWQ-THbrdfdgIOPU4mmEaw4Q9BKviNln8gM3HrSP3XtNaj9ooZfVtVGEOyvfDvJkhQBBWYSAu9cY7Mn5Di-lVLqw3X44uuZ350UT_R5hFmAU2r_t3IszSuNSXMMtPSZYYyROkJqm1E-UTaqZ8lzvUSk36cmZ-ya8z3FFeVCHJiwIW6UuOtWQGppIlo9-FWd5UO2stzNJVFx5PSonaMAqr7gdQ-rHxLy-9nPkfAAD___5tjhk) who came to help with a courtroom computer problem. He was also cited for the language he used in emails and texts to the District Clerk's Office about his staffing. The third incident also came in March, when Milliron threatened to have a lawyer arrested for asking to approach the bench. The commission's warning states that he failed to be "patient, dignified and courteous."
## UT Austin Tops New College Ranking
The University of Texas at Austin [topped 115 schools](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb8GOiPbIPu5cPEauk2bEg3MAE4MRvYs7P59tNlPSH90de75vA03CDHsywds5Pkxp2Gnq0RipjzAvXDYN-CVCaaVcvmidEDGQUtthFJC2QEmDicNqkY_SnSqJq-s65wy_zpTr95MhC1KaTqNs7Ot0XaUDjtwKKUdZR38a00pZZWWslONlehQTq1xozYIWHWSMHDKDa_E9IAyx2c6KTdT2uroV-ajVO3_SveV7q_raub0sG_5F1Lp_nWq0j2nQ0wpRlqoiDuLNyNGAi4inE8RCZY7iTKtKcUidrpEhv077Eups8fjCjGGYmzVyWWDEH8N-I_hTq9_AgAA__-35oXI) in _City Journal_ 's 2026 college rankings, finishing ahead of Florida, Notre Dame, MIT, and Claremont McKenna, with Yale at No. 10 and Texas A&M at No. 12. _City Journal_ , a magazine published by the conservative Manhattan Institute, [scored schools on 95 measures](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0EGSqyAQgOHT6E6LJgTCgsXbuMvbztJqoVUyKCnoxOT2U5krzAW-v-r_uo5XjCnuy3_cyPFrzuNOR03ETGXER-W4b8grE_qVSr1RvmMJoxRSdwAdmBE9xyeN0AY3iWChJQfGKgv6onS7OrSTOcuAZ4P6LDQSCXWxQs1TmEF53Ub30QDAgBRCQW9EsEH4k7aT1AFDowSFyLn0vBLTC-uc3vlJpfd5a5Nbme-1Of1r5NDI4TiO3kd-d7f8KDumPpelkQMWjj5RIwefU6KFuoL7d9yX2n3ybXHhfsSUYtWmUWLZMKZfn_-45enkTwAAAP__mwB4VA) covering governance, education, student life, and career outcomes. It gives no points for reputation or tough admissions, and no school scored above 80 out of 100. UT Austin [scored 79.7 out of 100](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAYhJ_G7mzxYwKhoLjGXa690sLmd-AWgwV_7OTtV4m0T7DtjGZG8_27TTcbYkj3v3ZDQ881TwnPGpEIy2QflULaLHlCu3gs9T_m3RY3ccZlB9CBmuxC4cAJWmdm5jS0aEBpoUFehWy9WUFfr4OYmZsdl9IpPjAhlNawDuKiZRvMuw0AFHDGBPSKOe3YMkg9c-msawRDFyiXnjwSPm1d4ysfWPolb200nmivzfCn4WPDx_M8-8WXnN5uw8dPoOGjLRSWiD9K90jhwFIDvbrPm2LTV0j3ri4-51g7zi8DKK373e9tMW4_Q4yhStUIdt9siJ91-iW0w_DvAAAA___OX4EQ), earning praise for its School of Civic Leadership, core curriculum, and test-required admissions. This is Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D-LA).
On Election Day, we knocked Jim Crow flat on its back. But if we’re not careful, it’ll rear its ugly head again.
Just look at what we were up against this year:
In April, the Supreme Court struck down Louisiana’s second majority-Black congressional district.
The very next day, Gov. Jeff Landry declared a state of emergency and suspended our congressional primaries, just days before early voting was set to begin and with mail ballots already in voters’ hands.
**_They redrew the lines. They canceled the vote. They did everything short of padlocking the polling places._**
And it didn’t work.

It changes clothes. It shows up as a new map, a new ID law, a sudden “state of emergency.” And the moment we stop showing up, it gets right back up and rears its ugly head.
That’s what’s at stake on December 12.
If our turnout drops off in this runoff, the same people who canceled our elections will tell the whole country that Nov. 3 was a fluke. But if we win, I’ll become the first Black woman Louisiana has ever sent to Congress, in a district they never expected us to win.
That’s how you keep Jim Crow down. Not with one election. With continued fervor.

After securing our largest Democratic majority in over 15 years, it’s clear Americans are ready for change. They want leaders who will fight for them, lower their costs, protect their freedoms, and hold those in power accountable.

_But I know that Republicans won’t make it easy._

name: Mary Peltola
subject: We're running on empty
body:
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261117-1.S1DRfh&refcode=em-20261117-1&t=1&akid=2310%2E1086043%2Etk9JYa)
Peter --
Here’s the truth: We’re running on empty.
While we are still waiting for every vote to be counted, we are starting to run out of resources.
I am so grateful to have had your support throughout this campaign. Seriously.
We started with $0 in our bank account, and we built this movement from the ground up without a dime from the greedy corporations hurting all of us. And we spent almost everything we had to win -- _and we will._
So we need your help again to keep us afloat while we fight to count every vote and power through until this race is certified. We can’t afford to fall short when Donald Trump and the entire DC establishment are working to overturn the results of our election and undo the will of Alaskans if I win.
I am so proud that this campaign is fueled by working people. But that does mean we have to keep asking for your support until this race is officially over.
I wouldn’t ask if it wasn’t so important. So please Peter:
**[Will you please split a donation between my campaign and Wes Moore to help make sure every vote is protected and counted fairly, and support all of our work through the finish line? I’m counting on your donations to help us run through the tape and finally flip this seat.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261117-1.S1DRfh&refcode=em-20261117-1&t=2&akid=2310%2E1086043%2Etk9JYa)**

Thank you as always,
Mary

name: David Hogg
subject: Wins in California

body:
California is proof of a clear shift in power.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261117-1&t=1&akid=4253%2E587540%2ELJBk-O)
Peter,
California just became a deeper shade of blue. Here’s why that matters:
**Randy Villegas** beat the political establishment not once, but twice this cycle. He ran on a platform of Medicare for All, lower costs, and immigrant rights. In the primary, he beat the Democratic establishment’s more conservative candidate, who shared donors with the GOP opponent and was backed by $2.8 million from AIPAC-affiliated groups. In November, Randy faced Republican incumbent, Rep. David Valadao, who none of the Democrats’ previous more moderate candidates had been able to beat. But Randy, a young progressive, won by double digits and will finally deliver the representation his district deserves.
In Los Angeles, **Angela Gonzales-Torres** defeated a Democratic incumbent who was under a House Ethics investigation due to sexual misconduct with staff. Her opponent had the endorsement of the California Democratic Party. Angela won by over 20 points. For Angela, this race was more than politics. It was personal.
Having grown up in the area, raised by a single mother and the daughter of a deportee, she’s witnessed the courage and perseverance of her community. Now, she’s going to fight for real change through more progressive policies.
California is proof of a shift in power. Younger generations are looking for newer, bolder voices to represent them in government. The electorate is changing every year as more and more people are eligible to vote, yet the makeup of our representation does not reflect this shift.
That’s why Leaders We Deserve is fighting so hard to support candidates like Angela and Randy that will bring a better representation and a bolder voice to Congress. **And our work for 2028 starts now, recruiting the next wave of candidates and laying a strong foundation to protect this year’s wins.**

clean_body: California is proof of a clear shift in power. Peter, California just became a deeper shade of blue. Here’s why that matters: Randy Villegas beat the political establishment not once, but twice this cycle. He ran on a platform of Medicare for All, lower costs, and immigrant rights. In the primary, he beat the Democratic establishment’s more conservative candidate, who shared donors with the GOP opponent and was backed by $2.8 million from AIPAC-affiliated groups. In November, Randy faced Republican incumbent, Rep. David Valadao, who none of the Democrats’ previous more moderate candidates had been able to beat. But Randy, a young progressive, won by double digits and will finally deliver the representation his district deserves. In Los Angeles, Angela Gonzales-Torres defeated a Democratic incumbent who was under a House Ethics investigation due to sexual misconduct with staff. Her opponent had the endorsement of the California Democratic Party. Angela won by over 20 points. For Angela, this race was more than politics. It was personal. Having grown up in the area, raised by a single mother and the daughter of a deportee, she’s witnessed the courage and perseverance of her community. Now, she’s going to fight for real change through more progressive policies. California is proof of a shift in power. Younger generations are looking for newer, bolder voices to represent them in government. The electorate is changing every year as more and more people are eligible to vote, yet the makeup of our representation does not reflect this shift. That’s why Leaders We Deserve is fighting so hard to support candidates like Angela and Randy that will bring a better representation and a bolder voice to Congress. And our work for 2028 starts now, recruiting the next wave of candidates and laying a strong foundation to protect this year’s wins. Thank you, David Hogg

Peter, I’m still smiling.

Nearly two weeks ago, voters across the country delivered a historic
upset. Democrats won Senate races in places the pundits had written off,
including states that hadn’t sent a Democrat to the Senate in decades.

My great-grandmother, Maebel James, used to say that if you don’t like
something, you should go further and do better. That’s exactly what
Americans did on Election Day. They didn’t like what they saw in
Washington, so they showed up and did something about it.

I spent a big part of this year boosting our Senate candidates. I traveled
to Michigan, Mississippi, Ohio, Georgia, North Carolina, and Florida — I
believed in them, and so did America.

I’ll tell you, I’m an optimist by nature, but this is the most hopeful
I’ve felt in a long time. Come January, we’ll be working together to:

* Tackle the cost of housing
* Stand up for federal workers, seniors, and veterans

the beginning of the month was strong, we have to make sure our

## Evans Announces 2028 Bid
Rep. Gabe Evans, a Fort Lupton Republican, [announced Monday he will run](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAQgJ9GOwygohYUf2O3f3ulGWHQSVjYAKvZffqLm7snuHIyyTfzfV-35QbkKWz_4Y66GLcEPLPHUjAteEDIkstxJbsler_9yzzXDGGRXComBBPDAqbQgUsHtdXOSQOqRi2GqZsk71Vb79qobpTCDk52a8-Vgl7J1mGr7ARmcrwmffGEEINouej7Rilw_GL1OPXjaKqOo6USU1N2NNHHBDY6_4oHpsbEe-31XsojV-2_Ss6VnM_zbCyGA9Nw7Ss5X1qVnH004NnPsMGK7CPJIIT4DAYzS8_AXEzs90xmXdmZiWFLmDPFAJ5ZyiWRKYwCu_rUSdvHSd5TVkPV8e0O5D-PlT82PbT8DgAA__-xIY0M) for Colorado's 4th Congressional District in 2028 instead of trying to win back the 8th. Evans [lost the 8th District](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGurCAQhp8GOwyggBYUt7Hb297SjDC6JAgbYDW7T3_jJufk9Kf9Z-bLfP-_23wDH3zc_sKOptp1jniWgLVinvGAWAQTw-Ldlv37HV72uRSIs2BCUc4p1zPY6g-ce2icWVdhQTVouB77UTCpuuZuRq2ZEg76geMi-aI5WqY7aVH1ouvGxpuLxznXvGNcylYpWNnFkjjKYbCkZ-h8Tbmtd7QppAwureGVDsytTXsTzL3WRyHdHyImIqbzPFu7lMvlmhMxfV0RMV3pj4TaFLeMpewQ6QYL0o83hRjTM1osND_j95JPEQJ1vtTsbaU9dbgiVGodHYiYmmzc4_Qh-KI06dm2gw-fF-sv2z2M-B8AAP__WgeQ2A) to Democrat Manny Rutinel this month. In the 4th, Democrat Eileen Laubacher unseated Republican Lauren Boebert, flipping a seat that has traditionally favored the GOP. His [announcement came within 72 hours](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOqzAMhZ8mbKkSh0AZMtyF7b_rHZEJBiKlpEpcqvbpr1KpT_Avlofj43O-fz_TD4YYju0v3sixX6eDniUSM-WJTjwKKLjOYdlyeL_jyz_mgscECjqptdT9hJ7DSVOLzeLWFTx2DTndD-0Aynam2R1Y4wczzDCgItOhVcaiIejX3vSzV01w1U9r3WujtLWXrsNVVS9Lg71evWgVLYFTvvBOPsWUcUlrfKWT8sWnWxPdznwvwvwRMAoYv5pPmXBQFQkY6xsBo9Z11G3DmeSnplwC-52K_J7KGZkjbTk9jkUWQpYt77LiEDA22S33Z4gxlK4XrdpuGOInCv-S4ungfwAAAP__QVmE3A) after the Associated Press called Boebert's loss Friday. Evans will continue representing the 8th District until January. The move mirrors [Boebert's own district switch](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OwyAQhuHT4I4IsI2dgmIbd9l2S4ufwRntBCIgjpLTr5wrbD3SM3q_n8t6sUiYtm97A9N8XBM8K0FrUFbYbapKqNlh2Aq-3_TyD1dtWpVQmkvJ5bRa33CHdbBdMDEqb3UHRk7n4azEqPvuapwdlYMpzlHOMUygRZB-HjT0zgkJY4fm8KSUk-yFHMeT1jaKwxrhPM6zZ4OAgC2XU7uCz5SLDTnSK-9QTj7fOjLX1u6V9V9MLUwtv2H_HJhajh6mFsreElPLZh3wTxhvmZdH4ph4wBihQGo8YG0FfeMxE-Unpo1TrgfQFRPuTyTCqic2iO1mkT7P2z932436CwAA__9e0IOL), when she left the 3rd District for the 4th after narrowly beating Adam Frisch in 2022.
## CPW Saves Durango Hatchery
Colorado Parks and Wildlife crews [worked around the clock](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQhZ8Gd1iAwT8FRRp3N21KawyDPQprVsDa2n36yJEipb_tN5pP55xfX8sXUKRj-wkPtNWF5cCrRKwV84InHEUJNa7kt0yfT3y711rgWJRQPZeSy2EBV-nERUPjbQjKQd-glcOkJyVM3zW71eOwGjHAGEBNYMZu6pwy2q9u0gaNbsjePinlIDshjWn7HoK4XQYnM46OaYGeaspt3dGlmDL4FOI7nZhblx5NtHutz8K6H0zNTM3XdbVuLXeX-87U_O-Lqfmm_xH-hPy78IuijxSQFzixcP_KcGyJByo736G6HfObh5iSp2Njam6y9c-LYqTSD0yL7QEU_4ap39zxtOpPAAAA__9liIlV) to protect the Durango State Fish Hatchery, home to about 330,000 fish, as two historic floods hit the Animas River. The river [peaked at 13,000 cubic feet](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL_upCAUhZ9GOwzgH8aCYpvpZtstzRUuSgbBwB2N8_Qbdx_h152ck3w5-f68phf44OPyGzbUZNwU8SwBiTBPeEAsksvH7O2S_fcbLvOZC8RJcjkwIZhQExjyB04d1FY7Jw0MNWqhxm6UvB_aetWDVWqc-9mAajk3vZqlm-3olOxsN9uu9vrmCSGUaLno-2YYwPGb1ePYPx6m6jhaTyk3tKJJIWWwyYUrHZgbk7Y66JVoL1X7q5LPSj7fPp1g0ifStWcspYlIlXyaFAnjnewnQ1wSc76sbAUyK-aLFTiwMIiWFUrmXf7PLoWQTh8XtkEp_kDmQkr2Lvy2g6FSZ23304fgy6Cqji8b-PDvGP3Q6aHl3wAAAP__x4uQFg) per second on Nov. 2, its highest flow since 1927. Staff stacked sandbags five high and used pumps and boards to keep water away from critical infrastructure. On Nov. 13, crews [stocked more than 2,900 trout](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQhZ_G7rAA_6ag2MZdtt3SGsOMjZaYCCZGydOvvLr3CW55dKRP3zl_7ssdfPDH9hseaNjScmDJAZkxLXjCkbXU0-rdlvznE972tWY4Fi31IJQSalzAsj9x6aB2hkhbGGo0arx1Ny37oa13QxpBr9RBC1Y5ia0a2o5avXaKiNxUe3PxlFKjaqXq-2YYgOTF6vHWT5OtOonOc0wN72hjiAlcpPCOJ6bGxkcdzM78zFX7q9JzpedSSuPwODGNV1_p-ZpV6TlEC0F8BfsswiGDD1kgUUycBUeR4USROdq_gnzeBcUQYvHHJnJ88V4ws_iWEBRidP7Y6mTcs_gQfB7GqpPbA3z478Y_vPU0-l8AAAD__wFfkHE) in the Animas to help rebuild the fishery. The fish had to leave the hatchery after floodwater from Junction Creek reached their raceways. Staff also rescued a rare San Juan cutthroat lineage from the flooded quarantine building. The facility, first built in 1893, is [Colorado's oldest state-owned hatchery](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuwyAUANDT4C0WfBtsBoYu3tK1I_qBj41ETATEkXP6Kr1CL_CG93O1V4wp7us33sk0F-xOr5qoNSqWDtwrcJhv0a8lvt_pdM9bxd0CB3UR4iImi67Fg-yInTchgEPVkRGTHjVwqYZuM1KTmJ0OQWmvZ6kVCuUHECModZtH3kXz8YQQkxi4kLJXCgP_WJK0nGfHRk4-tlz6tpHLKRf0OaQzH1R6l-9dMltrj8qGLwYLg8U9Xn1t2Kh3uX9WBsuGzW1UTgaLfxbc19wV4x-vmFKsamIjX-8Y05_W_hlxGPgNAAD__5QacVY).

The Trump administration attacked voting by mail. You may know the "Bah! Humbug!"-spouting Ebenezer Scrooge and his ghostly visitors from Charles Dickens’ _A Christmas Carol_.

What you may have missed on screen or in the pages of the book is the message of Christian faith at the heart of the story.

That’s why Hillsdale College produced the online course _“Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol”_ —and now you can receive the complete course on **DVD** as our special thank-you for your gift of **$100 or more**.

In this course, you’ll learn from Hillsdale Professor Dwight Lindley about how a Bible verse gets to the heart of Scrooge’s surprising encounters in _A Christmas Carol_ and reveals the true mystery of Christmas: Christ’s incarnation as a baby in Bethlehem.

**That’s why I hope you’ll claim your DVD box set of this excellent course for viewing at home or with a study group. You can use the secure link below to claim your DVD today:

**[https://secure.hillsdale.edu/donate/christmas-carol-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckctq5DAQRb9G3tno4VcvvAhxOwxMJ4QsZikqUtkukCwjyT3k7wcPPfmA2VZdzqHq_rrpG5CjbXkFjwOlpG2wOq-Y44H-K2WMX2E2a6SUPSQtuWxLIUrRaTCZ7qhrKOzQSNHPfYGD6C71RfJO1MU62L5Wpud1g589ciUbMBcOgJ_Smh7muaDh5AkhOqG4rFXFRTNjo7ABbmXTNqzmx24hY0VbIovJhLDvwVEmk6oQl8INa857YuqJyYnJKaE5IlYrOZcsOKzQHkxONmyQkcnp-5TSQAyutHfL1JRw8bjl52CRqZEr0conzqfn2_VlfBuv13cm2yN7ncIRzRnZY0g7mkzb8lh5tHR4pkb0QO4xNOB3oGVjavwW__Xq0_vIhC3jlpkaf769vuj3rvzx8VH-e0wRB7v_JucotR2r-XLSKxN8kf-3rvsg_wQAAP__hyyoUg)** **

Your generous gift not only brings this course into your home—it helps Hillsdale share the message of faith and freedom with millions across the nation through our free online courses, publications, and classical K-12 education programs.

Please respond soon. Quantities are limited.

Scrooge’s journey reminds us that even in a culture that’s grown cold to faith and generosity, we can still “honour Christmas with our whole hearts.”

This is our gift to you...a way to deepen your understanding of Dickens’ timeless story and share its Christian message with your family, friends, or community.

Thank you for helping Hillsdale keep learning, character, faith, and freedom alive this Christmas season.

Warm regards,

Bill Gray, '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

For most American families, the answer comes from the same short list of favorites. Today, we’re counting down America’s seven most popular dinners and giving each one a health score from one to five. This weekend, a tech entrepreneur posted a thread that should be Exhibit A in every congressional hearing on program integrity for the next year. Matt Mickiewicz (@MattMickiewicz) -- the co-founder of SitePoint, Flippa, and 99designs -- pointed a swarm of AI agents at public and private records and reported back with roughly $787 million in Medicare and Medicaid billing that cannot physically exist.
A physical therapist billed Medicare for 9,006 hours of treatment in a year that _contains 8,760 hours_ -- about 30 hours of therapy, every weekday, all year. A single mall parking lot claimed to serve more than a million summer meals in one August, up from 7,688 meals the year before, cashing a $4.9 million payday. A lab whose federal CLIA certificate covers roughly 600 tests a year billed Medicare for 105,977 genetic tests in 2024 -- including 816 tests for Rett syndrome, a childhood diagnosis, on patients averaging 73 years old.
Mickiewicz has no subpoena, no badge, and no line item in the federal budget. Everything he found is sitting in files the government already owns.
One honest note before anyone says it for me: these are billed amounts, not recovered losses. Medicare's public data files are annual, rounded, redacted, and aggregate claims under one billing number. The thread is analysis, not an indictment. The figures are his.
But the premise is not speculative. The government's own documents keep confirming him.
**The receipts...**

name: Teichert in the Trenches
subject: 💥The Risks We Don’t See💥
body:
A misperception about active risk and passive
---
| | | | | |
---
| | **💥****The Risks We Don’t See💥**
---
I hope last month’s leadership thought – World Class Risk Management – stuck with you for the last few weeks. It did with me!
In the midst of the stories about Wilbur Wright & Louis Pierre Mouillard, the four-step process to properly manage risk, and the six-step method to consider risk, there was a line that keeps resonating with me:
Ironically, taking no risk is actually risky – setting up an organization for failure when they are inevitably surpassed by others who refuse to stand still.
A misperception about active risk and passive risk is at the crux of the problem. Let me provide an illustration.
When I commanded Joint Base Andrews (2016-18), the Air Force Honor Guard fell under my command. These Ceremonial Guardsmen – known for being sharp, crisp, and motionless – were incredible examples of the precision and dedication of Airmen around the world.
They invited me to spend a morning with their Drill Team, and had a few tricks up their crisply-ironed sleeves. They wanted to train and film me walking the gauntlet – an impressive part of their showy routine. In about an hour, I was ready to go and the end result (using me as a prop) highlights their incredible professionalism:
| [](https://eufi5.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/SMK1E8tHeFuBmP64SPACXkt7Xr7g/VQDXiJEsVVMv)
---
When they posted it (without my knowledge), it went viral – gaining over 20 million views (including a repost from Snoop Dogg). Yet, there was an interesting point I learned during our training.
As they were teaching me to walk with the right cadence, my natural tendency was to slow down. After all, I saw the spinning rifles in front of me – with the bayonet tips traveling at over 40 miles per hour. I didn’t want to get hit by those! Thus, I was tempted to avoid active risk.
They warned me, however, of an important truth. The rifles were spinning just as fast behind me. And while slowing down might seem safer, it actually increased the risk because it put me in the danger zone of the threats I couldn’t see. Thus, through understandable hesitancy I was unknowingly accepting passive risk.
It’s human nature to avoid known threats while discounting unseen or unconsidered threats. As a result, individuals and organizations overweight active risk – myopically and excessively considering the risk of forward progress. Yet, in doing so, they often underweight passive risk – not seeing nor fully considering the risk of passivity.
As I said last month: It is not the job of a leader to avoid risk. In fact, a leadership mindset and organizational culture that avoids risk is rotten and stagnant.
Don’t assume risk because you are excessively scared of the risks that you see! Instead, LEAD WELL by carefully considering the concepts of both active risk and passive risk. And don’t forget what Mouillard says to a leader who has carefully considered the risks looming in front of them while properly considering the risks of staying behind: Daring Wins!

* John

| | | | **Teichert in the Trenches**

body:
| | | Hey friend ‐‐ it's Devan, Executive Director at the DSCC

I'm writing to thank you.

For two years, Democrats across the country worked _tirelessly_ to prepare for the midterms ‐‐ and your support helped power our victory.

Whether you volunteered, donated to campaigns, or just got out there and exercised your right to vote, we couldn't have flipped 8 seats (so far!) and taken back the Senate without your support. So from the bottom of my heart, **thank you for your dedication to our democracy and our future.**

Grassroots donations from Democrats like you helped the DSCC build unbreakable infrastructure in battleground states, fund crucial organizing programs, launch ad campaigns to get our message across to as many voters as possible, and fight back against the GOP's corruption.

At the beginning of the cycle, pundits didn't give us much of a chance. But we proved them wrong ‐‐ and our people‐powered grassroots movement beat Donald Trump, his Senate allies, and their megadonors.

I encourage you all to take some well‐deserved time to celebrate. I know these past two years haven't been easy, but fighting for the future of our country is always worth it.

We need to keep our positive momentum going as we prepare for 2028 ‐‐ **[so if you can, please chip in just $7 to help us defend Democratic held seats, protect and expand our Senate majority, and keep the pressure on Donald Trump and the GOP.](https://go.dscc.org/go/24583?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-ND-20261117-DevanDSCC-DevanThankYouAndImpact-ETG-sl1&refcode=DPE-ND-20261117-DevanDSCC-DevanThankYouAndImpact-ETG-sl1&akid=27526%2E9716520%2EihQqe-)**

Thank you again for your dedication to this fight. Grassroots supporters like you help steer our country back onto the right track. The movement we've built is strong, and I'm inspired by the progress we've achieved together.

Onward,

Devan
Executive Director, DSCC

I want to know what's working and what you want more of.
Let's get into it.
