* * *
## Iran Threat Reports Leave More Questions
CNN reports that U.S. intelligence indicates Iran has been developing potential plans involving a radioactive dirty bomb or chemical weapon targeting senior administration officials in Washington. Officials disagree about whether Iran could or would execute such an attack. The White House says there are currently no credible threats to the homeland. Iran has denied the allegations. [KTVZ](https://substack.com/redirect/2c5c2b90-3637-45b8-affe-0244fd01e6fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The American people are going to have questions. I certainly do.
We've been hearing about disruptions involving aviation, banks, and other major systems. Now we're hearing this. Are we under some sort of attack? Are these unrelated problems? There's no established connection between those outages and this reported Iranian planning, but the public deserves clear communication about what is happening.
And what exactly is our strategy in Iran? What did the previous strikes accomplish? What remains a threat? A dirty bomb is different from a nuclear weapon, but the broader question about what this conflict has achieved remains.
We keep getting frightening headlines without a clear explanation of where this is going. "Nothing to see here" isn't an answer.
[Read CNN's reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/2c5c2b90-3637-45b8-affe-0244fd01e6fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## Trump Arrives in Manila
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2be3fd6d-61bc-4c0f-bc94-594d845be2c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Trump has arrived in the Philippines ahead of his trip to China, where planned talks involve Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Nuclear weapons, trade, and the ongoing conflicts are part of the diplomatic backdrop. Trump is also floating a possible meeting with Kim Jong Un, although that meeting has not been confirmed. [apnews.com](https://substack.com/redirect/48cd7860-2cdc-4a63-a0aa-7fcdcb292171?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
There's a lot on this agenda. We'll see what actually comes out of the meetings.
[Follow the Asia trip](https://substack.com/redirect/48cd7860-2cdc-4a63-a0aa-7fcdcb292171?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## The White House Wants to Approve Congressional Testimony
The White House is directing agencies to obtain approval before employees testify before Congress. Its stated concern is politically motivated investigations. [axios.com](https://substack.com/redirect/2bfba23f-190a-43ff-9048-e6b95705bfae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Or investigations into Trump administration corruption. But, you know, whatever.
It looks to me like they're getting ahead of what they know is coming. Democrats take control in January, investigations begin, and now employees are being told to clear their appearances with the White House.
Congress is supposed to conduct oversight. I want to see whether this becomes a process for coordinating testimony or a way to keep people from answering questions.
[Read about the directive](https://substack.com/redirect/2bfba23f-190a-43ff-9048-e6b95705bfae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

First, five bucks a month gets you this daily briefing, the ad-free podcast, and helps support the research we're doing into healthcare, the incoming Congress, and policies affecting our communities. Want the podcast in Apple Podcasts? Second, this is day two. Give me some feedback. Leave a comment, email , slip into my DMs, or send me a text if you have my number. I want to know what's working and what you want more of. Let's get into it. Government Watchlist Tuesday, November 17. All times Eastern. Morning meetings may have begun or concluded by the time you read this. 9:00 a.m.: Greater Cleveland RTA Board meeting. . 9:30 a.m.: Cleveland Development, Planning and Sustainability Committee. A Lewiston sixth grader took $31,000 in cash to school for show-and-tell, and the show-and-tell part is the only piece of this anyone has explained. According to the police report the Maine Wire obtained, the family told Lewiston police they plan to open a hair salon and also keep cash on hand in case a relative is detained by ICE. Those reasons account for why the money was in the house... maybe. Where it came from is still the open question, and the Maine Wire reports nobody has answered it. Lewiston police say the investigation is open. It's unclear whether the money has been returned. Jon Fetherston has the details: [EXCLUSIVE: Lewiston Sixth Grader Hauls $31K Cash to Class for Show and Tell -- Family Cites Hair Salon Plans and ICE Fears](https://substack.com/redirect/38fe6500-d85f-4be9-91d2-cd77f50a7244?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

### [RECOUNT COMPLETE: Elizabeth Bosworth defeats John Andrews for State Senate, giving the Democrats a supermajority in the upper chamber](https://substack.com/redirect/9e81a91a-15f3-4bd9-bf61-ad033875c583?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The hand recount in Senate District 18 ended Monday with Democrat Elizabeth Bosworth ahead of Republican John Andrews, 10,413 to 10,360. That is a 53-vote margin (unofficial until the Secretary of State certifies). The totals come from the Secretary of State's Office, and the margin of victory was supplied by UOCAVA votes.
The result gives Democrats 24 Senate seats. That is the first supermajority in the chamber since 1985. The seat formerly belonged to Rick Bennett, who left the Republican Party to run for governor as an independent. Democrats will hold the governor's office and larger majorities in both chambers when the new Legislature convenes. The supermajority in the Senate and the big majority in the House of Representatives mean Republicans are just a few bad attendance days away from getting surprised with constitutional amendments.

### [Portland Police Chief Tells Councilors Department Has 45 Operational Vacancies](https://substack.com/redirect/506dea73-d195-4697-a9b1-52200e72694c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you file a police report at Portland headquarters, bring a book. Chief Mark Dubois told city councilors on Nov. 10 that people in the lobby can sit "honestly, easily an hour," and that his detectives "really have to pick and choose what they can work on and follow up on."
The department is budgeted for 158 officers and has 26 vacancies. Retirements, military service, medical leave and recruits still in the academy take more people off the street, which Dubois said leaves "45 operational vacancies." Asked how many officers the city needs, he said "probably close to 200," about 42 more than the budget covers.
The department has 12 detectives. Its crime reduction unit, which handles drug complaints and problem areas, has three officers, down from "like 17 people in it back a while ago," Dubois said. Recruiting hasn't closed the gap: of the last two recruit classes, he said, "17 people, but nine remain."
Dubois didn't say why the other eight left.
The department's numbers for Nov. 2 to 8 show what the shifts look like. Police handled about 1,300 calls for service, roughly 186 a day. That included 211 disturbances, 76 vehicle crashes, 51 alarms, 50 behavioral health incidents, 43 thefts and 16 assaults. Officers made 38 arrests and logged six nonfatal overdoses.

### [First the FAA, Now South Portland: City Says Cybersecurity Incident Knocked Out Multiple Services](https://substack.com/redirect/97ae931e-a6e0-4067-b531-53b690d58ac9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
South Portland's phones are down, and the city's preliminary read is that criminals did it. IT shut down the city network after finding a cybersecurity issue around 11:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14. In its [Monday evening update](https://substack.com/redirect/689a15f5-06c0-48ee-9d6f-65be82b40ded?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the city said the preliminary assessment indicates "cybercriminal activity," that it has engaged an independent forensic examiner and that "the majority of City data is unaffected."
City Hall, the assessor's office and the library were closed Monday and stay closed Tuesday while the city tests systems. The city phone system is down in both directions. In-person card payments don't work, and some online administrative and mapping services are offline. The city can't print receipts or other documents, and it isn't streaming meetings online. Police, Fire and EMS are unaffected, and the city says to call 911 for emergencies.
Separately, the Maine Wire says the online bill-pay vendor, Citizen Self Service, has had on-and-off outages for a week. The city has postponed the property tax due date to Monday, Nov. 23. Residents can use the drop boxes outside City Hall, and vehicle registration renewals can go through the state's Rapid Renewal site.
The update doesn't say who is behind the incident, whether personal information was accessed or whether anyone demanded a ransom. Mike Dery, the city's IT director, said, "It's all hands on deck." The city is working with state and federal agencies that it hasn't named.
### [Lewiston Mayor's Race Heads to Runoff, Harriman Resignation and Questions Over Needle Ordinance](https://substack.com/redirect/0411c317-e4f0-4438-824d-748f1d0ba6ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Early in-person voting in Lewiston's mayoral runoff started Monday at City Hall and runs through Dec. 10, the day absentee ballot requests close at 4 p.m. Election Day is Tuesday, Dec. 15, with all voting at Longley School from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., according to the [city's elections page](https://substack.com/redirect/9bf4aa30-4b0b-4fa6-b08f-5f952d314f41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Rick LaChapelle, the former council president, finished first in the five-candidate field with 45.7% on Nov. 3. Mayor Carl Sheline had 35.3%. Neither reached a majority, hence the runoff.
Meanwhile, Ward 3 needs a councilor. Councilor Scott Harriman, a Democrat who also holds House District 94, submitted his resignation Nov. 6, effective Dec. 4, according to council documents. The council has censured him three times. The first was in October 2023 over comments about other councilors. The second was in October 2025, after a finding that he used Signal, which can delete messages automatically, to talk to a city employee about city business, and the council determined those messages weren't kept as the public records law requires. Harriman apologized. The third came in June 2026, a 4-3 vote over his conduct at a public workshop. The allegations included interrupting colleagues and using obscene language toward one.
The Maine Wire has also reported that a former tenant accuses Harriman of unwanted sexual conduct and retaliation after she rejected him. Harriman has denied it several times, calls it politically motivated and says he evicted her over unpaid rent and other problems. She disputes that. The Maine Wire has asked House Speaker Ryan Fecteau (D-Biddeford) repeatedly for comment and got no response on how he'll handle the scandal-plagued member of his caucus.
Voters also settled the needle question on Nov. 3. They approved a citizen-initiated amendment to the syringe service ordinance 8,241 to 5,786 -- an overwhelming rejection of the needle policies that have turned Maine's cities into druggie wastelands. The ordinance requires one-for-one exchanges, caps each person at 20 syringes a day, requires a single fixed location and bans mobile units.

### [Update on the selection of Maine's constitutional officers](https://substack.com/redirect/94f55211-c6bf-4538-bf84-521f216475ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Maine's Legislature picks the attorney general, secretary of state and treasurer, and, as far as the Maine Wire knows, only one of those jobs is contested. Secretary of State Shenna Bellows and Treasurer Joe Perry have no known challengers, the Maine Wire reports. The attorney general's seat is open because Aaron Frey terms out at the end of the year.
State Sen. Anne Carney (D-Cumberland) and lawyer Timothy Shannon are both running and are reportedly lobbying legislators privately ahead of the Dec. 2 vote. Lawmakers choose after they are sworn in that day. Carney chairs the Judiciary Committee, and Shannon is a former Yarmouth town councilor who calls himself a progressive Democrat and ran against Frey eight years ago.
### [Duffy Floats $50 Billion Price Tag For Congress To Prevent Repeat Paralysis Of US Air Travel](https://substack.com/redirect/a79d6778-9902-46df-a41f-9c0f84e7285c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wants $50 billion so a bad day at the FAA never again grounds every plane in the country. He raised the figure from $30 billion at a Friday night White House press conference, per the Daily Caller News Foundation, and defended it Saturday with the line that the outage "is a sign for [Congress] to lean in."
### [New Disclosure Site to Shed Light on Federal Judges](https://substack.com/redirect/7c8728be-0df5-4e3f-a145-22f1d7893c86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Maine has a small federal bench, and a nonprofit says it will publish profiles of federal judges nationwide. Marco Polo, the group behind the Biden Laptop Report, says its next project is ThirdBranch.icu, a directory of Senate-confirmed federal judges with their professional and family connections and any potential conflicts that "could/should warrant recusal." Founder Garrett Ziegler calls federal judges "a new caste system in the United States" and says the site will carry more than 1,400 profiles over the next year plus, with no subscription.
### [Sanford Police Chief Eric Small, Who Once Ran for Pingree's Congress Seat, Announces Retirement](https://substack.com/redirect/06b033ce-4596-4793-9e23-4ef295df21a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Sanford's police chief is retiring on Christmas to spend more time with kids and horses. Eric Small, chief since October 2024 and a Sanford officer who rose to deputy chief in 2008, announced in a Friday Facebook post that he retires Dec. 25 after more than 30 years in law enforcement. He has lived in Sanford more than 20 years.
"I know I haven't always gotten everything right," Small wrote. "I've made mistakes, learned some hard lessons, and made decisions that not everyone agreed with. But I hope people know that I genuinely cared about this community and tried to do what I believed was right."
Next up is UNBROKEN Children's Foundation, the nonprofit he founded, which lets children who have suffered trauma work with and ride horses for therapeutic benefit.
### [Nuclear Startup Wins Local Approval For Up To 120 Small Reactors Beside Data Centers](https://substack.com/redirect/19a1da98-0ff3-4993-98c0-e527d1dd26a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A Utah county just approved a permit for a campus that could hold 120 small reactors, and it did so without holding a public hearing. Carbon County planners voted Thursday night, with one no, to approve Valar Atomics for between 40 and 120 reactors plus data centers on about 640 acres of state trust land near Wellington. The county attorney told the panel that Utah law makes this kind of permit an administrative decision. Valar can't build a reactor without a Nuclear Regulatory Commission license or Energy Department authorization, and the conditions keep plants half a mile from homes. Simon August of the Daily Caller News Foundation has the story.
### [Calais Border Patrol Find Canadian Illegals Establishing a Campsite on Island](https://substack.com/redirect/afe20bf5-6ec2-4ab3-8633-a36402e214ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The enemy to the north is once again encroaching on our sovereignty... Two Canadians who camped on an island in the St. Croix River without checking in at a border station were removed to Canada, Border Patrol says. The Houlton Sector's Calais station found them with construction materials, a small raft and a lot of trash, and described the site as "more than a simple campsite." Local authorities were notified of the possible environmental damage. The Friday press release named no suspects and gave no date.

The Portland newspaper reports that the governor-elect pushed a government-run option in her campaign but hasn't formulated a plan. She told the paper she wants to convene a working group after she takes office in January to design a proposal. Four states offer public option plans now: Washington, Colorado, Nevada and Minnesota. Pingree said her family's ACA premiums jumped from about $700 a month in 2025 to more than $2,000 this year.
Jeff Austin, president of the Maine Hospital Association, called her proposal "intriguing." We suspect this is one of many "intriguing" ideas Mainers will learn about over the next year.

Sanford's police chief is retiring on Christmas to spend more time with kids and horses. Eric Small, chief since October 2024 and a Sanford officer who rose to deputy chief in 2008, announced in a Friday Facebook post that he retires Dec. 25 after more than 30 years in law enforcement. He has lived in Sanford more than 20 years. "I know I haven't always gotten everything right," Small wrote. "I've made mistakes, learned some hard lessons, and made decisions that not everyone agreed with. But I hope people know that I genuinely cared about this community and tried to do what I believed was right." Next up is UNBROKEN Children's Foundation, the nonprofit he founded, which lets children who have suffered trauma work with and ride horses for therapeutic benefit. A Utah county just approved a permit for a campus that could hold 120 small reactors, and it did so without holding a public hearing. Carbon County planners voted Thursday night, with one no, to approve Valar Atomics for between 40 and 120 reactors plus data centers on about 640 acres of state trust land near Wellington. The county attorney told the panel that Utah law makes this kind of permit an administrative decision. Valar can't build a reactor without a Nuclear Regulatory Commission license or Energy Department authorization, and the conditions keep plants half a mile from homes. Simon August of the Daily Caller News Foundation has the story. The enemy to the north is once again encroaching on our sovereignty... Two Canadians who camped on an island in the St. Croix River without checking in at a border station were removed to Canada, Border Patrol says. The Houlton Sector's Calais station found them with construction materials, a small raft and a lot of trash, and described the site as "more than a simple campsite." Local authorities were notified of the possible environmental damage. The Friday press release named no suspects and gave no date. Around the Web The Portland newspaper reports that the governor-elect pushed a government-run option in her campaign but hasn't formulated a plan. She told the paper she wants to convene a working group after she takes office in January to design a proposal. Four states offer public option plans now: Washington, Colorado, Nevada and Minnesota. Pingree said her family's ACA premiums jumped from about $700 a month in 2025 to more than $2,000 this year. Jeff Austin, president of the Maine Hospital Association, called her proposal "intriguing." We suspect this is one of many "intriguing" ideas Mainers will learn about over the next year. While we are still waiting for every vote to be counted, we are starting to run out of resources.

I am so grateful to have had your support throughout this campaign. Seriously.

| "I am grateful to my Senate Republican colleagues who put their trust in me to continue to serve as Minority Leader at a crucial moment for our state.
As the sole legislative leader from Upstate, I am proud to lead a conference of fighters from every corner of New York who are committed to making our state safer and more affordable.
You can be assured that the Senate Republicans will be the voice for hardworking families who feel shut out of state government and who believe in the common-sense, free-market policies that made New York what was once the economic powerhouse of our nation.
As New Yorkers face a rising tide of socialism in state government and Senate Democrats swing further left to placate the radical agenda of their DSA members, Senate Republicans will stand up for taxpayers who do not want to see this state undone by an agenda that is fundamentally un-American.
The Senate Republican Conference will be a check on one-party rule and a voice for every New Yorker who want a state that is affordable, safe and full of opportunity."

body:
I’m going to be blunt with you.

| | |
---
| | Friend,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Friend, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _

# How to Use Dual Cameras in FaceTime
Ever since iPhone 17 Pros got the Dual Camera option in the Camera app, I've wondered when it would become available on FaceTime, and it finally is! As long as you and your contact have compatible devices and software, one of you can share both the front and back camera views simultaneously during a video call!
## Why You'll Love This Tip
* **Experience a more immersive FaceTime call that shows your face and point of view simultaneously.**
* **Never miss another special moment, like seeing a loved one opening your gift while seeing their face light up.**

## How to use iPhone Dual Camera in FaceTime
### System Requirements
_This tip was performed on an iPhone 17 Pro running iOS 27. Both parties need to have an iPhone 17 Pro or newer running iOS 27 for the steps to work. Find out how to update to the[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261398-8632868-ae2b4e862e-2u4e0e7575)._There are third-party apps that have made it possible to show both the front "selfie" camera and the back cameras simultaneously, but the feature is new to iPhones. Keep in mind that only one person can share both cameras at once. Here's how to have a double camera iPhone video call:
1. Open **FaceTime**.

|
---
2. Tap **New Call** at the bottom of the screen.

---
3. Type your contacts name in the "To:" field.

---
### Enjoying Your Tip of the Day?
If you'd like to learn more about iPhone Life's premium paid subscription, [click here](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261398-3292905-1b046d6865-2u4e0e7575)
4. Once you've selected a contact, tap **FaceTime**.

---
5. Tap the **Flip icon** at the bottom of the window showing your front camera.

---
6. Your back camera will now be visible in addition to your front one. If you want to turn off your front camera, you'll have to tap on your **front camera window**.

---
7. Tap the **crossed out profile icon** in the top left of your front camera view window.

---
8. You can then tap the **profile icon** in the top left of your window again to show both cameras again. Or tap the **flip icon** at the bottom left of your screen to only show your front camera.

---

Since only one person can share both camera views at the same time, if you are sharing both cameras and the other person taps the flip icon on their phone, they will start sharing both cameras while yours will return to only one camera view. There is no confirmation to switch from one person sharing both cameras to the other. Hopefully one day, it will be possible for both people to share both cameras simultaneously!
Now you know how to have a FaceTime call using the front and back cameras at the same time. This is one of the collect new FaceTime features Apple has released in a while! Next, learn [how to use both cameras simultaneously in the Camera app](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-261398-8632869-c530358428-2u4e0e7575).

I recently joined Morning Joe to discuss our election victory, and I made a point of speaking directly to President Trump about immigration.
Look, there's a reason every border district from my home in South Texas to way up in Washington state went blue.
This administration went too far on immigration enforcement.
They didn't just create chaos and fear within our communities. They tore the bottom out of our economy.
When people are too scared to show up at job sites, or when legal immigrants, including folks with green cards, step out of their homes and are pestered with questions by ICE, that's counterproductive.
The answer is clear to me, and I hope it's clear to this president: **We need immigration reform.**
I'm ready to talk with President Trump about a solution, and it doesn't have to wait until I'm sworn in.

# Iran
* **Iran targets U.S. military facilities in Bahrain for third time:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Tuesday it launched a drone attack targeting a U.S. radar system at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, in what it described as a response to repeated violations of Iranian airspace by U.S. military drones. AFP reported explosions in the Bahraini capital, Manama, after the Interior Ministry warned residents of an unspecified danger.
* U.S. Central Command [denied](https://substack.com/redirect/c971c08f-65eb-44a0-a3bf-778cdda0b9ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the radar system had been hit, saying multiple Iranian drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted without damaging U.S. equipment or injuring American personnel.
* **Qatar announces new talks with Tehran:** Qatar said Tuesday that mediation efforts to end the U.S.-Iran conflict were continuing, announcing plans to meet Iranian officials in the coming hours. "Today's meeting with the Iranian side will take place as part of mediation efforts and an exchange of views on the current proposals," Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said during a press briefing in Doha.
* Warning that "any escalation on the ground poses a challenge to mediation efforts," Al-Ansari urged both sides to exercise restraint and avoid further escalation.
* **Iran 's Navy says five tankers struck naval mines near Hormuz: **Another tanker [caught fire](https://substack.com/redirect/23849fb6-9f64-4a2c-b97e-250ac7546925?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and sustained severe damage on Tuesday after striking a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, bringing the reported number of tankers damaged in the past 24 hours to five, according to Iran's Navy. The Navy claimed the vessel was traveling through a "prohibited" area with its navigation systems switched off.
* Separately, Iran's IRGC Navy said a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil and a liquefied petroleum gas carrier had struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. It remains unclear whether the two vessels are included in the Navy's reported total.
* **Tehran warns NYT report linking dams to missile sites could pave way for attacks on civilian infrastructure:** Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf charged The New York Times of laying the groundwork for further U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iranian civilian infrastructure after the newspaper published an [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/7018624e-28c0-420c-a24c-8e6dab03b7c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) suggesting that some of the country's dams and water transfer projects may have been built partly to support underground missile facilities.
* The report cited researchers who found that the locations of numerous dams closely overlapped with suspected missile sites targeted in U.S. and Israeli airstrikes this year, although the researchers acknowledged that any connection remains speculative and that many dams serve essential civilian needs.
* "Prepping the next round on civilian infra," Ghalibaf [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/44f44148-563f-4412-a8ba-d56b5eba4ea2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X. "New rule: Any dam, port, or power plant near a U.S. or Israeli base is dual-use. We'll apply your logic consistently and even-handedly."
* **CNN goes Judith Miller: U.S. intelligence warns of suspected Iranian dirty bomb plot, Iran rejects claim as "fabricated": **U.S. intelligence [suggests](https://substack.com/redirect/f91d29c6-c635-428b-bd75-9c031c5bade8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran may be developing plans for a possible dirty bomb or chemical weapons attack targeting senior Trump administration officials in Washington, D.C., CNN reported Tuesday. Sources said the intelligence identified specific locations and targets but stressed that there was no evidence Tehran had decided to carry out an attack. The White House said there were "no credible threats to the homeland."
* Asked about the report, President Donald Trump warned that Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before" if it attacked Washington.
* Iran's UN mission rejected the chemical weapons allegations as "false and fabricated," while Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei accused those who started the war of attempting to manufacture justification for further attacks.
* Days earlier, Israel Hayom reported that Israel's Mossad had warned the CIA of an alleged Iranian drone plot targeting Trump and senior U.S. officials.
* **Only 31% of Americans support U.S. war on Iran:** Just 31% of American adults support the U.S. war on Iran, according to a new [Reuters/Ipsos poll](https://substack.com/redirect/6efbeee0-cd04-4ce5-a42d-f84b1d5dbb1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Trump's approval rating stands at 32%, near the lowest level of his presidency, after falling to a record low of 31% in mid-October.
* In an interview with Fox News, Vice President JD Vance acknowledged the war's political consequences, citing "the higher gas prices, the higher energy prices," after previously linking the conflict to Republican losses in the midterm elections.
* "People who want it to become a forever war, they can attack me all they want to because we signed up to not do this," Vance said, accusing some "neoconservatives" of wanting the U.S. to "stay there forever." Vance insisted there was "no daylight" between him and Trump, despite the president recently saying he had told Vance that the U.S. did not need a deal with Iran.
* **Iran claims capture of ninth U.S. drone over Qeshm Island; shoots down another:** The IRGC [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e825031d-5812-4985-9c3f-7323c7f8e6d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday that it had captured another U.S. MQM-170 drone through an electronic warfare operation over southern Qeshm Island, bringing the total number of such drones it claims to have seized to nine. The IRGC said its specialists took control of the aircraft and brought it down intact.
* Iran's army separately said it shot down a U.S.-made LUCAS attack drone over Hormuz, according to state broadcaster IRIB.

# Palestine
* **Israeli forces kill two Palestinians in Gaza attacks:** Israeli forces shot and killed a Palestinian man and wounded several others in the Al-Jaafrawi area east of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza on Tuesday, according to WAFA. Separately, a Palestinian succumbed to injuries sustained in an earlier Israeli airstrike in Jabalia, northern Gaza.
* **Israeli airstrike hits near UN fuel convoy in Gaza:** An Israeli airstrike struck "very close" to a UN-led fuel convoy in Rafah, southern Gaza, on Sunday, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/18256f56-e2f2-42aa-9aba-0fa69a76440c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the United Nations. UN deputy spokesperson Farhan Haq warned that strikes near humanitarian vehicles, particularly those carrying fuel, expose aid workers to "unacceptable risks," adding that the UN had raised the incident with Israeli authorities. Haq called for increased humanitarian funding and faster entry of essential supplies restricted by Israel.
* Earlier this month, a senior Palestinian source involved in negotiations [told](https://substack.com/redirect/74b89b2a-7ec2-4310-af80-57c885b80138?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Drop Site that Israel had ordered a complete halt to aid and commercial shipments entering Gaza from Egypt, warning that "fuel and gas come entirely through this route," which handles approximately 50-60 trucks daily.
* **Israeli settlers kill 72-year-old Palestinian woman, wound 10 others in Jericho attack:** Israeli settlers [shot and killed](https://substack.com/redirect/43618b6c-11fe-44b3-8e22-02576df7cfe7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 72-year-old Palestinian woman and wounded 10 other Palestinians during an overnight attack on Ein Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, west of Jericho in the occupied West Bank, according to WAFA. During the attack, settlers surrounded Palestinian homes while Israeli forces raided the village and closed three entrances to Jericho.
* Israeli soldiers also severely beat WAFA photojournalist Suleiman Abu Surour while he was covering the attack, leaving him with fractures and bruises. Soldiers detained him for six hours and confiscated his phone before releasing him.
* Later Tuesday, Israeli forces informed Fheidat's family that they were prohibited from holding a funeral for her in the village.
* The attack came nearly two weeks after settlers seized eight homes in the village at gunpoint and continued occupying them. **Read Katrine Dige Houm øller's report for Drop Site on the settlers' seizure of homes in Jericho [here](https://substack.com/redirect/f9a8872a-a371-4c06-b6a8-5d6a9332fbff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Elsewhere in the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers injure eight Palestinians as forces demolish homes:**
* **Bethlehem:** An Israeli settler drove a vehicle into a group of Palestinians gathered near a traffic accident in Tuqu, southeast of Bethlehem, on Monday, injuring eight people, according to WAFA.
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/445c1a8c-00fe-4845-aefd-9ab64c0a61d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three homes sheltering 21 Palestinians along with two livestock sheds and two water wells in the Al-Deirat and Al-Duwarat areas east of Yatta on Tuesday.
* **Tubas:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/b8770be5-f725-46b1-8a45-4d7d595480e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) greenhouses in Bardala in the northern Jordan Valley. Settlers also destroyed agricultural irrigation networks near Ein Al-Beida.
* **Occupied** **East Jerusalem:** Settlers [established](https://substack.com/redirect/9072ca2c-740e-4ddf-8113-a3b9a3796e1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a new settlement outpost near Palestinian homes in the Al-Hayy area outside Mikhmas, northeast of occupied East Jerusalem.
* **UK sanctions eight Israeli settlement firms and group blocking Gaza aid:** The UK [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/b5128e9b-454a-4ca0-9bd6-973e73ec426b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new sanctions on Tuesday targeting eight Israeli construction, property development, and architectural firms involved in expanding illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank, alongside Tzav 9, an Israeli group that has organized blockades of humanitarian aid entering Gaza. The sanctions include asset freezes and director disqualifications.
* "Do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution," Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said. The UK said Israel has approved more settlements under its current government than in the previous 20 years.
* **EU sanctions Gaza outlet over alleged Hamas fundraising:** The European Union announced new sanctions on Monday against Gaza Now, a Gaza-based social media outlet, and its founder, Mustafa Ayash, accusing them of soliciting funds for Hamas and other armed groups, according to the Associated Press. The sanctions include asset freezes for both the outlet and Ayash, who holds refugee status in Austria and will also face a travel ban across the 27-member bloc. Gaza Now has more than 470,000 followers on X and over one million on Telegram, and was previously sanctioned by the United States in 2024.

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah reports nine wounded in Sana 'a airstrike: **At least nine people were wounded in an airstrike on a shoe factory in the Al-Nahda neighborhood of Sana'a, according to the city's Health Ministry. Ansarallah-affiliated Al-Masirah TV also reported that Saudi airstrikes targeted a demining team in the Kitaf Wa Al-Boqe'e district of Saada governorate.
* **Saudi-backed forces reinforce defenses around Aden amid Ansarallah advance:** Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces deployed additional troops and military equipment Tuesday around Tur Al-Baha, roughly 85 kilometers (52 miles) from Aden, according to AP. The deployment follows the withdrawal of Saudi-backed forces from positions overlooking the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, allowing Ansarallah to consolidate control over the area. Ansarallah has repeatedly denied plans to attack Aden.
* **Saudi Arabia replaces Yemen coalition commander following withdrawal from Bab al-Mandab:** Saudi Arabia [replaced](https://substack.com/redirect/96b21894-f1b5-4ef6-a20d-860b0806eeaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the commander of its military coalition fighting Ansarallah on Monday, following the withdrawal of Saudi-backed forces from positions near Bab al-Mandab. King Salman appointed General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili to replace Lieutenant General Fahd Al-Salman, who was reassigned as an adviser to the Saudi defense minister, according to Saudi state media.
* The leadership change follows weeks of Ansarallah advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast. Saudi-backed forces have struggled to regain territory lost during the offensive, including the key port city of Mocha, while their withdrawal from Bab al-Mandab has allowed Ansarallah to consolidate control near the strait, a critical route for Saudi oil exports amid disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli forces continue ceasefire violations across southern Lebanon:**
* **Bint Jbeil:** Israeli forces [heavily shelled](https://substack.com/redirect/9e37d22a-4b7e-43f9-832b-2727347e233c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Al-Arish area between the towns of Haris and Hadatha on Tuesday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.
* **Marjeyoun:** Israeli warplanes [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/820e5b36-3915-463c-ab5e-c20e422081bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the town of Houla overnight, while Israeli forces opened fire in Khiam.
* **Nabatieh:** Forces shelled Wadi Al-Salouqi and the hills surrounding the towns of Shaqra and Qabrikha at dawn.
* **U.S. envoy urges Hezbollah to disarm voluntarily as UN peacekeeping mandate nears expiration:** U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz [called on](https://substack.com/redirect/8c063983-03a2-4a88-9788-48c1fd58efcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Hezbollah to voluntarily surrender its weapons to the Lebanese army on Monday. "No country can have two armies. I hope and pray Hezbollah will disarm. They should do that voluntarily," Waltz said.
* He also said he had met Lebanese leaders to discuss alternatives to the UN peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon, whose mandate expires on December 31.
* In June, Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement linking Hezbollah's disarmament to a gradual Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon and the deployment of the Lebanese army. Implementation has made little progress amid continued Israeli attacks and occupation of Lebanese territory.

# U.S. News
* **Hakeem Jeffries moves for recorded leadership vote as Ayanna Pressley flirts with bid:** A handful of House Democrats have said recently that they planned to write down the name of Rep. **Ayanna Pressley** (Mass.) in Wednesday's Speaker contest, relying on the tradition of a secret ballot. **Hakeem Jeffries** (N.Y.) subsequently suggested he'll push for a recorded vote, which would make each member's tally public. Jeffries needs 218 votes on the House floor to be elected Speaker. On Monday, Pressley [spoke at a town hall](https://substack.com/redirect/fa3226e8-ed76-441c-9f4e-347dc9ba67da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Boston about the race in the most open terms she had yet, but did not announce an official challenge: "I'm very humbled to even be in conversation when I think about the history of this seat that I occupy--**Tip O 'Neill **served in this seat, the Speaker of the House; **John F. Kennedy** served in this seat--this is a historic seat and we have had a historic electoral outcome. We are on the precipice of a historic vote for Speaker and we need to have a historic impact on Congress because that is the decisive mandate by the people, that we move with boldness, not timidity. Scared power isn't power at all. When you have the power you have to use it. Now I am making no declarations or announcements here. What I will say is that I do not need to be the Speaker of the House to speak for the people."
* **Permitting reform clears major Senate hurdle:** The Senate moved to end debate on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) by a 70-27 margin Monday evening, setting it up for final passage. Twenty-one [Democrats joined Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/17ac0d4b-17e7-4ad6-8536-dd744c3cd8a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in backing the bill that has the support of both the clean energy and the fossil fuel industries. Its cornerstone provision aims to massively expand transmission capacity, the lack of which is a fundamental obstacle to the buildout of clean energy, but which can also be used to transmit dirty energy. Some environmental advocates whose approach leans more heavily on litigating against energy projects--clean and dirty alike--argued Congress should wait until Democrats control both chambers and can write a better bill. Massachusetts Sen. **Ed Markey** , the lead Senate sponsor of the Green New Deal resolution, delivered a [lengthy address](https://substack.com/redirect/624bd798-c8d3-425e-bb7e-e77cca7941bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday against the bill. The bill's backers counter that the approach ignores the reality that the legislation needs the signature of President Trump and, unless the filibuster is removed, at least some support from Republican senators. Passing BAAJA during the lame duck, meanwhile, would not bar the next Congress from working on improving it.
* **Forensic scientist argues that evidence strongly points to Epstein homicide:** Forensic scientist **Michael Freeman** has begun [presenting](https://substack.com/redirect/086f4a54-ef68-445e-bae3-ab6626551998?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the findings in his year-long inquiry into **Jefferey Epstein 's** death, saying Epstein's injuries are most plausibly explained by homicidal strangulation. Freeman, who studies bias and error in death investigation, based his analysis on the autopsy file, given to him by Epstein's brother **Mark Epstein**. He claims the photos show fingernail marks above the ligature, evidence of neck abrasion and a deep shoulder hemorrhage, all of which point to struggle. His findings have been rejected by scientific journals so far, and some forensic pathologists agree the mark was atypical but say the images could still fit suicide. The New York City medical examiner's office says "it stands by its determination" of suicide.
* **GOP Rep. DesJarlais concedes his reelection race in Tennessee:** Tennessee**** GOP Rep. **Scott DesJarlais** [conceded](https://substack.com/redirect/00a5de1e-70b5-412f-bd06-0a8982902375?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Democrat **Victoria Broderick** on Monday in an unexpectedly close race to represent Tennessee's 4th District. Decision Desk HQ has not projected a winner, with Broderick leading 48.87% to 48.73% (a lead of just over 200 votes). She won despite being heavily outspent in a district Trump carried by 24 points in 2024. DesJarlais has served eight terms in Congress.
* **Rep. Ro Khanna suggests $1,700 refund checks for every American to cover costs of Iran War:** Rep. **Ro Khanna**(D-Calif.)****[proposed](https://substack.com/redirect/712ae08a-bd4a-404e-a986-4b840f466f4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $1,700 refund checks for every American to reimburse Americans for the economic costs of the Iran War, arguing the checks would compensate for higher gas, food, and electricity prices from war-related oil transport disruptions. He urged the House and Senate to pass the proposal in the first week of January ("let's put it on Trump's desk"). Moody's **Mark Zandi** estimates the war has cost households an average of $2,000.
* **White House tells agencies federal employees "must obtain approval" before agreeing to testify before Congress:** In a Monday memo to agency general counsels, Politico reported, White House counsel **Will Scharf** [said](https://substack.com/redirect/6191ff2e-2558-43de-8f1a-a454a6980e6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) agency personnel "must obtain approval" from the White House Offices of Legislative Affairs and Counsel before appearing at congressional committees. The directive comes a week after Scharf warned incoming House Oversight Chair **Robert Garcia** that Democratic investigations "may cross the line into blatant criminality," as Democrats prepare to scrutinize Trump, his family, and business interests next year.
* **Commerce and Justice Departments defend handling of Megaspeed:** The Commerce and Justice Departments issued a rare joint statement defending their handling of Megaspeed, the Singapore chip buyer at the center of Nvidia's alleged spy scandal, after Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** accused Commerce of failing to stop Nvidia's sales to the firm. Citing "inaccurate information circulating in public reporting," the statement said Commerce opened a probe in 2024 and that DOJ now leads a criminal case. They did not explain why Megaspeed was never blacklisted. President Trump said Monday that Commerce Secretary **Howard Lutnick** "might have delayed" doing so to avoid "a blow-up with China." Trump also cast doubt on the spy allegations against Megaspeed CEO **Alice Huang** , whose affair with Nvidia CEO **Jensen Huang** forced his resignation last week: "I don't know that she's a spy. Nobody's proven that," while adding that he "wouldn't mind" Huang returning. The turmoil sent Nvidia down 4.1% Monday and dragged the tech-heavy Nasdaq down 2.5% ahead of the company's quarterly earnings after the bell Tuesday.
* **Major software outage at Chase Bank:** A software bug at JPMorgan Chase [disrupted](https://substack.com/redirect/957b317b-bad5-492c-bcef-17aa24538be5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) online banking and Zelle transfers for thousands of customers at several major U.S. banks on Monday. A Chase spokesman said Monday the issue was "a software bug in an on-premise hardware system--it is not cyber-related," with other banks affected "only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us." Zelle's owner, Early Warning Services, said its network was fully operational. The disruption followed a Thursday Microsoft outage, Friday's FAA ground stop, and a United Airlines system outage Monday that delayed departures.

# Other International News
* **UN report: Drone strikes account for over 80% of civilians killed in Sudan in first half of 2026:** Drone strikes have come to be a "defining feature" of the war in Sudan, accounting for more than 80% of the civilians killed in the first six months of 2026, according to a new [report](https://substack.com/redirect/673d6e67-367f-4a9c-84ff-607fb04c52f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the UN Human Rights Office. The report documents the targeting of civilians and civilian infrastructure, indiscriminate attacks, and the continued use of sexual violence as a weapon of war. At least 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan between January until the end of October, with the actual civilian casualty figures likely to be higher, the report found. Civilians in the Kordofan region were the most heavily impacted, accounting for more than two-thirds of documented civilian casualties, followed by the Darfur region, where most of the remaining casualties occurred. "The findings in our report provide more evidence, if any were needed, of the ceaselessly unbearable civilian suffering of the war in Sudan and the warring parties' continued and brazen disregard for the laws of war," UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said.
* **Prominent Bahraini human rights activist dies at 62:** Nabeel Rajab, a prominent Bahraini human rights activist who helped lead the country's 2011 pro-democracy protests and spent years in prison for advocating political freedoms and freedom of expression, died Tuesday at the age of 62. His wife and daughter found him unresponsive at their home in Istanbul, Turkey. Rajab, a co-founder and former president of the Bahrain Center for Human Rights, was repeatedly arrested following the Saudi-backed crackdown on Bahrain's 2011 uprising. He was sentenced to five years in prison over social media posts criticizing the Saudi-led war in Yemen, before being released to home detention in June 2020. Rajab left Bahrain earlier this year amid a renewed crackdown on protests following the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, [telling](https://substack.com/redirect/82a97294-8c7d-45f4-9d24-42dbdf2fb276?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Associated Press that he feared arrest following Bahraini authorities torture of an imprisoned activist. Rajab devoted his final years advocating for Palestinian rights. In one [post](https://substack.com/redirect/39590d69-1ab3-4420-af1a-41a4740202ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), he shared footage of the destruction in Gaza, writing, "How will the people of this land, which has been reduced to rubble, and their future generations ever forgive our silence, whether we are governments or ordinary people?"
* **Five European countries announce plan to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda:** Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece, and the Netherlands [said](https://substack.com/redirect/2622fd80-84d1-4b63-99bf-9dd581d2c2c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday they would send rejected asylum applicants to Rwanda as early as next year, Al Jazeera reported. The joint announcement noted that the arrangement is still being negotiated. Rwanda's interior minister, Vincent Biruta, said arrivals could return home, integrate in Rwanda, or move to another country where they can legally reside, claiming that the mechanism would employ an "independent monitoring mechanism" and cooperate fully with UNHCR. Germany's interior minister said it differs from the scrapped 2022 UK deal, which the UK Supreme Court ruled unlawful because Rwanda was not a safe third country, because only those whose claims are rejected would be sent. Forty-seven aid, union, and rights groups urged the countries to abandon the scheme, saying it accepts "the risk of serious human rights violations," and Human Rights Watch said it would provide additional resources to Rwanda's government, which it accuses of serious abuses.
* **Nigeria 's military says it is receiving U.S. intelligence and satellite help in strikes on militants: **Nigeria is getting real-time U.S. intelligence and satellite support to target militant leaders ahead of January elections, its defense minister Gen. Christopher Musa [said](https://substack.com/redirect/249cd66f-8ace-4dc0-a1b9-e87a1d965fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday, according to Reuters. Musa said troops killed several terrorist and bandit leaders in overnight operations in the northwest and northeast, aided by U.S. satellite imagery, intelligence sharing, and training, and that it is awaiting more helicopters from the U.S. and Italy. He also said Nigeria has agreed a 5-kilometer cross-border "right of pursuit" arrangement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad. Boko Haram and ISWAP attacks on military positions have surged in recent weeks, the military claims, ahead of a January election in which President Bola Tinubu seeks a second term.
* **Mongolian president announces his resignation after accusations of corruption:** Mongolian President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/233d4b57-0a7a-4256-b86f-47b9ead9007e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his resignation on Tuesday after the opposition Democratic Party accused him and several top officials in his ruling Mongolian People's Party of corruption. In announcing his resignation he said he would "be investigated and will have my honor restored." He has been president since 2021, and parliament's 126-member State Great Khural must approve his resignation.
* **Costa Rican journalist shot dead in capital:** Camilo Rodriguez, who published allegations against suspected drug traffickers and politicians, was shot and [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/d3836c65-58c1-4fe0-8a7e-8e3e97d955a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday afternoon on a highway outside San Jose. Attorney General Carlo Diaz said the scene resembling a contract killing and was likely linked to his reporting, adding that Rodriguez had reported threats but declined protection. Rodriguez is the first known journalist killed in Costa Rica in 25 years.
* **Russian strikes two Kyiv bridges hours after Ukraine holds new talks on ending the war:** Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy [held](https://substack.com/redirect/6a789c73-b24b-4de1-992f-f426bcea2abb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) online discussions Monday with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and representatives of France, Germany, Britain, Italy, and Poland. He called the discussions "not easy," and noted that parties agreed to meet in Berlin with the "Coalition of the Willing."
* In Kyiv, Russian strikes hit the North and South bridges over the Dnipro, the city's mayor reported on Monday evening. Two people were killed and the bridges were closed.
* Separately, Ukraine struck the Crimea Bridge overnight and targeted oil refineries, killing two people near the bridge. Monday's overnight drone attack, which featured as many as 200 drones, was the biggest such attack on Russia since 2022, according to Russian data.
