The Statue of Liberty says, 'Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free.' It doesn't say anything about speaking English or being able to be a computer programmer. Aren't you trying to change what it means to be an immigrant coming into this country?" Miller's reply has since been replayed across every platform that matters. He pointed out the obvious: the poem was added decades after the statue was conceived and was not part of the original monument. He called Acosta's framing "insulting, ignorant and foolish," and then delivered the line that made him famous on the right and infamous on the left -- that the question revealed Acosta's "cosmopolitan bias to a shocking degree." Strip away the theater and Miller was simply correct on the facts. Emma Lazarus wrote "The New Colossus" in 1883 to help raise money for the statue's pedestal. It had nothing to do with immigration policy at the time; it wasn't mounted on a plaque inside the pedestal until 1903, seventeen years after the statue's dedication. It has never been law. The statute -- the actual Immigration and Nationality Act and its many ancestors -- is what governs who comes in, and every Congress since the founding has amended it to favor some qualities over others. A correspondent citing a pedestal poem as binding American tradition is not making a legal argument. She's making a vibe. The country, through hard experience, has learned to tell the difference. That is the "free lesson" of the caption. It isn't Miller's politics, which his critics find repellent and his fans find brave and which are irrelevant to the pedagogy here. The lesson is procedural, and it is elementary: know the difference between a symbol and a source of law; verify the provenance of the thing you're citing; ask yourself whether your question is a question or an argument wearing a question's clothes. A correspondent with a national platform flubbed all three in under a minute, and the man across the split screen -- a partisan operative who holds no journalism degree -- did not. The factories never stopped Which raises the uncomfortable question: what, exactly, are the schools teaching? The volume numbers tell one story. Missouri: 484 journalism bachelor's degrees a year. Columbia: 230 master's degrees. Add Medill, Newhouse, Annenberg, UT-Austin and the rest, and you get a national industry producing thousands of journalism graduates annually, each one tuition-schooled in the craft. Meanwhile, trust in the press sits at or near record lows -- Gallup finds roughly three in ten Americans expressing confidence in mass media, with majorities of both parties agreeing that reporters favor one side. The factories have never produced more. The product has never sold worse. The Method, hollowed out The cruelty of the Mizzou caption is that the school is, on paper, the best of them. The Missouri Method -- the founding idea of 1908 -- puts students in real newsrooms doing real work: six professional outlets, including an NBC affiliate and an NPR member station, where a twenty-year-old files the story and lives with the corrections. KOMU, that student-staffed NBC affiliate, was among the first to carry the news of Miller's appointment. On paper, this is the finest idea in American journalism education. It is also an idea that has been hollowed out by its surroundings, because a newsroom can teach only what its newsroom believes -- and what too many of them believe is that reporting is a form of advocacy with better sourcing. That campus should know. In 2015, the world watched student photographers get shoved and shouted off the quad at Mizzou while Melissa Click, a professor of communication -- not, it must be said, j-school faculty, a distinction the deans insisted mattered -- called for "some muscle" to remove them. It mattered to no one else. The first home of journalism education spent a news cycle as the national symbol of hostility to journalists, the university eventually fired her, and the clip outlived every explanation. Eleven years later, when a right-wing account captions a Miller video "Journalism 101 at MIZCOMO," the joke only works because nobody has forgotten. | | ---|---|--- The objection -- and what it concedes Now, the objections, because there are good ones. Miller is an advocate, not a reporter. The clip is one exchange, curated by people who wanted it to go viral. Celebrating it is cheering for your team's debater, not for journalism. Fine. But that objection concedes the whole game. The test of a school is not whether its graduates are agreeable. It is whether they can survive contact with an adversary who knows the file better than they do. A well-trained reporter wins that exchange -- or at minimum does not hand the other side the clip of the decade. If the only person in the briefing room asking what the law actually says is the president's attack dog, the failure isn't Miller's. The failure belongs to whoever taught the press that a poem is a citation. The fix The remedy is unfashionably boring. Journalism 101, real version: read the statute before the poem. Attribute every claim, including the flattering ones. Publish corrections at the same font size as the error. Cover, at some point in your education, people you did not vote for, and file the story even they would admit was fair. Grade students on the questions they got answered, not the gotchas they landed. None of this is left or right. All of it was standard practice once, which is how the profession earned the trust it has since spent. The schools should also notice what the market is telling them. "Most popular" and "most prepared" are different rankings, and readers care about only one. The programs that figure out that their true product is trust -- not clout, not activism, not access -- will own the next fifty years. The ones that keep graduating 484 degrees a year into an industry the public doesn't believe will keep supplying the other side's best footage. The caption was the degree Stephen Miller did not teach Journalism 101 this week. He never attended a j-school, he isn't a journalist, and the clip is nine years old. What he did was stand in front of the country's most expensive journalism education and demonstrate, in ninety seconds, what it forgot to include. The world's first school of journalism sits in Columbia, Missouri. This month, on the internet, its name is best known as the punchline of a lesson it didn't give. The free lecture was never Miller's. It was the caption. Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. | | ---|---|--- You're currently a free subscriber to . Peter, the Squad
is back on the Hill, and they didn’t come back to play it safe.

They’re in the halls of Congress fighting for working families. And
they’re putting in the work now so our movement can start the new
congressional term ready for what’s next.

Voters just elected Democratic majorities in both the House and the
Senate. That means real leverage, and the Squad intends to use every bit
of it. Come January, they’ll block extreme agendas, hold powerful
interests accountable, and fight for justice on every front.

Here’s what that looks like:

Taking on corporate price gouging, executive overreach, and constitutional
violations. Corporations have spent years jacking up prices on everything
from groceries to rent while working families struggle to keep up.
Meanwhile, the Trump administration has pushed the limits of its power at
every turn. The Squad will use this new majority to demand answers and
push back.

Holding the line against giveaways to the ultra-wealthy and rollbacks of
worker protections. Billionaires don’t need another tax break. Workers
need stronger protections, not weaker ones. The Squad won’t trade away
working people’s rights to make the richest people in the country even
wealthier.

Advancing progressive legislation that puts working people first, not the
well-connected. That means fighting for Medicare for All, affordable
housing, childcare, paid leave, abortion justice, and programs like SNAP
that millions of families count on to get by.

It's a standard tactic among politicians running for federal office. When you don't have anything else to campaign on, yell about lazy, do-nothing civil servants. "And if I'm elected, I will take your mandate to Washington to cut the civil service to the bone!" Pause for applause.
One of the very few who actually tried it was Bill Clinton.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..sRrAp5-sXTmYN5swoRyM4Cb0bnmw0EKT5xy33xq8scc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=225372628)
With the Cold War over, Clinton felt the federal workforce needed change. Two years later, and with Congress's support, he signed the Federal Workforce Restructuring Act of 1994, which reduced the federal workforce by nearly half a million people. Everyone, even the civil servants, had to admit the process had worked.
But Clinton never denigrated the value of civil service workers. He started the process by saying, "We will turn first to Federal employees for help. They know better than anyone else how to do their jobs if someone will simply ask them and reward them for wanting to do it better."
Civil servants provide expertise that cannot be replicated. I routinely worked with people who had thirty years of experience and were the smartest in their fields. Civil servants can be conservative and cautious in the face of change; bureaucratic conservatism often blunts fresh political appointees' desire to come in and make their mark quickly, before they have had a chance to understand the true impact of their decisions. The protection of the Civil Service Acts also guaranteed that civil servants could give an honest assessment without worrying about their jobs... well, at least it used to be that way.
Jump to 2025. Donald Trump has just been inaugurated. He campaigned on a near-hatred of government workers. One of his first actions was to illegally create the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and illegally appoint a non-government employee, Elon Musk, to run it. Trump gave Musk unlimited, extra-legal powers to fire any government employee he saw fit. DOGE began firing people capriciously, without warning and without any logical basis. Courts overturned these firings again and again; they found that nearly all of Musk's actions were illegal, but damage was done. The FAA and air safety are a prime example.
Trump started with a commission that President Biden appointed in 2023 to recommend upgrades to America's air traffic control system. Trump disbanded the commission as soon as he took office.
Then, three weeks after a tragic accident over the Potomac River, four hundred FAA employees, many in radar maintenance and aviation safety, were informed by a late Friday night email that their employment had been terminated. In the weeks that followed, another 1,300 took early retirement. Both the Professional Aviation Safety Specialist union and the Air Traffic Controllers Association warned that this would significantly affect aviation safety and airline operations, but the cuts went ahead.
We saw the impacts last week. For the first time since 9/11, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop, canceling tens of thousands of flights. Sean Duffy, the Secretary of Transportation and former MTV reality TV star, has tried to tell us that while upgrading the air traffic control system, a contractor in Arkansas was plugging a fiber-optic cable into a router, and the next thing you know, nobody was flying anywhere.
I have no idea whether that explanation is true, but here's one thing I do know. The civil servants, the group with the expertise to manage the massive job of upgrading our air traffic control systems, are largely gone. This would have left the program to contractors focused on completing the job quickly to maximize profits, and to inexperienced political appointees focused only on speed to gain recognition.
So, the next time you hear a political candidate say the federal civil service is the root of so many problems in the federal government, remind them that before DOGE fired tens of thousands of experienced civil servants, you didn't have to wait two days for your flight.
**THE NEWS YOU NEED TO SEE**
**Alabama Political reporter:**_**" Alabama Arise warns proposed SNAP rule could increase hunger"**_
The Department of Agriculture is proposing a policy change that will cut SNAP benefits for millions of people. The change will prohibit states from extending SNAP income limits to families receiving other forms of assistance. Opponents say it will push more people into food insecurity. The USDA acknowledges that the policy will remove 6.5 million people from SNAP rolls, but it will save $45 billion... the cost of one unnecessary war with Iran.
[https://www.alreporter.com/2026/11/17/alabama-arise-raises-alarm-regarding-proposal-to-limit-snap-eligibility](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/18193a0d-c7c3-4a1c-aebe-e0497222f061?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Farm Action:**_**" Rancher Prices Fall Nearly 20% Amid Trump's Beef Import Plan"**_
As predicted, Trump's plan to import tens of thousands of tons of beef from Argentina has devastated America's cattle farmers. Trump did it to try to bring down prices in the run-up to the mid-term elections. That clearly didn't work.
[https://farmaction.us/rancher-prices-fall-nearly-20-amid-trumps-beef-import-plan/?fbclid=IwY2xjawVoQflleHRuA2FlbQIxMABwZG9mAWJyaWQRMUJlYll4STE3Vjlyc2VTbmJzcnRjBmFwcF9pZBAyMjIwMzkxNzg4MjAwODkyAAEfRI-6DdusjcdF4nrbI6nLijnTC609RIbHB8zgT12nJzwjZd0vze7q18xPqPA_aem_FjRehzpcE2sq0dW9Z6Nfqg](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/299e16e9-5985-46da-91b8-6f793f77ad2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Yellow Hammer News:**_**" Defense industry gives its highest honor to Mike Rogers for 'dogged determination'"**_
In the least surprising news of the week, the National Defense Industrial Association awarded the 2026 Dwight D. Eisenhower Award to Mike Rogers (R-Lockheed Martin) for his "dogged determination" to double the defense budget no matter the need. The irony is that in his farewell address to the nation, President Eisenhower said, "In the councils of government, we must guard against the acquisition of unwarranted influence, whether sought or unsought, by the military-industrial complex. The potential for the disastrous rise of misplaced power exists and will persist."
[https://yellowhammernews.com/defense-industry-gives-its-highest-honor-to-mike-rogers-for-dogged-determination/](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f0802671-2a71-4b98-8f2d-b568917bbe38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

clean_body: 11/17/26 | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? 11/17/26 | | | Nov 17 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- It's a standard tactic among politicians running for federal office. When you don't have anything else to campaign on, yell about lazy, do-nothing civil servants. "And if I'm elected, I will take your mandate to Washington to cut the civil service to the bone!" Pause for applause. One of the very few who actually tried it was Bill Clinton. Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. With the Cold War over, Clinton felt the federal workforce needed change. Two years later, and with Congress's support, he signed the Federal Workforce Restructuring Act of 1994, which reduced the federal workforce by nearly half a million people. Everyone, even the civil servants, had to admit the process had worked. But Clinton never denigrated the value of civil service workers. He started the process by saying, "We will turn first to Federal employees for help. They know better than anyone else how to do their jobs if someone will simply ask them and reward them for wanting to do it better." Civil servants provide expertise that cannot be replicated. I routinely worked with people who had thirty years of experience and were the smartest in their fields. Civil servants can be conservative and cautious in the face of change; bureaucratic conservatism often blunts fresh political appointees' desire to come in and make their mark quickly, before they have had a chance to understand the true impact of their decisions. The protection of the Civil Service Acts also guaranteed that civil servants could give an honest assessment without worrying about their jobs... well, at least it used to be that way. Jump to 2025. Donald Trump has just been inaugurated. He campaigned on a near-hatred of government workers. One of his first actions was to illegally create the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and illegally appoint a non-government employee, Elon Musk, to run it. Trump gave Musk unlimited, extra-legal powers to fire any government employee he saw fit. DOGE began firing people capriciously, without warning and without any logical basis. Courts overturned these firings again and again; they found that nearly all of Musk's actions were illegal, but damage was done. The FAA and air safety are a prime example. Trump started with a commission that President Biden appointed in 2023 to recommend upgrades to America's air traffic control system. Trump disbanded the commission as soon as he took office. Then, three weeks after a tragic accident over the Potomac River, four hundred FAA employees, many in radar maintenance and aviation safety, were informed by a late Friday night email that their employment had been terminated. In the weeks that followed, another 1,300 took early retirement. Both the Professional Aviation Safety Specialist union and the Air Traffic Controllers Association warned that this would significantly affect aviation safety and airline operations, but the cuts went ahead. We saw the impacts last week. For the first time since 9/11, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop, canceling tens of thousands of flights. Sean Duffy, the Secretary of Transportation and former MTV reality TV star, has tried to tell us that while upgrading the air traffic control system, a contractor in Arkansas was plugging a fiber-optic cable into a router, and the next thing you know, nobody was flying anywhere. I have no idea whether that explanation is true, but here's one thing I do know. The civil servants, the group with the expertise to manage the massive job of upgrading our air traffic control systems, are largely gone. This would have left the program to contractors focused on completing the job quickly to maximize profits, and to inexperienced political appointees focused only on speed to gain recognition. So, the next time you hear a political candidate say the federal civil service is the root of so many problems in the federal government, remind them that before DOGE fired tens of thousands of experienced civil servants, you didn't have to wait two days for your flight. THE NEWS YOU NEED TO SEE Alabama Political reporter:" Alabama Arise warns proposed SNAP rule could increase hunger" The Department of Agriculture is proposing a policy change that will cut SNAP benefits for millions of people. The change will prohibit states from extending SNAP income limits to families receiving other forms of assistance. Opponents say it will push more people into food insecurity. The USDA acknowledges that the policy will remove 6.5 million people from SNAP rolls, but it will save $45 billion... the cost of one unnecessary war with Iran. Farm Action:" Rancher Prices Fall Nearly 20% Amid Trump's Beef Import Plan" As predicted, Trump's plan to import tens of thousands of tons of beef from Argentina has devastated America's cattle farmers. Trump did it to try to bring down prices in the run-up to the mid-term elections. That clearly didn't work. Yellow Hammer News:" Defense industry gives its highest honor to Mike Rogers for 'dogged determination'" In the least surprising news of the week, the National Defense Industrial Association awarded the 2026 Dwight D. Eisenhower Award to Mike Rogers (R-Lockheed Martin) for his "dogged determination" to double the defense budget no matter the need. The irony is that in his farewell address to the nation, President Eisenhower said, "In the councils of government, we must guard against the acquisition of unwarranted influence, whether sought or unsought, by the military-industrial complex. The potential for the disastrous rise of misplaced power exists and will persist." Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. ## **Grand Theft Crazy: What Washington and Parents Need to Wake Up To**
Today on Capitol Hill, the Senate Judiciary Subcomittee on Crime and Counterterrorism is convening a groundbreaking bipartisan hearing on the massive online gaming platform Roblox - and what millions of American children are actually being exposed to behind closed bedroom doors.

Most parents and grandparents know Roblox simply as that popular game their kids are constantly asking for money to play.
What families don't realize is what is lurking inside that platform. Beyond the inappropriate content accessible inside user-created spaced, the ability for predators and unknown adults to reach out directly to young children has become a massive, growing crisis - one that has already sparked nearly 200 federal lawsuits.
**Yet as alarming as the Roblox hearing is, we are about to hit an entirely new level of concern this Thursday when** _**Grand Theft Auto VI**_**launches.**
Analysts are already projecting billions of dollars in opening sales and a $2 billion hit to the U.S. economy from millions of workers expected to call out sick on release day.
**But the lost productivity isn 't even close to the real problem. **
What this game is going to allow players to do - and what millions of underage kids across America are about to treat as normal, everyday entertainment - should alarm every single parent, leader, and citizen in this country.

| | Who are the supervillains shaping today's culture, and how are their ideas influencing the world around us? Peachy Keenan returns to the Moms for America Podcast after her lively conversation about Domestic Extremist, this time bringing her signature humor and fearless commentary to Supervillains, a satirical look at the people, movements, and ideologies reshaping American culture. With sharp wit and plenty of laugh-out-loud observations, Peachy shines a light on the cultural craziness we see unfolding around us. But beyond the humor is an important conversation about recognizing the forces influencing our families, challenging the ideas that threaten our values, and standing strong for what matters. It's time to pull back the curtain, call out the absurdities, and remember that we don't have to sit back and watch culture happen. Join us for a fun, thought-provoking conversation with Peachy Keenan! | | America is facing a battle of ideas, and the stakes couldn't be higher. From the rise of socialism and efforts to rewrite American history to attacks on parental rights, religious freedom, and the sanctity of life, some dangerous ideas are gaining ground. And moms cannot afford to sit this one out. But there is good news. America was built on enduring principles that still have the power to unite, strengthen, and restore our nation. Capitalism and free markets, protecting women's spaces, freedom to live our faith, gratitude for America, racial reconciliation, parental rights, and the belief that every life is sacred are ideals worth defending and passing on to the next generation. Our children are growing up in a culture where these values are increasingly challenged. That makes our role as mothers more important than ever. We must teach our children to recognize the difference between ideas that undermine freedom and those that make America exceptional. Six terrible ideas. Seven great ones. One nation worth fighting for. Peachy Keenan Is Here! | | | Who are the supervillains shaping today's culture, and how are their ideas influencing the world around us? Peachy Keenan returns to the Moms for America Podcast after her lively conversation about Domestic Extremist, this time bringing her signature humor and fearless commentary to Supervillains, a satirical look at the people, movements, and ideologies reshaping American culture. With sharp wit and plenty of laugh-out-loud observations, Peachy shines a light on the cultural craziness we see unfolding around us. But beyond the humor is an important conversation about recognizing the forces influencing our families, challenging the ideas that threaten our values, and standing strong for what matters. It's time to pull back the curtain, call out the absurdities, and remember that we don't have to sit back and watch culture happen. Join us for a fun, thought-provoking conversation with Peachy Keenan! Find the Moms for America Podcast on all your favorite platforms , , and . | | | | | | 6 Terrible Ideas vs. 7 Great Ones - Fighting for America's Soul | | | America is facing a battle of ideas, and the stakes couldn't be higher. From the rise of socialism and efforts to rewrite American history to attacks on parental rights, religious freedom, and the sanctity of life, some dangerous ideas are gaining ground. And moms cannot afford to sit this one out. But there is good news. America was built on enduring principles that still have the power to unite, strengthen, and restore our nation. Capitalism and free markets, protecting women's spaces, freedom to live our faith, gratitude for America, racial reconciliation, parental rights, and the belief that every life is sacred are ideals worth defending and passing on to the next generation. Our children are growing up in a culture where these values are increasingly challenged. That makes our role as mothers more important than ever. We must teach our children to recognize the difference between ideas that undermine freedom and those that make America exceptional. Six terrible ideas. Seven great ones. body:
I’m writing today to thank you so much for your support for the DNC this year. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10344%2E22930333%2Ev8-Kse)
---
Derek, This is Emily, the DNC’s Email & SMS Director. I’m writing today to thank you _so much_ for your support for the DNC this year. Now that the midterms have ended, I want to show you some of the work that DNC supporters like you helped fund. **Because of you, the DNC was able to:**
* Invest more than $1 million dollars every month into state Democratic parties.
* Recruit an army of organizing volunteers to make **3.3 million calls** , including 450,000 calls to Democrats who voted in 2020 but then sat out in 2024.
* Train and deploy voter registration fellows, who registered thousands of voters across key battlegrounds in Arizona and Nevada.
* Host more than 250 training sessions with 25,000 Democrats across all 50 states.

**And that’s just _some_ of the impact that you’ve had this year, Derek.** Democrats won big, across the country, this year because we built a grassroots movement in every state, and we couldn’t have done it without you. _Thank you._** **[Donate](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.9s4leO&amount=7&refcode=em_20261117_10344_fr&t=6&akid=10344%2E22930333%2Ev8-Kse)** Let’s do it again in 2028,
Emily Email & SMS Director
Democratic National Committee

body:
The race for my old House seat is one of the closest elections of 2026.
#
Peter,
Though the midterm elections happened two weeks ago, the race for my old U.S. House seat in Minnesota’s 1st district still hasn’t officially been called.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261117-jj.dvEt16&amount=5&refcode=em20261117-1355&t=1&akid=1355%2E34582%2EHwYj_I)
**With 99 percent of votes counted, it looks like Small Town PAC-endorsed Democrat Jake Johnson won. But since he’s only up by a razor-thin margin of about 300 votes, less than 0.1 percent, his Republican opponent has requested a recount.**
[****](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261117-jj.dvEt16&amount=5&refcode=em20261117-1355&t=2&akid=1355%2E34582%2EHwYj_I)
Like me, Jake is a former high school teacher and father who decided to run for Congress to fight for working-class communities in Southern Minnesota. He’s ready to go to Washington to make things cheaper, fight corruption, and invest in our small towns.
This district hasn’t been represented by a Democrat since I stepped away from it in 2018 to run for governor, and some political pundits considered it a long shot at being flipped this November. Just two years ago, Republican Brad Finstad won by 17 points.
But thanks to an outpouring of grassroots support, Jake’s campaign was able to knock tens of thousands of doors, bring voters from all walks of life together, and go up against the flood of spending by the Republican incumbent and his corporate donors.
[**Jake flipped this seat from red to blue with your help — now, we need to make sure he has the resources to keep fighting if this goes to a recount. So Peter, will you split a contribution of $5 or more to Small Town PAC and Jake’s legal fund today?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261117-jj.dvEt16&amount=5&refcode=em20261117-1355&t=3&akid=1355%2E34582%2EHwYj_I)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261117-jj.dvEt16&amount=5&refcode=20261117-1355&t=22&akid=1355%2E34582%2EHwYj_I)**
This is going to end as one of the closest U.S. House races of 2026. Let’s help Jake finish the job and officially become the 254th Democrat in the House!
With gratitude,
Tim

Anyone who’s spent time on the water in Hampton Roads knows that the tide always turns.
Four years ago, I lost this seat. I didn’t second-guess the fight then, and I’m glad I didn’t.
On November 3rd, the tide turned.
The people of Hampton Roads sent me back to Congress. And we weren’t alone. Across the country, voters delivered a blue wave that flipped the House with what’s on track to be the largest Democratic majority in decades. Democrats flipped Senate seats in places like Kansas, Texas, and Ohio to take back that chamber too.
All cycle, I said Democrats needed to flip just three House seats to take back the majority. We blew right past that number, and VA-02 was one of the seats that got us there.
I’m proud of that. I’m also not one to oversell, so here’s the plain truth about how we did it:
We spent down to zero.
When you’re in a Toss-Up race against an incumbent and a flood of outside money, you don’t hold anything in reserve. You leave it all on the deck.
Every dollar went into this victory. That was the right call. But it means that before I’m sworn in, we need to settle up.

**November 17, 2026**
A patch of ground sits a step from my kitchen, a mess of uneven earth and scattered attempts to enrich the soil. At the table, I spend weeks planning in two-minute bursts, waiting for a clearer idea before beginning, knowing full well that the path appears through the work.
Wages increased 0.4%. Consumer prices increased 0.4%. Real average hourly earnings showed no increase. The numbers show an economy moving, but not necessarily moving households forward.
In the capital, representatives trade blame after a loss and sign rushed pledges for work left undone, while public responsibility calls for something more enduring: stewardship.
Financial security requires more than income, margin, or predictability.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

# [Commerce dodges the Megaspeed Entity List question, praises Lutnick](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Commerce and Justice released a joint statement Monday on the Megaspeed probe that opened in 2024, praising Secretary Howard Lutnick **[while leaving unexplained why the company was never added to the Entity List.](https://substack.com/redirect/23208f01-bb07-4af1-b189-63bd36757a4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Investigation timeline:** Commerce opened the Megaspeed case in 2024 over restricted chips possibly reaching China and began requesting Nvidia sales records by May 2025.
* **Nvidia 's own ban:** Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its no-sell list in June 2025 after Commerce investigators visited Singapore and interviewed then-CEO Alice Huang.
* **Entity List gap:** Despite pressure from four other agencies, Commerce never added Megaspeed to the federal Entity List, which would have restricted American technology sales beyond Nvidia's private ban.
* **Bessent 's framing:** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday that Commerce "has the pen" and that Treasury, War, USTR and State had wanted Megaspeed blacklisted for months.

# [Gmail users report email issues days after Outlook outage](https://substack.com/redirect/2725cab1-7be7-4ebf-a274-c7553284728b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Gmail users reported an uptick in trouble sending and receiving emails over the past 24 hours, according to Downdetector, days after Microsoft Outlook suffered a multi-day outage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/91a07d7d-40f1-4a29-a0c4-5a4ab4c09db4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Downdetector spike details:** Reports peaked around 2:40 p.m. ET Monday before easing, then began climbing again Tuesday morning.
* **Google status check:** Google's Workspace Status Dashboard has not listed any active disruptions.
* **Prior outage context:** The apparent trouble comes days after Microsoft Outlook, one of the most widely used enterprise email platforms, suffered a multi-day outage last week.
* **Widespread Outage:** DownDetector[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/429d8c68-d5b3-4288-a473-d5bb1d36d1cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[is reporting widespread outages](https://substack.com/redirect/429d8c68-d5b3-4288-a473-d5bb1d36d1cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **including, Apple's iCloud ecosystem, Marriott, the National Weather Service, as well as **[reports of the classified NSA internal communications network.](https://substack.com/redirect/17c158ed-11d8-4333-8109-aeb55cc92379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/17c158ed-11d8-4333-8109-aeb55cc92379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

# [Nvidia shares drop ahead of earnings as Huang resignation fallout continues](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia shares **[dropped nearly 3.5% at the open Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/0d2f7e6d-5a4d-483e-a780-cfd08d14ebf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the company headed into after-the-bell earnings following a 4% Monday drop to the lowest close since July 1, 2025, amid fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Huang resignation details:** The board announced Huang's resignation Thursday after reports of a relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy; he told employees of the affair in a Nov. 8 email.
* **Board actions:** Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back and has established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson.
* **Scrutiny and rules:** Lawmakers are increasing scrutiny of Chinese access to advanced chips restricted by export controls; BIS announced an interim final rule Monday aimed at preventing remote access by Chinese companies.
* **Petition context:** An online petition for Huang's reinstatement drew more than 190,000 signatures, including Elon Musk.

* * *
# [Nvidia warns buyers of legal risks on China cloud access](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia has **[warned customers that a proposed law could expose them](https://substack.com/redirect/3397a4e8-f72e-448f-88ba-0f2dd899c5eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and the chipmaker to legal action over Chinese firms gaining remote access to AI chip capacity hosted overseas.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Policy shift:** Nvidia said it would not sell chips to customers who rent more than 50 percent of the GPUs to Chinese companies.
* **RASA details:** The Remote Access Security Act, which passed the House in January but has not yet cleared the Senate, would give the government broader authority over cloud access similar to physical hardware.
* **BIS rule:** Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security announced an interim final rule Monday designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
* **Customer messaging:** Nvidia messaged buyers in recent months about the risks under the proposed act and related controls.

# [Neocloud stocks face big trouble from Nvidia Eisman says](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Investor Steve Eisman **[speaking on CNBC](https://substack.com/redirect/815e9ac8-0364-41e8-a221-e1f550d7c86c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** said Tuesday that AI neocloud stocks will be the biggest losers from the Nvidia fallout, describing the company as a "virtual vertical holding company and it's unwinding."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Neocloud losses:** CoreWeave and Nebius have each fallen more than 50 percent over the last three months as the AI trade pulled back.
* **Anthropic view:** Eisman said lingering profitability concerns around Anthropic's expected Thursday debut are less important to the broader AI trade as expectations have come down.
* **Data center risk:** He flagged potential slowdowns in data-center construction if Democrats take control in January, ranging from a 10-30 percent reduction to a full moratorium that he said would put the country into recession overnight.
* **Hyperscaler benefit:** In a moderate slowdown scenario, Eisman said hyperscalers would benefit most and become cash-flow positive again.

# [Fed's Warsh starts task force hearing on AI risks](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh opened the first task force hearing Monday on how AI could raise GDP growth or increase unemployment, saying the central bank's role is neither advocacy nor opposition.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Warsh 's framing:** "Our job is to prepare for whatever comes next," Warsh said, noting AI's ability to generate new ideas and speed innovation.
* **Best-case path:** In an optimistic scenario, Warsh said AI could produce productivity gains shared across labor and capital, lifting real GDP persistently above its long-run average while the U.S. stays near full employment.
* **Risk focus:** He highlighted higher unemployment and bad actors using AI for nefarious purposes as "highly disruptive and economically costly," referring to the technology as "super intelligence."
* **Barr 's warnings:** Governor Michael Barr outlined financial-system risks including AI-fueled bank runs, herd-like trading models, and autonomous agents exploiting vulnerabilities.

# [Lisa Cook declines White House hearing on possible removal](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook will not take part in a White House hearing on her possible removal, her lawyer told administration officials Monday night, arguing the process is unfair and threatens the Fed's independence.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Process concerns:** Abbe Lowell wrote that Cook has no legal obligation to join an unfair hearing and a duty to protect the institution's unique status; the administration has ignored nearly 20 letters raising issues.
* **Allegations origin:** The hearing stems from a committee Trump created in August to examine 2021 mortgage fraud claims involving two properties listed as primary residences; Cook's team says the conduct predates her time in office and is not cause for removal.
* **Trump comments:** Her lawyers cite Trump's public statements, including an October 10 remark calling her an "automatic no vote" on lowering rates, as evidence the outcome is predetermined.
* **Original schedule:** The hearing had been set for November 5.

* * *
# [JPMorgan systems recover after hours long "technical outage"](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
JPMorgan Chase systems were coming back online Monday after an hourslong nationwide outage traced to a software release, with the FBI confirming no signs of malicious cyber activity.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Software release cause:** The disruption stemmed from a software update rolled out earlier Monday that affected a subset of systems, limited to Chase and related transactions.
* **Customer impact timeline:** Issues began around 10 a.m. at some branches, with customers reporting trouble accessing accounts and withdrawing funds; resolved by early afternoon at branches.
* **Official statements:** Chase said it was a technical issue not cyber-related, and customers retained access to accounts and funds though some transactions took longer.
* **Other banks unaffected:** Bank of America, Wells Fargo, PNC and U.S. Bank reported normal operations, with Zelle functioning as usual.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/3dd2bddd-f88f-464c-94eb-9d398dced523?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# **[Microsoft pins Outlook outage on hidden bug from July](https://substack.com/redirect/9cd4c90a-8fc8-466a-bc80-e71853a6a559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Microsoft **[revealed a software bug introduced in July](https://substack.com/redirect/6cfd3b2e-0bc9-4b35-a216-e99be175b23e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and undetected for months triggered last week's global Outlook and Microsoft 365 outage that left more than 80 percent of servers unresponsive at peak.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7733ae8f-34ae-4433-bcc4-f2b04e8c5a7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Root cause factors:** The latent defect combined with increased demand from Teams traffic shift and reduced server capacity overwhelmed the network gateway during peak U.S. hours on Nov. 12.
* **Peak impact:** At its worst, more than 80 percent of servers became unresponsive as the failure cascaded globally after safeguards failed to contain it.
* **Recovery process:** Engineers applied a fix and restarted servers gradually; Teams and some apps recovered earlier while Exchange Online email lagged.
* **Not cyber or AI:** Executive Charles Lamanna confirmed it was neither a cyberattack nor caused by AI tooling, and apologized for the business impact.

name: Eric Sorensen
subject: The Gayest Congress in American History
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143607213/660781658/-1160839820?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMmRkMDdmYS1iMGUyLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zuhpX1x3Ur-YnVQze1b_IGCyZRg_oxNALSJTvonbe2w=)
Peter, Early in my career as a meteorologist, I was forced out of a job because being gay went against the station’s “morals clause.” Surviving that experience made me determined to fight against injustice so discrimination doesn’t happen to anyone else. I’ve been thinking about that a lot this week, because the Congress that takes office in January is on track to be **the most LGBTQ+ Congress in American history** , with at least 17 out members. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143607214/660781659/-1160839820?refcode=em-11.17.26-all-d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMmRkMDdmYS1iMGUyLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zuhpX1x3Ur-YnVQze1b_IGCyZRg_oxNALSJTvonbe2w=) Here’s where it gets _even better_ : **All nine of us who sought re-election in the House won.** And I get to say that one of those nine is representing Illinois’ 17th District. Somewhere there’s a kid in Rockford or Peoria or the Quad Cities who is wondering whether there’s a place for them, and a Congress that looks more like the country they live in is a pretty good answer. I didn’t run for Congress to make history, but because I spent twenty years earning this community’s trust by showing up before and after the storm, and I wanted to keep doing that work for my neighbors. I’ll keep fighting to make sure every American is treated with dignity, including the servicemembers I’ve stood up for on the House floor. I’ll keep doing it for everyone in this district, whether they voted for me or not. And I’m grateful beyond words that you’ve been part of this. body:
| | | Welcome back to the WFP newsletter, Peter! On November 3rd, voters across the country sent a clear message to Trump and MAGA. They delivered it by electing Working Families Party candidates the pundits had confidently written off, even as corporate money outspent us by millions in race after race. **The best part? All over the map, Democrats won by running on**** _our_****agenda: bringing down the cost of living, rooting out corporate corruption, taxing the billionaire class, hitting pause on data centers, and ending foreign wars.** That’s no accident. For years, the corporate wing of the Democratic Party told us these ideas were “too bold to win.” This cycle, our candidates proved them wrong, and the rest of the party followed our lead. **Now, let’s dive into the highlights, plus some big news about who should lead the Senate:**
* * *
**_All We Did Was Win Win Win_** Here’s the quick version. _(The long version is further down, for those of you who like to savor things.)_
* WFP candidates won nearly _every_ federal general election battleground race.
* We’re sending at least **16** new WFP members to the House and **2** to the Senate.
* More than **100** new WFP state legislators were elected, and **38** of them flipped Republican-held seats.
* WFP candidates helped flip legislative chambers in **Pennsylvania** , **Michigan** , **Georgia** , **Wisconsin,** and **Arizona**.**Every one of those states except Georgia now has a Democratic trifecta.**
* **Jane Kim** , our former California WFP State Director, won her statewide race for Insurance Commissioner with more than four million votes. Four. Million.

That’s a lot of winning, and none of it happened without supporters like you. Want to help keep it going?
[**Become a dues-paying WFP member for $10 or more a month, or make a one-time donation today, to help carry this movement through 2027 and all the way to 2028.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9DMNvF0eW12ixTi_e6u1brkkMadhgtOm695gUxB_vffEfk97KthhMYcsCRreQyG1gvINoQ6AnUF1r2wd1tnEDA1gezECWrCf-5e2jgHByTLlmQmz-hvrNHDJIJys2xNbvkOtzC7hfzmdJmUoKzUkI9YCwevpB1FgUnI23IG0obMggHNQHmCBtZlay4xlpoLzyQTICJ_xo4Vm8Dl1IqBCB0RdstFjMbCS27Da2JmHeGDjJ_dhI8r6EERZBcu9AANmrKkven9uxr331zpUlsiL1IIxXxLg7IOnzQg9cwa0w2SyY9YTiUrP8irowTjeAjySiFjHTzlJcJXuoZFNzbAD_lf-ghp11nGh1k66-JlDP0SE/4vt/wMm3q9ooTfOGswrt63X2XA/h0/h001.vj5Wc92pt--zUc0a9PkCtgW3aL7a3ODj_3gKc2yvWps) **[Donate »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9DMNvF0eW12ixTi_e6u1brkkMadhgtOm695gUxB_vffEfk97KthhMYcsCRreQyG1gvINoQ6AnUF1r2wd1tnEDA1vNtngjxwjZdRAHYVy3XWteEGLjGAnbT5zhLWBdzTFJmz02Mt-4o69KDAmuyPuyjgaXdV-7tCkEMhCLV0yebOD0fMkWWYtVBCtyDkS5951DegS-tfMX5Z4HxvUjinb1XOcW3d2OEX2O-b_0viXYgwFS4YVEw9ZgSr6_mAgyTc8ppCR9pAX252cTNYj9BtmUsKnguwAusLiZVPZuW9cBIvb6VPJJR1lSXUrZB_AInsOwJcm-JwPiL28UE0rULBLpN-vFwhe4jNVxSTyiIUuho70/4vt/wMm3q9ooTfOGswrt63X2XA/h1/h001.0nZi5C_nyKeoCaR1P7q5L8SX62-SbDGPcEAbT18PSiY)**
* * *
**_First Up: Senate Leadership_** Election Day was only the warm-up. Now the real work begins: turning these victories into policies that actually make a difference in people’s lives. And step one is making sure the Senate is led by someone who’s ready to fight for working people. So we’re making it official: **WFP is endorsing Senator Chris Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader.** He’s a co-sponsor of the Medicare for All Act. He’s fought the out-of-control funding for ICE and DHS, and he even flew to El Salvador to demand the return of Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a constituent the Trump administration wrongly deported. He was also one of the first senators to sign on to block offensive weapons sales to the Israeli government. **That’s _exactly_ the kind of leadership voters just asked for.** More than 1,000 of you have already called your Senators to urge them to back him. Let’s keep the phones ringing: Text **LEADER** to **30403** or dial **833-636-3260**. We’ll give you a script, so all you need is a phone.

* * *
**_The Full Picture_** Choosing new leadership is just one piece of the bigger picture. [**In a new post-election memo,**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYd6eLP33O2GRZpvuK-wGuROD5UGDO2q2cP_bAqM3DTBFoonrHoePrLhDR-p5xbTC41pmLP-PF0yuxxTxktuN4WiivMcYVNq0ySWfTRlNt_F-d2WgAl4tzdvotYD3BdEH5wH5Mu-zJ5SHHsMtFT1fk9P74i7PYuVSD87uZT2RD8WOoBUBLTI16TERcoyoYThrnArl-27jFMj7v2TIJyEU0AnyYNIV0wBOMo-hVhVSZTJ_atxHPsCK-Lf65I9hfjEgA/4vt/wMm3q9ooTfOGswrt63X2XA/h2/h001.3H0IbVK20iPB5a-MR6erfRnEs7SGVSKhgaFsoL8vPz4) our National Director, Maurice Mitchell, breaks down how we won, what it means for the Democratic Party, and where our movement goes from here. **If you read one thing about this election, make it this one:** **[Read the memo »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYd6eLP33O2GRZpvuK-wGuROD5UGDO2q2cP_bAqM3DTBFoonrHoePrLhDR-p5xbTC41pmLP-PF0yuxxTxktuN4WiivMcYVNq0ySWfTRlNt_F5TTurV7YYsLd2VQO3Xru8m-Oj6rRk2w9pTNT7z8oGu0Jk19cZ-87D0aGJPxhOrA4-mscLEbDxuc7Ontj5haFTfRVR4ZqvVROQ4o7fbKWs1wwDX1UCksdKLfT65s26HD_vKRuTZO3XH5Zvi39AAsIjw/4vt/wMm3q9ooTfOGswrt63X2XA/h3/h001.oVG4U3pe4TtoqPX6PoRZru3RxkOUbqzC1FH4w1dujGQ)**

**_Winning the Battlegrounds_** Back to Abdul. **His Senate race in Michigan was one of the toughest in the country, Peter.** Outside groups spent nearly $350 million to stop him and hit him with Islamophobic attacks along the way, but voters sent him to Washington anyway. **That same pattern held across the map:** the more money and attacks our opponents threw at WFP candidates, the more voters rallied behind them. Next door to Abdul, **Will Lawrence** won one of the most expensive House races in the country, and in **Pennsylvania** , firefighter and union leader **Bob Brooks** posted the biggest margin of any swing district in the state. Out in **California’s** Central Valley, **Randy Villegas** , an autoshop owner who once served on CA WFP’s state committee, won with one of the biggest overperformances in the country. Beyond the battlegrounds, WFP members won **seven more races** in safer seats where the Democratic establishment backed someone else, including former NJ WFP State Director **Analilia Mejia** in New Jersey and longtime WFP leader **Brad Lander** in New York City.
* * *
**_WFP Is the Future of the South_** Some of our most telling results came in places nobody expected us to compete. Which, frankly, is our favorite kind of place. In **Georgia** , WFP candidates helped Democrats flip a legislative chamber. The shift was so decisive that the outgoing Republican governor quietly called off his planned special session to redraw the state’s maps. Guess the crayons can go back in the box. In **Florida** , WFP state legislator **Angie Nixon** came within three points in a race the Democratic establishment had written off. _Three points_. In _Florida_. And in **Tennessee** , **Justin J. Pearson** ran 20 points ahead of Kamala Harris’s 2024 numbers in a district gerrymandered specifically to keep him out. For years, the Democratic establishment has treated the South as somewhere to skip. These results say otherwise. **We showed up, and we’re**** _not_****leaving.**
* * *
**_Power in the Statehouses_** Congress wasn’t the only place we cleaned up, Peter. **WFP also elected more than 100 new state legislators, and many of them won in places Republicans had gotten very comfortable in:** In **Wisconsin** , Oak Creek Mayor and labor union leader**Dan Bukiewicz** won a State Assembly seat south of Milwaukee that Republicans have held since 2013. In **Michigan** , elementary school teacher **Jaime Churches** won back the Downriver State House seat she lost two years ago. In **Washington’s Yakima Valley** , state human rights commissioner and daughter of immigrant farmworkers **Chelsea Dimas** won her rematch for a State House seat, beating the Republican who edged her out in 2024. In some states, WFP champions will now help _run_ the legislature. In **Colorado** , WFP-backed **Rep. Jen Bacon** was chosen as Speaker of the House, the first Black woman to hold the job. That means long-stalled ideas like stronger worker protections and rent control finally have a real shot. WFP champions also won leadership roles in **Arizona**. And in **Delaware** , nearly half of the Democrats in the legislature were elected with WFP’s support. WFP champion Rep. Madinah Wilson-Anton came within just two votes of becoming Speaker. Two votes!

clean_body: | | | Welcome back to the WFP newsletter, Peter! On November 3rd, voters across the country sent a clear message to Trump and MAGA. They delivered it by electing Working Families Party candidates the pundits had confidently written off, even as corporate money outspent us by millions in race after race. The best part? All over the map, Democrats won by running on ouragenda: bringing down the cost of living, rooting out corporate corruption, taxing the billionaire class, hitting pause on data centers, and ending foreign wars. That’s no accident. For years, the corporate wing of the Democratic Party told us these ideas were “too bold to win.” This cycle, our candidates proved them wrong, and the rest of the party followed our lead. Now, let’s dive into the highlights, plus some big news about who should lead the Senate: All We Did Was Win Win Win Here’s the quick version. (The long version is further down, for those of you who like to savor things.) WFP candidates won nearly every federal general election battleground race. We’re sending at least 16 new WFP members to the House and 2 to the Senate. More than 100 new WFP state legislators were elected, and 38 of them flipped Republican-held seats. WFP candidates helped flip legislative chambers in Pennsylvania , Michigan , Georgia , Wisconsin, and Arizona.Every one of those states except Georgia now has a Democratic trifecta. Jane Kim , our former California WFP State Director, won her statewide race for Insurance Commissioner with more than four million votes. Four. Million. That’s a lot of winning, and none of it happened without supporters like you. Want to help keep it going? First Up: Senate Leadership Election Day was only the warm-up. Now the real work begins: turning these victories into policies that actually make a difference in people’s lives. And step one is making sure the Senate is led by someone who’s ready to fight for working people. So we’re making it official: WFP is endorsing Senator Chris Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader. He’s a co-sponsor of the Medicare for All Act. He’s fought the out-of-control funding for ICE and DHS, and he even flew to El Salvador to demand the return of Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a constituent the Trump administration wrongly deported. He was also one of the first senators to sign on to block offensive weapons sales to the Israeli government. That’s exactly the kind of leadership voters just asked for. More than 1,000 of you have already called your Senators to urge them to back him. Let’s keep the phones ringing: Text LEADER to 30403 or dial 833-636-3260. We’ll give you a script, so all you need is a phone. The Full Picture Choosing new leadership is just one piece of the bigger picture. our National Director, Maurice Mitchell, breaks down how we won, what it means for the Democratic Party, and where our movement goes from here. If you read one thing about this election, make it this one: After the Vote The week after the election, nearly 100,000 people joined us for After the Vote , our post-election mass call, to celebrate these wins and talk about what comes next. Okay, Your Turn Abdul shared his priorities. Now we want to hear yours, Peter. How are you feeling after the election? What do you make of Democratic leadership? Which new champions are you most excited about? It only takes a few minutes, and it helps make sure WFP keeps fighting for what matters most to you. This is your party, after all. Winning the Battlegrounds Back to Abdul. His Senate race in Michigan was one of the toughest in the country, Peter. Outside groups spent nearly $350 million to stop him and hit him with Islamophobic attacks along the way, but voters sent him to Washington anyway. That same pattern held across the map: the more money and attacks our opponents threw at WFP candidates, the more voters rallied behind them. Next door to Abdul, Will Lawrence won one of the most expensive House races in the country, and in Pennsylvania , firefighter and union leader Bob Brooks posted the biggest margin of any swing district in the state. Out in California’s Central Valley, Randy Villegas , an autoshop owner who once served on CA WFP’s state committee, won with one of the biggest overperformances in the country. Beyond the battlegrounds, WFP members won seven more races in safer seats where the Democratic establishment backed someone else, including former NJ WFP State Director Analilia Mejia in New Jersey and longtime WFP leader Brad Lander in New York City. WFP Is the Future of the South Some of our most telling results came in places nobody expected us to compete. Which, frankly, is our favorite kind of place. In Georgia , WFP candidates helped Democrats flip a legislative chamber. The shift was so decisive that the outgoing Republican governor quietly called off his planned special session to redraw the state’s maps. Guess the crayons can go back in the box. In Florida , WFP state legislator Angie Nixon came within three points in a race the Democratic establishment had written off. Three points. In Florida. And in Tennessee , Justin J. Pearson ran 20 points ahead of Kamala Harris’s 2024 numbers in a district gerrymandered specifically to keep him out. For years, the Democratic establishment has treated the South as somewhere to skip. These results say otherwise. We showed up, and we’re notleaving. Power in the Statehouses Congress wasn’t the only place we cleaned up, Peter. WFP also elected more than 100 new state legislators, and many of them won in places Republicans had gotten very comfortable in: In Wisconsin , Oak Creek Mayor and labor union leaderDan Bukiewicz won a State Assembly seat south of Milwaukee that Republicans have held since 2013. In Michigan , elementary school teacher Jaime Churches won back the Downriver State House seat she lost two years ago. In Washington’s Yakima Valley , state human rights commissioner and daughter of immigrant farmworkers Chelsea Dimas won her rematch for a State House seat, beating the Republican who edged her out in 2024. In some states, WFP champions will now help run the legislature. In Colorado , WFP-backed Rep. Jen Bacon was chosen as Speaker of the House, the first Black woman to hold the job. That means long-stalled ideas like stronger worker protections and rent control finally have a real shot. WFP champions also won leadership roles in Arizona. And in Delaware , nearly half of the Democrats in the legislature were elected with WFP’s support. WFP champion Rep. Madinah Wilson-Anton came within just two votes of becoming Speaker. Two votes! Watch Our WFP Champions Grow Many of this year’s biggest wins went to people who have organized alongside WFP for years, as staff, members, and longtime allies. Jane Kim founded California WFP and led it as State Director. Now she’s California’s next Insurance Commissioner , after beating an insurance industry that spent heavily to keep its friendly relationship with its own regulator. But Jane isn’t the only former WFP State Director heading to Washington. In New Jersey , Analilia Mejia won a full term in Congress, capping a remarkable year: an upset in a crowded February primary, a special election win in April, and now the seat outright. In Wisconsin , JoCasta Zamarripa , a WFP champion through her years on the Milwaukee City Council and in the state legislature, won her race for Secretary of State. In Georgia , Ruwa Romman moved up to a hard-fought State Senate seat. And in Washington , educator and WFP Solidarity Pack member Kelabe Tewolde won his race for state representative, defeating a corporate Democrat who had held his seat for 27 years. WFP Mayors From Coast to Coast The momentum didn’t stop at the statehouse. It walked right into city hall. In Los Angeles , Nithya Raman is taking the reins. She joins New York’s Zohran Mamdani and Chicago’s Brandon Johnson, which means WFP-backed mayors now lead the country’s three largest cities. Read that again. And it’s not just the biggest cities. In Providence , voters elected David Morales as mayor, and he’ll govern alongside a WFP-aligned City Council majority ready to deliver the rent stabilization he ran on. And in DC , newly-elected Mayor Janeese Lewis George will fight for working-class residents with a fresh crew of WFP councilmembers at her side. No big deal. (It’s a big deal.) Moving On Up in NY Speaking of New York, more than 360,000 voters there backed Governor Kathy Hochul on the WFP line. That puts us on track to pass the Conservative Party and claim Row C on the ballot. But it wasn’t just the governor’s race. Voters across the state backed WFP candidates for the legislature, too, which means New York WFP is set to send its biggest delegation ever to Albany. Photo of the Week The front page of The Morning Call in Pennsylvania’s Lehigh Valley, the Thursday after the election, says it all — sweeping wins in purple districts. Someone on staff has definitely already laminated it: Those wins helped flip the Pennsylvania legislature and give Democrats a trifecta in one of the most important swing states heading into 2028, opening up big opportunities for WFP. Okay, victory lap’s over. Now we get to work, Peter.Winning elections was never the end goal. Passing policies that make people’s lives better is. This election gave Democrats a real shot at winning back working-class voters and building a majority that lasts through 2028 and beyond. That means lower costs, real accountability for corporations and billionaires, and limits on Big Tech’s power over our communities. And we’ll have our champions’ backs every step of the way. As we keep fighting to block the far right and build working-class power across the country, your grassroots support matters more than ever. In solidarity (and still a little giddy), Team WFP Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Reply directly to this email and let us know. This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. # **Black Friday Virtual Silent Auction Is Live!**
---
|
---
| The holiday season is here, and what better way to give meaningful gifts while supporting an incredible cause? Autism Health's Black Friday Virtual Silent Auction is officially OPEN, offering a wonderful opportunity to shop for unique holiday gifts while making a difference in the lives of individuals and families impacted by autism. From one-of-a-kind collectibles and wellness packages to special experiences and thoughtful gifts, there's something for everyone! Whether you're shopping for loved ones or treating yourself, every winning bid helps support Autism Health's mission of advancing research, providing educational resources, expanding family support programs, and making meaningful care more accessible to those who need it most. Our auction is completely virtual, so you can browse and place bids from the comfort of your home, no matter where you live. It's a wonderful way to get a head start on your holiday shopping while giving back to a cause that truly matters. **The auction is LIVE NOW and closes Sunday, November 29, 2026, at 6:00 PM PST!** Don't wait until the last minute! Explore our auction items, place your bids, and share this opportunity with friends and family. Click the link below to browse our auction and start bidding today! Thank you for supporting Autism Health and helping us continue creating better solutions for a brighter tomorrow. Your generosity makes our mission possible!

|
---

This special event will bring together philanthropists, community leaders, healthcare professionals, and advocates who share a commitment to advancing research, education, and innovative solutions for individuals with autism and their families.

We invite you to be part of this extraordinary evening at the beautiful Sherwood Country Club in Thousand Oaks, California, while taking advantage of our exclusive Early Bird ticket and table pricing, available through November 30, 2026!

**Date:** Saturday, January 30, 2027
**Location:** Sherwood Country Club
[320 W Stafford Road
Thousand Oaks, CA 91361](https://us.list-manage.com/TrkBYhaf9bB?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332)

# **Join Us for The Autism Health Summit!**
---
|
---
| The countdown has begun for the **2027 Autism Health Summit** , taking place **April 29 through May 1, 2027, at The Legacy Center Resort & Spa in San Diego, California.** Join parents, physicians, researchers, healthcare professionals, educators, and advocates from around the world for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and hope.

**We're excited to announce that our headline speakers include Del Bigtree, Dr. Henry Ealy, and Tyler Hudson, with many more nationally recognized experts to be announced in the coming months.** Attendees will gain valuable insights into the latest research, innovative therapies, integrative medicine, environmental health, and practical strategies to support individuals with autism and related neurological conditions.

We're also pleased to offer **Continuing Medical Education (CME) and Continuing Education Unit (CEU) credits** for eligible healthcare professionals, making the Autism Health Summit an outstanding opportunity to expand your knowledge while earning valuable continuing education credits.

Now is the best time to register! Secure your ticket before prices increase and receive **$50 OFF your registration during the month of November by using promo code AHS50 at checkout.** This special offer expires at the end of the month.

Whether you're a parent, caregiver, practitioner, educator, therapist, or advocate, the Autism Health Summit offers an unparalleled opportunity to learn from leading experts, connect with a passionate community, and leave empowered with practical knowledge you can apply immediately.

Reserve your seat today using the registration link below. **We look forward to welcoming you to San Diego, April 29 through May 1, 2027!**

* * *
We are, without a doubt, governed by the greatest collection of morons and losers in the history of the United States. Possibly the world. I don't have the data, but I'm comfortable with the claim.
As I write this, I'm in the back of an Uber in L.A., on my way to do Stephanie Miller's radio show. I'm out here for an event tonight. And I'm sitting here genuinely worried that I'm not home with my family, with my son, in the event that something really, cataclysmically bad happens.
Because every time I turn on the news or open social media, every other story is about some new catastrophe in this country and the administration's complete inability to do fix it. A nationwide ground stop. United arlines down for half the day yesterday. Hackings and outages pile up, with tech systems going dark one after another and no credible explanation from the people in charge. Our banking systems are being disrupted. Apparently our national intelligence systems are, as well.
I'm not trying to freak anybody out. Maybe it's all random shit. Maybe one piece of technology broke and sent the dominoes tumbling. Maybe we're under a cyberattack. I have no idea.
What I wish is that I could trust my government on two things. First, that it would be honest with me about what's happening. Second, that it's staffed by competent people who know what they're doing and will act in the best interest of the public.
I know neither of those things is true. I know they're going to lie their asses off to protect themselves, to look good in the eyes of the public. And I know they don't have a clue what they're doing.
Then I check Twitter and see Markwayne Mullin trying to talk about technology he very clearly doesn't understand. A lot of people want to point out that he's a plumber, and I'm sure some people find that funny. But his occupation isn't the problem. The problem is that he's anti-intellectual and refuses to surround himself with people who know what the hell they're doing.
You can be put in a position of power without being an expert on everything. There are plenty of smart plumbers in this country. But if you get thrust into a leadership role that requires you to understand technology, cybersecurity or AI, you damn sure better hire people who fucking know something about it. You'd better surround yourself with people who are genuinely going to act in the public's best interest.
Government is supposed to be about improving people's lives, not about lining the pockets of a small handful of people who are already this fucking rich and powerful. Instead, we're governed by idiots, idiots for a cause. And that cause is keeping Donald Trump happy, keeping the Epstein class out of jail, and helping them concentrate even more wealth and power. What else do these people do at this point?
And it's not just me who's nervous. I just saw a clip of Sean Hannity talking about how he's a doomsday prepper with a year's worth of food in his basement, all but bragging about having a ton of guns. And he's not just doing this for the fun of it. They seem freaked out, too.
* * *
#### _**[We shouldn't have to wonder whether the people running our government are competent enough to keep our families safe. We shouldn't have to guess what's happening when critical systems go down. And we sure as hell shouldn't have to rely on an administration that puts loyalty to Donald Trump ahead of the public good to tell us the truth. That's why Endless Urgency exists. Not to scare you. Not to feed the outrage machine. But to help us understand what's happening, demand answers, and remind each other that we're not powerless. Paid subscribers make that work possible. For $8/month, you can help us strengthen our independent coverage and keep this work accessible to everyone.](https://substack.com/redirect/3d11c2ef-b0f1-4398-8d24-b58fdd8ef5fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/3d11c2ef-b0f1-4398-8d24-b58fdd8ef5fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
I'm not losing my mind. I'm looking around and thinking that this is exactly what the American people voted against two weeks ago. They do not trust that the people they elected are doing anything to improve their lives or keep them safe. Everybody is struggling right now, and these people have learned absolutely nothing.
The President of the United States couldn't be bothered to show his face on camera for nearly a week in the middle of a nationwide crisis. In moments like this, people generally want to see their president and know he's on top of things. Maybe not this one. Maybe it was better that he stayed hidden. But I'd like to know where the hell he was. Was he having a dementia episode? Getting his hairpiece refitted? What the hell was going on? It's bizarre.
So I'm sitting in this Uber thinking about my son, and I'm not worried about a website being down for an afternoon. I'm worried about what happens if the electrical grid goes down. I'm worried about what happens next, whatever that is, because I don't trust this government to be doing what it's supposed to be doing behind the scenes to keep us safe.
That's why you want qualified, knowledgeable public servants at every level of government. Right now there are a thousand Markwayne Mullin's, a thousand Sean Duffy's, a thousand Pete Hegseth's, a thousand Kash Patel's and a thousand Donald Trump's running the federal government, and none of them know anything except how to steal from the working class. It's a grift on top of a grift on top of, you guessed it, another grift.
We've got two more years of this. Thankfully, Democrats will have one hand on the wheel when we take over the House and the Senate in January. God bless. We'll keep exposing these people and slowing them down from the horrible things they want to do. But it's going to be a rough two years.
That means we have to keep building our communities. We have to keep standing with and supporting one another. We have to keep fighting for the people we love.
I'll be honest with you: I'm feeling the anxiety today. I'm anxious about where all this ends up. Like a lot of you, I wonder whether we can make it through the next two years.
I believe we will, and we'll do it together. Americans have gotten through far worse times than this. But this is absolutely absurd.
So take care of yourselves today. Make good decisions. Be kind to your fellow human beings. And if your internet's down, go outside.
Love you guys.
With urgency,
--Mike

Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know. We are, without a doubt, governed by the greatest collection of morons and losers in the history of the United States. Possibly the world. I don't have the data, but I'm comfortable with the claim. As I write this, I'm in the back of an Uber in L.A., on my way to do Stephanie Miller's radio show. I'm out here for an event tonight. And I'm sitting here genuinely worried that I'm not home with my family, with my son, in the event that something really, cataclysmically bad happens. Because every time I turn on the news or open social media, every other story is about some new catastrophe in this country and the administration's complete inability to do fix it. A nationwide ground stop. United arlines down for half the day yesterday. Hackings and outages pile up, with tech systems going dark one after another and no credible explanation from the people in charge. Our banking systems are being disrupted. Apparently our national intelligence systems are, as well. I'm not trying to freak anybody out. Maybe it's all random shit. Maybe one piece of technology broke and sent the dominoes tumbling. Maybe we're under a cyberattack. I have no idea. What I wish is that I could trust my government on two things. First, that it would be honest with me about what's happening. Second, that it's staffed by competent people who know what they're doing and will act in the best interest of the public. I know neither of those things is true. I know they're going to lie their asses off to protect themselves, to look good in the eyes of the public. And I know they don't have a clue what they're doing. Then I check Twitter and see Markwayne Mullin trying to talk about technology he very clearly doesn't understand. A lot of people want to point out that he's a plumber, and I'm sure some people find that funny. But his occupation isn't the problem. The problem is that he's anti-intellectual and refuses to surround himself with people who know what the hell they're doing. You can be put in a position of power without being an expert on everything. There are plenty of smart plumbers in this country. But if you get thrust into a leadership role that requires you to understand technology, cybersecurity or AI, you damn sure better hire people who fucking know something about it. You'd better surround yourself with people who are genuinely going to act in the public's best interest. Government is supposed to be about improving people's lives, not about lining the pockets of a small handful of people who are already this fucking rich and powerful. Instead, we're governed by idiots, idiots for a cause. And that cause is keeping Donald Trump happy, keeping the Epstein class out of jail, and helping them concentrate even more wealth and power. What else do these people do at this point? And it's not just me who's nervous. I just saw a clip of Sean Hannity talking about how he's a doomsday prepper with a year's worth of food in his basement, all but bragging about having a ton of guns. And he's not just doing this for the fun of it. They seem freaked out, too. * I'm not losing my mind. I'm looking around and thinking that this is exactly what the American people voted against two weeks ago. They do not trust that the people they elected are doing anything to improve their lives or keep them safe. Everybody is struggling right now, and these people have learned absolutely nothing. The President of the United States couldn't be bothered to show his face on camera for nearly a week in the middle of a nationwide crisis. In moments like this, people generally want to see their president and know he's on top of things. Maybe not this one. Maybe it was better that he stayed hidden. But I'd like to know where the hell he was. Was he having a dementia episode? Getting his hairpiece refitted? What the hell was going on? It's bizarre. So I'm sitting in this Uber thinking about my son, and I'm not worried about a website being down for an afternoon. I'm worried about what happens if the electrical grid goes down.
