That's why you want qualified, knowledgeable public servants at every level of government. Right now there are a thousand Markwayne Mullin's, a thousand Sean Duffy's, a thousand Pete Hegseth's, a thousand Kash Patel's and a thousand Donald Trump's running the federal government, and none of them know anything except how to steal from the working class. It's a grift on top of a grift on top of, you guessed it, another grift. We've got two more years of this. Thankfully, Democrats will have one hand on the wheel when we take over the House and the Senate in January. God bless. We'll keep exposing these people and slowing them down from the horrible things they want to do. But it's going to be a rough two years. That means we have to keep building our communities. We have to keep standing with and supporting one another. We have to keep fighting for the people we love. I'll be honest with you: I'm feeling the anxiety today. I'm anxious about where all this ends up. Like a lot of you, I wonder whether we can make it through the next two years. I believe we will, and we'll do it together. name: Chad Bianco
subject: Must read.
body:
Spared by Newsom.

| | | | | |
---
| |

My fellow Californians,
**Twice, California voters rejected attempts to abolish the death penalty. Twice, Sacramento was told NO.**
Yet Gavin Newsom is moving to overturn 548 death sentences handed down by juries who heard the evidence and delivered their verdicts.

These are convicted murderers, serial killers, child predators, and sadistic torturers. Monsters who kidnapped innocent children, subjected helpless victims to unimaginable suffering, and brutally extinguished innocent lives.
Their crimes represent the darkest depths of human cruelty and depravity. Behind every one of these atrocities are grieving parents, shattered families, and loved ones who have spent decades waiting for justice.
**Now Governor Newsom believes his judgment should outweigh the decisions of juries and the California voters.**
**The people have spoken. Sacramento needs to listen.**
As your Sheriff, I will always stand for victims, accountability, and the rule of law.

With gratitude,
**Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County**

This is Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D-LA), and I need to talk to you about your health care.
Last year, Trump and his MAGA Congress pushed through nearly $1 trillion in cuts to Medicaid to help pay for tax breaks tilted toward the wealthiest Americans.
Families here in Louisiana are feeling it. Across this district, I hear from people worried their rural hospital won’t be there when they need it, and seniors wondering how they’ll afford their medicine.
On Dec. 12, voters in Louisiana’s 5th District get to decide who will stand up for them in Washington.
**My MAGA opponent has lined up behind Trump at every turn. Send him to Congress, and Trump gets one more vote to keep cutting the care our families depend on.**
Me? I’ve spent my career fighting to protect it.
As a State Representative, I wrote a law strengthening seniors’ right to buy Medicare supplement coverage. And I helped pass a law requiring Medicaid to cover the dental procedures patients need before they can get other critical medical care.
That’s the record I’m taking to Washington. In Congress, I’ll stand with our new Democratic majority to protect and expand Medicare and Medicaid, lower the cost of prescription drugs, and keep our rural hospitals open.
But I can’t do any of it if MAGA keeps this seat.
**I lead by 0.73% heading into the Dec. 12 runoff, in one of the reddest districts in America.** If I win, I’ll be the first Black woman Louisiana has ever sent to Congress. MAGA will do everything it can to stop us.

body:
Fund our deputies. No new committee

| | | | | |

| STOP DEFUNDING OUR DEPUTIES $125 million shortfall · Over 600 fewer deputies at risk
---
| |

**A MESSAGE FROM SHERIFF CHAD BIANCO.**

Friends,

Thank you to everyone who called and emailed your Supervisor over the last couple of weeks. The Board is hearing you. **We're not done. We have until January to make our voices heard.**

Our message is simple:
* **Fund our Sheriff's Department.**
* **Do not create another "oversight" committee.**

---
| | | | | |

We already have federal, state and local oversight. Another committee won't make your neighborhood safer. It just spends more of your money and hands more control to politicians, all while making the jobs of our deputies harder.
**Call your Supervisor. Email your Supervisor.** Be respectful, be assertive, and keep it short: fund our deputies, and no ad hoc committee. **Then share this with your Facebook friends and neighbors.**
The Board needs to hear from all of us, not just the activists who already pressured the Board to **defund the Sheriff’s Department by $125 million.**
---

clean_body: Your policy may renew automatically. A better deal takes a little checking. ** | | | | | Tuesday, November 17, 2026 Good morning,Flyover readers! Some bills get paid month after month without much thought. Car insurance is often one of them. But just because you've been with the same company for years doesn't mean it's still the best fit for your budget. Today's sponsor, , makes it easy to compare car insurance quotes side by side and see whether a better option is available. If it's been a while since you checked your rate, take a look below. It could be a simple way to keep more money in your pocket. Cole The Flyover Your car insurance deserves a second look. You probably know what you're paying for groceries, gas, and your monthly subscriptions. But when's the last time you checked whether you're getting a competitive price on car insurance? It's easy to stick with the same company for years. The policy renews, the payment goes through, and you move on with your day. But renewing your policy doesn 't tell you whether another insurer could offer a better deal. That's why we're sharing , today's sponsor. helps you compare car insurance quotes side by side, making it easier to see how your options stack up. Its network includes more than 100 insurance companies, and checking rates won't affect your credit score. Here's why checking matters: Different insurance companies can quote different prices for the same driver. Your driving history, vehicle, and location all play a role, but insurers weigh those details differently. So even if you haven't changed cars or had an accident, it can still be worth comparing your options. Maybe you'll find a lower price for the coverage you need. Maybe you'll feel better about the policy you already have. Either way, you'll have more information before your next renewal. And with plenty of other demands on your budget, a recurring bill is a sensible place to look for potential savings. Peter, Things have not slowed down since this month's historic election. While every single statewide race flipped, the story downballot was tougher. Our own race came closer to flipping than any Democratic challenger in history - just **5 points**. Our local Texas House District race is even closer. After weeks of counting mail-in and provisional ballots, the Republican incumbent defeated Democrat Brittany Black by just **SEVEN VOTES**. That tells me our odds for flipping these seats in 2028 are stronger than they've ever been, and I'm committed to seeing that through. But right now there's a more urgent fight on our hands. You may recall me talking about Keith Self's outrageous campaign targeting McKinney City Council officials and our Republican mayor over the city's approval of EPIC City, a planned mosque and community center meant to serve our community's Muslim population. Well that fight isn't over. In fact, it's heating up right now. Peter,

I’m checking in one more time from new member orientation in Washington. Since last week, incoming members have been in workshops and meetings with the broader caucus so we can hit the ground running once we’re sworn in on January 3rd.

But you didn’t send me here to wait until January to start delivering.

**Last Thursday, I joined 50 incoming freshmen to sign a letter to House Democratic leadership. We are calling on them to adopt a rule banning Congressmembers and their spouses from owning or trading stocks.**

Members of Congress should not be getting rich trading in stocks for industries they’re supposed to be regulating. We’re asking leadership to put this rule in place the day the new Congress is sworn in.

A stock trading ban on its own won’t fix Washington. We’ll need bigger reforms, including a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United and end the dark money in our elections. But voters sent a loud and clear message on Election Day that they’re fed up with corruption and self-dealing.

This is an important way to show them we heard that message.

clean_body: | = Peter, I’m checking in one more time from new member orientation in Washington. Since last week, incoming members have been in workshops and meetings with the broader caucus so we can hit the ground running once we’re sworn in on January 3rd. But you didn’t send me here to wait until January to start delivering. Last Thursday, I joined 50 incoming freshmen to sign a letter to House Democratic leadership. We are calling on them to adopt a rule banning Congressmembers and their spouses from owning or trading stocks. Members of Congress should not be getting rich trading in stocks for industries they’re supposed to be regulating. We’re asking leadership to put this rule in place the day the new Congress is sworn in. A stock trading ban on its own won’t fix Washington. We’ll need bigger reforms, including a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United and end the dark money in our elections. But voters sent a loud and clear message on Election Day that they’re fed up with corruption and self-dealing. This is an important way to show them we heard that message. | | Thanks - and I’ll be in touch again soon. name: Team Victoria
subject: GOP Lost Because We Failed to Deliver. Why? The Power of Money.
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/spartzforcongress/statement-17473919?e=57d5bacdc3)
---
| |
---
| | **Spartz: GOP Lost Because We Failed to Deliver. Why? The Power of Money.**
---
| | Republicans lost because we failed to do the one thing voters hired us to do: stop Washington from treating taxpayers like an open ATM. Some will blame the Iran war. Others will point to the hatred of President Trump or the Democrats’ well-oiled Obama machine. Those factors mattered. But the central failure is simpler and more damning: Americans handed Republicans the House, the Senate, and the White House to lower costs, cut spending, challenge monopolies, and confront corruption. Too many of my colleagues chose instead to protect the same special interests that bankroll both parties’ political machines. I pressed for a stronger reconciliation package and voted against the weak instructions because I refused to pretend half-measures were victories. I reluctantly supported a revised version only after securing limited reforms to claw back some of the trillions insurers and hospital systems have siphoned off through Medicaid overbilling. It was not enough. Worse, Republicans failed to explain even those modest wins, allowing Democrats to rebrand efforts to stop fraud and overbilling as “cutting benefits.” Washington runs on legalized corruption. Special interests extract subsidies, regulatory protections, no-bid contracts, and government-protected monopolies. They return a fraction of that money through campaign contributions, PAC donations, and lucrative future K Street jobs. Powerful lobbyists and entrenched D.C. staffers control the agenda, while members either lack the backbone to resist or dream of cashing in themselves. Challenge the machine, and you become the target of fabricated attacks and multimillion-dollar smear campaigns. Play along, and the money and favorable coverage arrive on schedule. The legislative scorecard tells the story. A reconciliation-compatible SAVE Act died in the Senate. Healthcare price transparency never reached the floor. Medicare PBM transparency and hospital billing reforms were pushed to 2028. Medicare Advantage overbilling was ignored entirely. No serious fiscal commission was created to confront the debt, Social Security, and runaway spending. Housing reforms to help first-time buyers stayed bottled up. Energy, agricultural, and small-business reforms, including incentives for struggling rural communities, were stripped or left out in the Senate. Delphi pension restoration remains stuck in the Senate, leaving retirees waiting. When lobbyists cannot kill reforms in the House, they run to the Senate, where the swamp runs even deeper. Meanwhile, Democrats spent years building a permanent grassroots, data, and communications machine designed to exploit frustration and shift blame. Republicans still have nothing comparable. Too many in our own ranks refuse to confront corruption within the party, fight special interests, or support candidates who will actually deliver. We still have weeks left with a Republican Congress. Leadership should force votes on unfinished business: immediate healthcare transparency, a fiscal commission, Delphi pensions, housing, energy and rural reforms, and a viable path for election integrity. Let voters see who is willing to fight, and who is not. The same dynamics play out in state and local races, just with smaller checks. The establishment will now use these losses to argue that primary challenges are reckless and that so-called “sensible moderates” must be protected. Yet these are the same politicians whose failure to deliver created the opening for Democrats, and who have repeatedly joined them to protect special interests. We cannot rebuild the Republican Party by protecting the politicians who helped break it. Unless we confront corruption within our own ranks, 2028 will be even worse. George Washington lost battles, but he never surrendered the war. Thomas Paine was right: “These are the times that try men’s souls.” We lost a battle, not the Republic. Americans can still take it back, but only if enough Republicans choose the voters over the money.

| Team, As CADEM's Communications Director, I spent the final weeks before Election Day focused on one thing: making sure Californians understood what Democrats were fighting for and what was at stake. Now, Democrats have won. And we won _big_. But winning does not mean our work is over. It means it's time to shift our strategy. We need to: 1️⃣ **Explain what comes next.** We need to help Californians understand what Democrats are fighting for and what our victories make possible. 2️⃣ **Push back with the facts.** We must respond to misinformation early and give organizers, volunteers, and voters accurate information. 3️⃣ **Keep the conversation going.** We have to continue listening and talking directly with Californians instead of waiting until the next election to reconnect. We do this through year-round digital outreach and grassroots organizing: sharing accurate information, supporting volunteers, and continuing the direct voter conversations that helped us win. Pedestrians walk past a sign reading "No one surrenders here" in Havana, Cuba, on Nov. 14, 2026. Photo by Joaquin Hernandez/Xinhua via Getty Images.
_Story by Blake Burdge. Published in collaboration with[Belly of the Beast](https://substack.com/@bellyofthebeastcuba)._
In September, a rare public opinion poll backed by two major U.S. universities suggested that Cubans overwhelmingly blame their own government for the country's economic crisis and do not oppose a U.S. military intervention.
The results appeared to vindicate the Trump administration's hard-line policies toward the island.
But a close look at the survey, which has been [promoted](https://substack.com/redirect/4239fbd1-3e1d-4c5f-b2fc-01f041f7a3af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as "the first-ever nationally representative study" of Cuba and has been cited by [PBS NewsHour](https://substack.com/redirect/79f8055a-cb82-4aa2-be76-6cf16c95f4c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Americas](https://substack.com/redirect/a9a21ce2-4910-4025-9290-8c5ac89a35fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) _[](https://substack.com/redirect/a9a21ce2-4910-4025-9290-8c5ac89a35fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[Quarterly](https://substack.com/redirect/a9a21ce2-4910-4025-9290-8c5ac89a35fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Foreign](https://substack.com/redirect/52cfd967-742c-44e6-a2bb-f7727df632c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) _[](https://substack.com/redirect/52cfd967-742c-44e6-a2bb-f7727df632c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[Affairs](https://substack.com/redirect/52cfd967-742c-44e6-a2bb-f7727df632c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), reveals a stark disconnect between how the poll was presented and what its findings actually show.
Media coverage also failed to examine the millions of dollars in U.S. government funding received by the organizations connected to the poll--including for programs aimed at influencing the very public opinion the poll sought to measure.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3a6e844d-403a-41e3-965b-f73c5bf005f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
##### In this video, Belly of the Beast asked Cubans in the streets of Havana whether they would support a U.S. military intervention.
## The Money Behind the Poll
The poll was overseen by Vanderbilt University's Latin American Public Opinion Project Lab (LAPOP), which [describes](https://substack.com/redirect/6f6e8c3c-edcb-4505-b373-2c8df9331543?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its flagship survey, AmericasBarometer, as "the leading source of comparative public opinion data on democracy and governance across the Americas" since 2004.
Data from AmericasBarometer frequently appears in[ State Department reports](https://substack.com/redirect/f2ca7778-12cc-44e5-b10f-cab217e1fea4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),[ academic research](https://substack.com/redirect/84803d02-9410-4de5-8701-b37da00c77d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and the World Bank's "[governance indicators](https://substack.com/redirect/12eaee6d-0237-4557-91a3-1f5c1ca9f5c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
Every two or three years, AmericasBarometer publishes a region-wide report called Pulse of Democracy. This year's report features polls from 21 countries, including, for the first time, Cuba.
For the Cuba poll, LAPOP contracted a company called CubaData ([incorporated](https://substack.com/redirect/08fa2581-38c0-4d9a-a28c-2d1646197f17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Titusville, Florida, as Cuba Data LLC) that specializes in conducting digital surveys on the island via cell phone.

## U.S.-Funded Apps
The U.S. government has long funded media and communications projects aimed at bringing about regime change in Cuba.
Journalist Tracey Eaton[ documented](https://substack.com/redirect/5eb0067f-ab01-4e1b-94ac-749247db61fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than $218 million in U.S. government disbursements for Cuba "democracy promotion" (also known as "regime change") programs between 2001 and 2021. Roughly $25 million went to media and information projects, of which NED managed $15.6 million.
Some programs have clearly stated their intentions. For example, a 2019 USAID initiative [offered up to $2 million](https://substack.com/redirect/a1d148da-c537-4444-9739-78a8ea133370?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for projects that would "dispel the myths about the successes of the Cuban Revolution," including its education and healthcare systems.
Other programs were covert. One of the most notorious was ZunZuneo, a text-message network modeled on Twitter that launched in Cuba in 2010 thanks to $1.7 million in funding from USAID.
ZunZuneo's plan was to attract subscribers with sports, music, and weather updates, and then introduce political content that could spark anti-government protests, according to documents[ obtained by the Associated Press](https://substack.com/redirect/7cf8dc57-1531-45eb-84e0-1fe257b84545?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2014.
More than 40,000 Cubans used the network without knowing the U.S. government was behind it.
The revelations embarrassed USAID and led to Congress grilling its administrator, Rajiv Shah. Sen. Patrick Leahy (D-Vt.), who chaired the subcommittee overseeing the agency's funding, [called the project](https://substack.com/redirect/8c4d8637-5c71-462b-8c2b-8433dc8d9920?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "dumb, dumb, dumb."
More than a decade later, the U.S. government is surreptitiously funding another social media app aimed at Cubans.
Apretaste, the app CubaData uses to recruit and register its survey respondents, bills itself as a free social network for Cubans, promising users the freedom to express themselves "without fear of censorship." Its [app-store listings](https://substack.com/redirect/fb9fbb76-6262-4311-8977-d4d6f28c3e20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) name Agora Cuba as its developer but make no mention of its NED funding.
Salvador Pascual, Agora Cuba's executive director,[ told EFE](https://substack.com/redirect/84e907c8-37f0-4c17-a0d7-4a7eb58e8403?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a 2016 interview that the app would be used to conduct market research and polling for U.S. companies. "We are the only ones who have this information about Cuban people, who also want to socialize," he said.
The app has been used[ repeatedly to recruit people to participate in polls conducted by CubaData](https://substack.com/redirect/1f5f3c48-7337-4e82-b1c2-cef8e1947f38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which is [run by Diaz Espi](https://substack.com/redirect/f161f7c1-be64-4d6b-a7a5-05c9b5120b3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Those polls in turn are regularly [publicized](https://substack.com/redirect/b849084a-2dbe-4e37-a95f-fa212ddadb75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Diaz Espi's Diario de Cuba.
Asked about the potential for bias in hiring a polling organization that is both funded by the U.S. government and led by an outspoken exile known for his anti-government activism, Jordan responded that LAPOP "adheres to rigorous scientific standards to ensure that its research is non-partisan."
In a written response via email, Diaz Espi told Belly of the Beast and Drop Site that Diario de Cuba did not participate in the LAPOP survey or share staff, resources, or user databases with CubaData or Agora Cuba. He said he did not participate in the survey's design, implementation, or analysis, and that his own role was "exclusively institutional." He did not specify what that meant.
He said NED and NDI supported separate, earlier research conducted by CubaData, but did not finance LAPOP's Cuba poll.
Pascual did not respond to requests for comment.
## How Blame Became the Headline
The Cuba poll asked 73 questions, but one of them has dominated media coverage of it: "Who is primarily responsible for the current crisis facing Cuba?"
Respondents could make only one choice.
Seventy-four percent chose the Cuban government. Sixteen percent chose the U.S. government.

## A Nationally Representative Poll?
The Pulse of Democracy report describes the poll as "a rare window into how Cubans understand the country's current crisis, who they hold responsible, and what they see as the country's most urgent priorities."
The report omitted a key detail disclosed in LAPOP's [technical documentation](https://substack.com/redirect/d586ecf8-8134-41b5-861f-37dec0271ec8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): respondents were drawn from a pool of CubaData users who had registered through the Apretaste app. The app can be downloaded on Android devices, but iPhone users must use a VPN to access it; Apple's app store geoblocks users physically located in Cuba to avoid violating U.S. sanctions. Apretaste is not widely known on the island--Belly of the Beast and Drop Site asked more than three dozen Cubans if they had heard of it and only one said they had (although they had not downloaded or used it).

Screenshots of the Apretaste app.
The app offers a kitchen sink of features, including daily prayers and jokes, a dating service, and news (most of the featured media outlets are openly opposed to the Cuban government, and several are U.S.-government funded).
Apretaste also offers a chance to win cash prizes in raffles by participating in surveys. We entered false information about our age, marital status, race, and education level in the most recent survey--about the importance of pets in everyday life. There was no process to verify our identity.
Vanderbilt spokesperson Julia Jordan said CubaData screened for bots or "heavy multi-device usage" and its "communication and data transfer are protected by advanced encryption." She did not respond to questions about how respondents' age and residence were verified or whether duplicate submissions could be identified.
In exchange for completing the survey, we received virtual credits usable for raffle entries. Winnings accumulate in a separate dollar-denominated balance. Apretaste says users can [claim their prizes](https://substack.com/redirect/605c52ea-c7dc-411c-81ad-03e29fc17668?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as mobile phone credit with Cubacel, Cuba's state-owned mobile service, or as USDT, a cryptocurrency pegged to the U.S. dollar, once they reach its minimum payout threshold.
The app displayed more than 100 users who had won raffles for participating in the AmericasBarometer survey. Each user's profile and information--including name, age, race, and city of residence--was visible.
Vanderbilt has touted the poll, which it[ says](https://substack.com/redirect/c1a657db-dbc0-46d0-ab6a-00d907b0f015?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) collected responses from 1,095 adults living in Cuba, as "[the first-ever nationally representative study](https://substack.com/redirect/4239fbd1-3e1d-4c5f-b2fc-01f041f7a3af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" of Cuba.
The report itself contradicts this claim, acknowledging the survey was not nationally representative because it was based on an online panel that skewed younger, more urban, and more connected to the internet.
According to Jordan, "political and security restrictions" prevented researchers from randomly selecting respondents from Cuba's population.
She did not respond to questions about why a poll that was not nationally representative was promoted as if it were.
"The researchers can claim that they collected data from a specific number of Cubans, but they should not claim that the sample is nationally representative," said Krosnick. "Simply stating that there is no other way to conduct a survey in Cuba is not an excuse for the use of misleading language that cultivates the impression that the survey is more rigorous and valuable than it is."
## What Cubans Think Other Cubans Think
One of the report's featured findings states that "opposition to U.S. military intervention appears limited."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2628f605-43c4-44f0-8b93-a462f3af34cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A chart showing how survey respondents answered a question about what they think other Cubans think about a U.S. military intervention. Source: LAPOP Lab, The 2026 Pulse of Democracy.
Unlike[ the other 72 questions in the poll](https://substack.com/redirect/df5f0936-308d-4464-8c51-6134f3999522?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which asked respondents their opinion, this question asked people what they thought other Cubans' opinions were.
Forty-three percent answered that they believed most Cubans would support an intervention. No question asked whether the respondents themselves would support an intervention.
According to Jordan, the question was framed in this way due to Cuba's "politically sensitive environment...where respondents may be reluctant to disclose their personal views on controversial political questions."
However, the survey asked other seemingly controversial questions directly, such as whether respondents had confidence in Cuba's president and whether they believed the country should be annexed by the United States.
Krosnick questioned the value of asking people what they think about what other people think.
"Answers should not be viewed as correctly indicating how other people would feel or as correctly indicating how the respondent would feel," he said.
Jordan agreed.
"The results should not be interpreted as a direct measure of personal support for military intervention," she wrote in an email response. "Nor should we assume that respondents can accurately predict how other Cubans would react."
Jordan declined to answer why this disclaimer was not included in the Pulse of Democracy report or in any of Vanderbilt's promotional language.
## A Long History of Shaping Public Opinion in Cuba
Despite the questions surrounding the LAPOP poll, its finding that many Cubans blame their government for the country's crisis will come as no surprise to anyone who spends time on the island.
Cuba's economy has been in free fall for eight years as "maximum pressure" sanctions have scared off foreign trade, investment, and credit while decimating the state's ability to provide basic social services that were long taken for granted. Since January, Trump's oil blockade and punishing secondary sanctions are plunging the country into a crisis that UN experts have called a "[silent Gaza](https://substack.com/redirect/ab2f9db4-f050-41a4-a47d-9e23e2e65781?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
But sanctions are an abstract concept. On the ground in Cuba, people can't see executive orders and Treasury Department regulations--only their effects.
Turning hardship into anger directed at the Cuban government was precisely what State Department official Lester Mallory proposed in an April 1960[ memo](https://substack.com/redirect/4877fc8e-1bd6-4379-9ab2-59b5fdc54520?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that argued for economic warfare on Cuba**** less than**** two years**** before the embargo was imposed by John F. Kennedy.
Mallory called for denying Cuba money and supplies to drive down wages, cause hunger, and desperation, and bring about the government's overthrow. "The only foreseeable means of alienating internal support," Mallory wrote, was "through disenchantment and disaffection based on economic dissatisfaction and hardship."
U.S. efforts to destroy Cuba's economy, he wrote, should be "as adroit and inconspicuous as possible."
Sixty-six years later, Mallory's strategy is in full display.
As the U.S. government systematically cuts Cuba off from the rest of the world, it also discreetly funnels millions of dollars a year to organizations whose mission is to convince people both on and off the island that the Cuban government is solely to blame for the country's economic crisis.
The recipients of those funds include media outlets aimed at a Cuban audience, such as Diario de Cuba,__ that report on the country without mentioning U.S. sanctions or their impact.
One question the LAPOP poll did not ask: Where do Cubans receive news and information about the causes of the crisis they are enduring?
If it had, the answers might have revealed that the same organizations and individuals measuring public opinion in Cuba were also shaping it.

In September, a rare public opinion poll backed by two major U.S. universities suggested that Cubans overwhelmingly blame their own government for the country's economic crisis and do not oppose a U.S. military intervention. The results appeared to vindicate the Trump administration's hard-line policies toward the island. But a close look at the survey, which has been as "the first-ever nationally representative study" of Cuba and has been cited by , and , reveals a stark disconnect between how the poll was presented and what its findings actually show. Media coverage also failed to examine the millions of dollars in U.S. government funding received by the organizations connected to the poll--including for programs aimed at influencing the very public opinion the poll sought to measure. In this video, Belly of the Beast asked Cubans in the streets of Havana whether they would support a U.S. military intervention. The Money Behind the Poll The poll was overseen by Vanderbilt University's Latin American Public Opinion Project Lab (LAPOP), which its flagship survey, AmericasBarometer, as "the leading source of comparative public opinion data on democracy and governance across the Americas" since 2004. Data from AmericasBarometer frequently appears in, and the World Bank's "." Every two or three years, AmericasBarometer publishes a region-wide report called Pulse of Democracy. This year's report features polls from 21 countries, including, for the first time, Cuba. For the Cuba poll, LAPOP contracted a company called CubaData ( in Titusville, Florida, as Cuba Data LLC) that specializes in conducting digital surveys on the island via cell phone. CubaData is co-owned by Pablo Diaz Espi, a Cuban exile who shortly after the fall of the Berlin Wall. Diaz Espi Spain, where he is the founder of a Madrid-based news outlet called Diario de Cuba whose agenda is to "." Both Diario de Cuba and CubaData have been the beneficiaries of U.S. government funding. Between 2013 and 2021 , Diario de Cuba received grants totaling at least $2.3 million from the National Endowment for Democracy (NED), according to figures published in annual reports, academic studies, and news articles. NED describes itself as a non-governmental organization that "promotes democracy" around the world, but it receives its entire budget from Congress and has assumed many of the CIA's former activities, funding political parties, unions, media outlets, and other civil society organizations to advance U.S. foreign policy objectives. "A lot of what we do today was done covertly 25 years ago by the CIA," Allen Weinstein, a former NED president,. | | ---|---|--- The National Endowment for Democracy awarded $2,387,601 in grants to Asociacion Diario de Cuba between 2013 and 2021 according to NED grant figures for , , , , , , , and , as published in annual reports, academic studies and media reports. In 2026, NED is , including programs to "challenge the state's narrative by exposing regime failures," expose the Cuban government's "malign influence in Latin America," and disseminate research on dismantling Cuba's power structures in a "post-authoritarian context." Whether Diario de Cuba has continued to receive funding is difficult to determine because NED no longer publicly identifies many grant recipients, a policy it says is intended to protect them from government retaliation. Last year, however, NED President Damon Wilson and board member Mel Martinez, a former Republican senator from Florida, , including Diario de Cuba, saying they "undermine the regime's legitimacy." In addition to NED funding, Diario de Cuba has also received money from the State Department. In September 2020, the U.S. Embassy in Havana awarded the outlet a $12,960 contract for news-monitoring services,. In 2022, the outlet received a $530,000 State Department grant "to strengthen Cuban civil society and boost youth participation in advancing democratic demands," . CubaData has also received funding from NED. In 2021, the company was the beneficiary of a to the National Democratic Institute (NDI), an organization affiliated with the Democratic Party that was established to receive NED funding and carry out U.S.-funded democracy-promotion programs abroad. NDI contracted CubaData to use polling data "to analyze Cubans' needs, perceptions and beliefs about topics of public interest." At the time, NDI's Cuba program was by Karla Velasquez Figuera, a Venezuelan lawyer based in Mexico who served as an intermediary between Cuban dissidents and the State Department, . Cuban state television intercepted telephone and text exchanges between Velasquez and dissidents, portraying her as the "godmother" of the San Isidro Movement, a prominent anti-government organization. Velasquez also carried out "" activities at Diario de Cuba for Diaz Espi. The experience, in a recent interview, led to her later being hired as "" for CubaData. In a about "latent dissidence" in Cuba, Velasquez thanked NED and NDI for making it possible to implement the study's data-collection methodology. Velasquez did not respond to a request for comment about her work with NDI, Diario de Cuba, and CubaData. CubaData runs its polls through a mobile phone app called Apretaste, which is owned by a software developer called Agora Cuba, a nonprofit organization at the same Titusville, Florida address as CubaData. Agora Cuba's executive director is Salvador "Salvi" Pascual, a Cuban-born technology entrepreneur based in Florida who co-founded CubaData with Diaz Espi in 2018. Agora Cuba, like Diario de Cuba and CubaData, has received U.S. government funding. Between 2016 and 2021, NED's document more than $332,000 in grants to Agora Cuba, according to NED's grant listings and tax filings. An NED grant of $44,252 listed for 2021 was equivalent to more than 94 percent of Agora Cuba's reported revenue that year. | | ---|---|--- The National Endowment for Democracy provided $332,198 in documented grants to Agora Cuba between 2016 and 2021 according to NED Form 990 tax filings for , , , and . LAPOP itself has also long relied on U.S. government funding. In October 2024, Vanderbilt a five-year, $12.5 million USAID award to support the project and other surveys. USAID was reportedly supplying. But that funding was cut off in 2025 when Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) dismantled USAID. Notre Dame's Kellogg Institute for International Studies stepped in to help fund half of this year's AmericasBarometer budget, . Vanderbilt University officials contacted by Belly of the Beast and Drop Site did not respond to questions about how they funded the other half. | | ---|---|--- U.S. government funding and institutional ties among the organizations involved in the 2026 AmericasBarometer survey of Cuba. U.S.-Funded Apps The U.S. government has long funded media and communications projects aimed at bringing about regime change in Cuba. Journalist Tracey Eaton more than $218 million in U.S. government disbursements for Cuba "democracy promotion" (also known as "regime change") programs between 2001 and 2021. Roughly $25 million went to media and information projects, of which NED managed $15.6 million. Some programs have clearly stated their intentions. For example, a 2019 USAID initiative for projects that would "dispel the myths about the successes of the Cuban Revolution," including its education and healthcare systems. Other programs were covert. One of the most notorious was ZunZuneo, a text-message network modeled on Twitter that launched in Cuba in 2010 thanks to $1.7 million in funding from USAID. ZunZuneo's plan was to attract subscribers with sports, music, and weather updates, and then introduce political content that could spark anti-government protests, according to documents in 2014. More than 40,000 Cubans used the network without knowing the U.S. government was behind it. The revelations embarrassed USAID and led to Congress grilling its administrator, Rajiv Shah. Sen. Patrick Leahy (D-Vt.), who chaired the subcommittee overseeing the agency's funding, "dumb, dumb, dumb." "We are the only ones who have this information about Cuban people, who also want to socialize," he said. The app has been used, which is . He said he did not participate in the survey's design, implementation, or analysis, and that his own role was "exclusively institutional." He did not specify what that meant. He said NED and NDI supported separate, earlier research conducted by CubaData, but did not finance LAPOP's Cuba poll. Pascual did not respond to requests for comment. Respondents could make only one choice. Seventy-four percent chose the Cuban government. Sixteen percent chose the U.S. government. | | ---|---|--- Another question allowed respondents to assign blame to multiple actors. More than 45% attributed the crisis to U.S. sanctions or policies, either entirely or in part. | | ---|---|--- The second question was left out of the Pulse of Democracy report. Instead, the report's Cuba chapter leads with the heading "Blame Attribution Is Directed at the Cuban Regime, Not the U.S.," citing the 74% figure. Julia Jordan, Vanderbilt's spokesperson, told Belly of the Beast and Drop Site the findings should be interpreted together. Asked why the second question was not included in the report, she said the Cuba chapter presents only a "small number" of results and that the public data "allow researchers and journalists to examine additional questions." It's not clear that any did. Media outlets** and foreign policy journals covering the poll cited only the first question. Polling experts questioned the survey's methodology and how the results were presented. "A question that forces a single choice and one that allows shared responsibility captures different things," said Mariano Torcal, deputy director of the Research and Expertise Center for Survey Methodology (RECSM) in Barcelona, Spain. "Readers are better served by seeing both [questions] and understanding how each was asked." Stanford professor Jon Krosnick, who specializes in studying survey methodology, found flaws in both questions--one failed to define the crisis; the other steered people toward a narrow set of explanations. "Honestly, I wouldn't put much stock in either one," he said. A Nationally Representative Poll? The Pulse of Democracy report describes the poll as "a rare window into how Cubans understand the country's current crisis, who they hold responsible, and what they see as the country's most urgent priorities." The report omitted a key detail disclosed in LAPOP's : respondents were drawn from a pool of CubaData users who had registered through the Apretaste app. The app can be downloaded on Android devices, but iPhone users must use a VPN to access it; Apple's app store geoblocks users physically located in Cuba to avoid violating U.S. sanctions. Apretaste is not widely known on the island--Belly of the Beast and Drop Site asked more than three dozen Cubans if they had heard of it and only one said they had (although they had not downloaded or used it). | | ---|---|--- Screenshots of the Apretaste app. The app offers a kitchen sink of features, including daily prayers and jokes, a dating service, and news (most of the featured media outlets are openly opposed to the Cuban government, and several are U.S.-government funded). Apretaste also offers a chance to win cash prizes in raffles by participating in surveys. We entered false information about our age, marital status, race, and education level in the most recent survey--about the importance of pets in everyday life. There was no process to verify our identity. Vanderbilt spokesperson Julia Jordan said CubaData screened for bots or "heavy multi-device usage" and its "communication and data transfer are protected by advanced encryption." She did not respond to questions about how respondents' age and residence were verified or whether duplicate submissions could be identified. In exchange for completing the survey, we received virtual credits usable for raffle entries. Winnings accumulate in a separate dollar-denominated balance. Apretaste says users can as mobile phone credit with Cubacel, Cuba's state-owned mobile service, or as USDT, a cryptocurrency pegged to the U.S. dollar, once they reach its minimum payout threshold. The app displayed more than 100 users who had won raffles for participating in the AmericasBarometer survey. Each user's profile and information--including name, age, race, and city of residence--was visible. body:
#

Peter —
Here’s the truth: We’re running on empty.
While we are still waiting for every vote to be counted, we are starting to run out of resources.
I am so grateful to have had your support throughout this campaign. Seriously.
We started with $0 in our bank account, and we built this movement from the ground up without a dime from the greedy corporations hurting all of us. And we spent almost everything we had to win – and we will.
So we need your help again to keep us afloat while we fight to count every vote and power through until this race is certified. We can’t afford to fall short when Donald Trump and the entire DC establishment are working to overturn the results of our election and undo the will of Alaskans if I win.
I am so proud that this campaign is fueled by working people. But that does mean we have to keep asking for your support until this race is officially over.
I wouldn’t ask if it wasn’t so important. So please Peter:

Mary

Peter —

Now that we’re past the midterm elections, we thought it might be a good
time to reintroduce ourselves!

COURIER is an independent, reader-funded newsroom covering politics across
20 states and a national bureau. We reach millions of Americans every day
in the same feeds where right-wing lies spread fastest.

We don't have a billionaire owner. We don't take corporate marching
orders. And we don't hide any of our local reporting behind paywalls,
because when real news gets locked away, right-wing propaganda fills the
gap.

But while this election cycle may be over, our work at COURIER never ends
on Election Day.

With new majorities taking power in Congress and statehouses across the
country, COURIER’s year-round, on-the-ground reporting is more important
than ever if we are going to hold officials accountable to the people who
just elected them.

Over the next several weeks, we would love to share some of our most
insightful and impactful reporting with you, as well as opportunities to
get more involved and support this mission.

If that sounds good to you, let us know by clicking here to make sure you
continue receiving our emails:

Friend, There are so many exciting updates from this election:
* **We saw a huge increase in voter turnout in my district.** For example, 28% more people voted in Dearborn and Dearborn Heights this year than the last midterm election in 2022. Michigan’s percentage of voter turnout was the 4th highest in the country.1
* **Relatedly, most of the people we endorsed inside and outside Michigan won**. In addition to Democratic majorities, we secured a record number of _progressives_ in power.
* **Important ballot measures passed** , including measures to block data centers, to get money out of politics in Michigan and Montana, and to protect LGBTQ+ rights in Vermont and Virginia. Voters protected abortion rights in Missouri, Virginia, and Nevada.
* **Transgender candidates (including nonbinary people) won** their elections and reelections across the country, even in states like Alabama, Iowa, and Kansas. At least 48 openly trans people will be in public office next year — including Joanna Whaley, the first openly trans person elected to Michigan’s state legislature.

**We won a lot! But that doesn’t mean that our work is over.** For example, anti-trans ballot measures passed in four states (though organizations, schools, and elected officials are fighting back). And some Democratic candidates adopted right-wing rhetoric, attacking trans people while campaigning. **The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (run by Democrats in the House of Representatives) even ran an anti-trans ad in South Carolina.** 2 Unacceptable! **This week is Trans Awareness Week** , a time to celebrate trans people and renew the fight for trans rights and lives. Anti-trans, anti-Muslim, and anti-Black rhetoric and policies have been on the rise, endangering our communities. **We need to push Democrats to firmly push back against hate and fight for**** _all_****marginalized people.** [**Will you chip in for the fight ahead, so together we can build on this momentum and push Democrats in power to enact a progressive agenda that will change people’s lives for the better?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvx7QQDKFwkQMBaEt-a9W1TFfkQ_xrRrxYC0yKeAe5Gkz_s-Bgm6EocadTxm_T3Lx0YeEvfp5eHE4j0F5SMfB1jJQpkI3jg3aZjAzteqrxvcB-eAhNPfOzji8tKauVT8WUncjMoW-GapdGMfrQbBiAUZVkuc67KgqfsaWy1EjMxDDUFdtVVonY25wEvLfPejxbhuop7QxQWIRi40xq5erjAHSpyY1EC_aIN5RwQER1qxSktIo7g08FmOYsSQ0idX-CUhhlanHC6yRrgG5X8dVuaGko7yjaUP7C7CA42aD_EI-hO9cHscdbY6VUl1AMknqwEHvE6ADb4Att3Lvi5rdzOtQATxGsaFBLLI2byMbaOQqY2m1TRxrnS3u6uXTsEEaE/4vt/EoSn5yJCR-2rnpeEgmNC0w/h1/h001.hO0-yYvvDmdgeJRCxt0qglGniS8VT20xW6IITtktIUQ) | [CHIP IN TO PUSH FOR TRANSFORMATIVE CHANGE](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvx7QQDKFwkQMBaEt-a9W1TFfkQ_xrRrxYC0yKeAe5Gkz_s-Bgm6EocadTxm_T3Lx3W8y2zxdtncBGkyH8oxgISdZpIUL4zEPA5wjJ4BLhL2Sonzxb6KXGNyHGLWq__vM2ZfHKZDYtAWNdpzV_u3rcVYmyWCcA15koLN2k-nj5DPlCwuhSa5rrsPwt7QMCxcVzqDnc5FpLnTFJOQbD4KPEBofLfKOR-1wv1723klM_jvZyRAH6GWj_UHj3P_0uWMtQ3oBbCqJzZzTdzYRiK8G9D1mjanmLC0QroxFYtqhcB5F51zqa_OVQh38YwdS7Y-l465iar6u44b8J61LC8PkubSk7_Wsz6jsyZmJlEaxq02AxvVJtg7iDcMSMJiiJdDBc/4vt/EoSn5yJCR-2rnpeEgmNC0w/h2/h001.-2y5RuJYXdMbbpyVtt-EeP7HSBM4HrIAaMnt_MgWOiI)

Thank you. We have a real opportunity to protect our loved ones and neighbors, reverse Trump’s harms, and expand our rights.
We have the chance for a new Reconstruction period, like the one 150 years ago where Black people gained a huge number of seats in the U.S. Congress — which was the last time a Black person represented Mississippi in the U.S. Senate, until Scott Colom!
Back then, white supremacists pushed back against necessary progress, ending Reconstruction and starting Jim Crow.
**Now, we need to put the work in to make sure this era lasts.**
We need to keep pushing Democrats so we can move beyond the failed, unjust status quo and instead listen to what the American people want.
That means **fighting for a people’s agenda** that includes universal healthcare, reproductive justice, a $25+ minimum wage, an end to U.S. support for the war on Iran and the genocide in Gaza, and more.
Even in heavily gerrymandered states, progressives and democratic socialists came close to winning!
Angie Nixon came within 2 points of beating Florida’s Republican incumbent for U.S. Senate. The people who came out to vote for her in Florida helped flip more than 20 seats blue, in the state legislature and U.S. Congress — even though Florida Republicans just redrew district maps in their favor!
In Oklahoma, N'kiyla Jasmine Thomas — the Native and democratic socialist U.S. Senate candidate — got 40% of the vote! Some Oklahoma residents are saying that she may have won if the districts weren’t rigged for and by Republicans.
We could see even more progressive wins in 2028. But we need to keep up this momentum and deliver results as soon as possible.

I want to acknowledge that this Friday, trans people and allies around the world will mark**Trans Day of Remembrance** , mourning the lives of trans people who died this year due to anti-trans violence.
This year, Metro Detroit lost 16-year-old Jadyn Kimsel. In February, the young musician and artist was asked what kept him going, and he said: “So I can be remembered as a man.”
Heartbreakingly, his family posted an obituary that misgendered him. So his friends wrote about him online, saying: “We will remember him as living as his authentic self.”3
I will not stop fighting for a better world, where trans people can thrive with dignity and live safely as their true selves.
Bentley Hudgins, the first out nonbinary and trans person elected to Georgia’s state legislature (who won with 92% of the vote), released a video after the election saying:
> “ _There is so much that we can do now in Georgia [after flipping the state legislature and statewide seats]. We can save lives... The future is worth fighting for, and we belong here. We belong in this country. I can't wait to see what we do next.”_ 4
Trans folks, you matter and you belong here.
In love and solidarity,
Rashida

enforcement threat

Minority Leader
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
joined on the leadership team by Sens. Byron Pelton, Janice Rich,
Scott Bright and Barbara Kirkmeyer; a gray wolf, #2516, died in Utah,
bringing the reintroduction death toll to 20
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
including five shot by Colorado Parks and Wildlife this year for
killing livestock; and XX-XY Athletics and Born Again Used Books asked
the 10th Circuit to shield them from Colorado’s anti-discrimination
law
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
on pronouns and names, while the state says they face no credible
threat of enforcement.

🇺🇸 ON THE NATIONAL STAGE... A faulty 25-year-old router at an
FAA site in El Dorado, Arkansas, was traced as the cause of Friday’s
nationwide flight grounding
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
Democrats gained at least 12 state legislative chambers and five
governorships, yet voters approved all six statewide tough-on-crime
ballot measures
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and a Buckley Institute survey found 44.6% of college students say
violence can be justified to stop hate speech
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

🗣️ COMMENTARY SPOTLIGHT... Wayne Laugesen writes that nearly one
in three young men has chatted with an AI romantic partner
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
as the U.S. fertility rate hits a record low, urging a return to
marriage; Derek Van Why argues for stewardship over activism
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and Vanessa Rutledge argues Colorado Springs’ delay of the Project
Taurus data center is part of a pattern of local delays sending jobs
and investment out of state
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

FREE SPEECH FIGHT: STATE TELLS 10TH CIRCUIT BUSINESSES FACE NO REAL
ENFORCEMENT THREAT
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

A Denver athletic apparel company and a Colorado Springs Christian
bookstore took their free speech fight to a federal appeals court
Monday, asking it to shield them from Colorado’s anti-discrimination
law while the case goes forward.

The state’s answer was that they face no credible threat of
enforcement. The three-judge panel of the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of
Appeals has to decide whether the businesses face a real enough threat
of enforcement to ask for a preliminary injunction in the first place.

A federal judge in Denver has already answered that question two
different ways. In March, Chief U.S. District Judge Regina M.
Rodriguez ruled they hadn’t shown a credible threat. In September,
she found they had.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

44.6% OF COLLEGE STUDENTS JUSTIFY VIOLENCE TO STOP HATE SPEECH, POLL
FINDS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_A year after Charlie Kirk’s assassination on a college campus,
nearly half of surveyed college students said violence can be
justified to stop hate speech, with the share climbing sharply since
2017._

*
SUPPORT FOR VIOLENCE HAS RISEN SHARPLY SINCE 2017: The Buckley
Institute survey found 44.6% of college students agreed violence can
be justified to stop hate speech, up from under 30% in 2017, even as
two-thirds of students correctly said hate speech is still protected
under the First Amendment.

*
A SHARP IDEOLOGICAL DIVIDE: A majority of liberal students agreed
violence can be justified, compared to fewer than a third of
conservatives, and liberal students were also most likely to say
shouting down a speaker is sometimes appropriate.

*
CLASSROOM INTIMIDATION TRACKS WITH SUPPORT FOR VIOLENCE: Students who
said they’d avoid a class taught by a professor they disagreed with
were more than twice as likely to justify violence (64%) as those who
wouldn’t avoid it (29%), while at Utah Valley University, where Kirk
was killed, the share saying violence is “never” acceptable jumped
from 81% to 95% after his death.

and culture throughout the state of Colorado. The only way we can

DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️

WHY I CHOOSE STEWARDSHIP, NOT ACTIVISM
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY DEREK VAN WHY | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 16

_One great, existential threat is conditioned into every schoolchild
in America: environmental collapse. The globe is warming, and the
climate is changing, but the narrative lacks any sense of agency._

__

THE DETERMINATION WEAPON: CHRISTIANS, WHAT BIG TEETH WE HAVE!
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 15

_Little Red Riding Hood went to Grandma’s house and found a wolf in
her bed. He had Grandma’s clothes, Grandma’s place in the house,
and enough manners to call her “my dear.” Then he opened his
mouth, and all hell broke loose. I thought about those teeth when my
good friend Heidi Ganahl ran for governor of Colorado in 2022._
__

JEFFCO 5A FLIPS TO PASSING BY 327 VOTES AND LANDS INSIDE RECOUNT RANGE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | NOVEMBER 13

_For more than a week, Jeffco Public Schools’ $73 million tax
increase was losing. District leaders had already said what that would
mean. On the evening of Wednesday, Nov. 4, the day after the election,
interim Superintendent Rob Stein and Board of Education President
Michelle Applegate put out a statement on the results, according to
Chalkbeat Colorado._
__

subject: I’m suing OpenAI. Here’s what you need to know →
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ROB BONTA FOR CALIFORNIA ATTORNEY GENERAL 2026 FPPC ID #145642**
body:
It’s not too much to ask that this technology be developed safely. | | | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143617416/660810634/-95927501?refcode=261117em_rb_openai-lawsuit&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYzRiZDliMy1jY2UyLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=feA9hMPQv6wSsRcLGJbdXvdIBeePHoXRVvq8QcnmxHk=&emci=68cad6ad-cce2-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=ac4bd9b3-cce2-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=33430436)
---
I've just filed a lawsuit against OpenAI for failing to control its AI models, disregarding public safety, and knowingly misleading the public about the potential dangers of its product. The artificial intelligence technology OpenAI is developing may be new, but California’s laws against business practices that put public safety at risk and deceive consumers are not — and they apply to every company, no matter how powerful it is or how quickly it wants to move. Let me be clear: I believe in the technological and economic power of AI. I believe it could lead to some of the most incredible improvements in the history of humankind. But companies can — and must — protect people while harnessing its potential. _It is simply not too much to ask that as we advance this technology, it be done safely. OpenAI has a moral _and legal_ obligation to keep public safety at the forefront, and it fell short of that obligation when it failed to properly secure and monitor the testing of its AI models._ Earlier this year my office began a formal investigation into a security incident involving OpenAI and Hugging Face. OpenAI itself admitted that it was aware of 80 — eighty! — incidents involving loss of control and access to third-party networks and websites. But when we asked for the information we needed to investigate those incidents, OpenAI refused. Here’s what we do know: → We know these failures were the predictable results of an internal culture that prioritizes rapid growth over safety and accountability — or put another way, that prioritizes profit over people. → We know there were warning signs, and that OpenAI disregarded them. → We know that despite assuring the public that its testing was being done under constant oversight, it wasn’t even OpenAI that discovered it had lost control of its agents — it was Hugging Face. → And we know that OpenAI is violating California law and disregarding public safety. **That’s why we’re suing.**
---
California is proud to be the innovation capital of the nation and the world, and as Attorney General, I will continue to fight for innovation that follows the law and keeps the public safe — full stop. —Rob
---

| | Friend, Anyone who’s spent time on the water in Hampton Roads knows that the tide always turns. Four years ago, I lost this seat. I didn’t second-guess the fight then, and I’m glad I didn’t. **On November 3rd, the tide turned.** The people of Hampton Roads sent me back to Congress. And we weren’t alone. Across the country, voters delivered a blue wave that flipped the House with what’s on track to be the largest Democratic majority in decades. Democrats flipped Senate seats in places like Kansas, Texas, and Ohio to take back that chamber too. All cycle, I told you Democrats needed to flip just three House seats to take back the majority. We blew right past that number, and VA-02 was one of the seats that got us there. I’m proud of that. # **[Nvidia smashes $115.8B quarter in first earnings call after Jensen exit](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, as interim CEO Colette Kress hosted her first earnings call days after Jensen Huang's resignation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

**Revenue tops expectations:** Results exceeded analyst forecasts near $109 billion, with Data Center sales at $107.6 billion, up 110% year over year and 21% from the prior quarter.
**Margins and earnings hold:** GAAP gross margin reached 74.8% and non-GAAP 74.9%, while diluted EPS came in at $2.70 GAAP and $2.68 non-GAAP.
**Vera Rubin ships rapidly:** The company began shipping Vera Rubin NVL72, calling it the fastest product ramp in its history, with racks at CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle and Nebius.
**Guidance points to $130 billion:** Fourth-quarter revenue is expected at $130 billion plus or minus 3%, with no China Data Center compute assumed; a $0.25 dividend is set for December 23.

# [Google flags first AI-only cyberattack amid US tech outages](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Google **[said that](https://substack.com/redirect/fe9ed866-a6ea-41e1-947a-48a439c326f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Russian-speaking operators used an AI agent to fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation **[with no human in the loop,](https://substack.com/redirect/34ca2f3b-9161-46a3-9d5f-415c3e816ec8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as technical failures grounded flights, **[froze banking](https://substack.com/redirect/cba3e1c0-9807-423a-b21f-b581dba6300b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , and knocked out **[Microsoft](https://substack.com/redirect/cba3e1c0-9807-423a-b21f-b581dba6300b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[Apple](https://substack.com/redirect/f6a9d77a-7445-4dbb-af47-50a27e22c870?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** services.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Microsoft outage spans continents:** Outlook and Teams failed for about 36 hours starting Nov. 12 across more than 70 countries after a network capacity upgrade, with Microsoft calling it a technical issue unrelated to cyber or AI.
* **FAA grounds flights nationally:** A nationwide ground stop lasting more than four hours on Nov. 13 stemmed from outdated air-traffic equipment and copper upgrades, rippling into multi-day airline disruptions.
* **Banking hit by software bug:** JPMorgan Chase reported a temporary issue from a software bug in on-premise hardware on Nov. 16, stating there was no evidence it was cyber-related, with knock-on effects for some Zelle and other-bank transactions.
* **Apple services slow or unavailable:** **[Thousands of Downdetector reports](https://substack.com/redirect/8f87cb03-28ff-47ff-87e3-83ede7209a7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** hit Apple Pay, the App Store, iCloud (**[beginning 11:45 a.m. EST](https://substack.com/redirect/f6a9d77a-7445-4dbb-af47-50a27e22c870?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**), and Apple Support on Nov. 17; Apple confirmed issues with iCloud Account & Sign In and AppleCare on Device for all users, later attributing the problems to an internal update

# [FBI: ARTEX AI breaches critical systems in under 3 hours](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The FBI issued a FLASH advisory Monday on hackers weaponizing the open-source ARTEX AI framework since at least August to **[automate multi-stage intrusions](https://substack.com/redirect/fc031da4-0662-49fa-92a6-5a0788ccb3ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** against energy, manufacturing, telecom and other targets, with some reaching privileged access in under three hours.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Framework lowers attack barrier:** ARTEX, released on GitHub in July by developer Autumn-27 and later removed, connects to models including DeepSeek Flash and translates natural-language goals into automated reconnaissance, exploitation and exfiltration with minimal human input.
* **Exposed consoles exceed 1,600:** Researchers found more than 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX console instances in early November, with the tool remaining available via forks, archives and a commercial version after the original repository came down in October.
* **Supply-chain hits reach thousands:** Campaigns against South Korean financial institutions stole personal data on about 67,000 people, while a ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise gave access to more than 2,250 downstream tenants.
* **FBI urges surface reduction:** The advisory recommends inventorying internet-facing apps, enforcing least privilege, monitoring for sequential lookups and preserving evidence, noting ARTEX compresses detection windows through high-volume noisy traffic.

* * *
# [November outages hit Microsoft, FAA and JPMorgan in days](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A **[string of technical failures](https://substack.com/redirect/05f33663-ccbd-45a5-b791-41ad61fc341d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in mid-November disrupted Microsoft tools for 36 hours across more than 70 countries, triggered a multi-hour FAA ground stop, and locked thousands of customers out of major bank online services.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Microsoft cites network upgrade:** Outlook and Teams stopped working starting Nov. 12 after an issue during a network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent change; Microsoft said the problem was technical and unrelated to cyber or AI.
* **FAA stop lasts over four hours:** The Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop stemmed from outdated air-traffic communications equipment and copper cable upgrades, with ripple effects lasting several days as airlines rebooked passengers.
* **JPMorgan blames software bug:** On Nov. 16 thousands of customers at several major institutions reported online banking problems tied to a temporary software bug in on-premise hardware systems at JPMorgan Chase, which found no evidence it was cyber-related.
* **Aging infrastructure highlighted:** The FAA incident became a political headache for the Trump administration and underscored vulnerabilities in the nation's aging telecommunications systems.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/af513983-8976-4105-a5dc-50483da0e30f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [SpaceX $40B Nvidia chip debt hits market this week](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A portion of SpaceX's $40 billion debt financing for Nvidia AI chips **[may begin selling as soon as this week](https://substack.com/redirect/ad442ce6-caf7-431e-a857-0e28d017dd70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ad442ce6-caf7-431e-a857-0e28d017dd70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)through an Apollo-backed special purpose vehicle that keeps the obligation off the company's balance sheet.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **SPV issues asset-backed securities:** Atlas SP, managed by Apollo, will buy the Nvidia chips and issue the securities, with Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management underwriting the deal.
* **Off-balance-sheet structure preserved:** The arrangement is designed to avoid adding the debt directly to SpaceX's books while funding the AI chip purchases.
* **Timing targets this week:** The article, published Tuesday, said a portion of the financing could start being sold as soon as this week.
* **IG ratings maintained:** The structure helps SpaceX preserve its investment-grade ratings while scaling AI compute.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/af513983-8976-4105-a5dc-50483da0e30f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [JPMorgan CFO Barnum steps down as Dimon succession advances](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Longtime JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum **[will step down next year after first-quarter earnings](https://substack.com/redirect/f18edc56-9623-4446-8de1-2bfa0d7cecea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in April and become vice chair through early 2028, with Bregje de Best succeeding him as part of broader preparations for CEO Jamie Dimon's eventual exit.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Barnum requested the move:** Dimon said Barnum, who has served as CFO since 2021, requested the transition after six years in the role.
* **De Best takes the seat:** The 43-year-old de Best, currently CFO of the commercial and investment bank and a JPMorgan employee since 2006, will become group CFO.
* **Dimon tenure context set:** Dimon is expected to remain CEO for three more years; the announcement follows recent leadership changes including Marianne Lake's retirement and the elevation of Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to co-presidents.
* **Tenure above average:** Barnum's six-year stint slightly exceeds the 4.8-year average for CFOs at S&P 500 companies.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/af513983-8976-4105-a5dc-50483da0e30f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [Cisco CEO: AI industry is bigger than one person after Huang exit](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins **[said the AI industry is bigger than any single individual,](https://substack.com/redirect/c24d436d-3095-49e2-9cd2-dad4df678597?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/c24d436d-3095-49e2-9cd2-dad4df678597?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)pointing to 42,000 people at Nvidia and deep talent across hyperscalers and accelerator companies amid speculation over Jensen Huang's future.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bbba64a3-943e-4466-a5de-0f6cb4a291fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Broad intellect across sector:** Robbins stated there are smart people at Nvidia, other accelerator companies, hyperscalers and networking firms building the technology.
* **Not concerned about continuity:** He added he is not all that concerned about the future of tech because of the distributed base of expertise.
* **Context of leadership questions:** The comments came as discussion continued around Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's resignation amid personal scandals.
* **Scale underscores resilience:** Robbins highlighted Nvidia's 42,000-person workforce as evidence the industry does not rest on one person.

name: Becca Balint
subject: I've been waiting FOUR YEARS for this.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Becca Balint for Vermont**
body:
Hope you're ready, because I sure am! | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143618171/660813171/-785282667?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYjM5N2M4OS1kMWUyLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=StCUsNdsPdc23mVrBAhMj2C0NBmla4foWGSWaRrbUGk=)
---
Peter, I've been thinking a lot about something lately. **Washington has gotten awfully good at telling the American people what they CAN'T have.** Can't afford to expand healthcare. Can't make housing more affordable. Can't ask billionaires and giant corporations to pay their fair share. Can't possibly find the political will to take on the special interests pulling the strings. **Funny how there's always an excuse when working families need something, but somehow Washington manages to find a way when the wealthy and well-connected come calling.** _Well, I'm tired of the excuses. And I have a feeling you are, too._ Last week, I asked you what your biggest priorities were for the new Congress. What you wanted us to fight for. What changes you were hoping to see. And I want to tell you something. **I'm taking this responsibility VERY seriously.** Because for the first time since I was elected, Democrats are preparing to take the House majority. And after four years of watching Republicans bend over backward for Donald Trump, give away Congress's power, and put corporate interests ahead of everyday Americans, we've got some serious work to do. **And I don't intend to waste a single minute of this opportunity.** Here's something I believe with every fiber of my being: **The power we hold in Congress belongs to the PEOPLE.** It belongs to the parent working two jobs and still struggling to pay rent. The senior choosing between groceries and prescription drugs. The young person wondering whether they'll ever be able to afford a home. **It belongs to YOU.** And somewhere along the way, too many people in Washington seem to have forgotten that. They've gotten comfortable letting corporations write the rules, billionaires buy influence, and politicians treat public office like their own personal investment portfolio. **I mean, for crying out loud, can we PLEASE start by banning members of Congress from trading stocks?** That seems like a pretty reasonable place to start! And while we're at it, let's take on the corporate monopolies driving up costs, fight to make healthcare affordable, protect our democracy, and make sure Congress actually does its job holding those in power accountable. **Because the American people gave us an opportunity to change the direction of this country. And we owe it to them to DELIVER.** Now, I know what you're probably thinking. _Becca, that sounds like a pretty ambitious to-do list._ **You're darn right it is! But I didn't run for Congress because I thought the work would be easy. I ran because I believe deeply in what government can accomplish when we have the courage to stand up for people.** And after four years in the minority, you better believe I've got some pent-up energy. **So,** Peter**, I want to ask you one more thing:** **Are you ready to help us make the most of this moment?** **[YES, BECCA! LET'S GET TO WORK!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143618173/660813173/-1195217103?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYjM5N2M4OS1kMWUyLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=StCUsNdsPdc23mVrBAhMj2C0NBmla4foWGSWaRrbUGk=)** I know we're going to face resistance. I know the corporate lobbyists aren't going to suddenly pack up their bags and head home. And I know Donald Trump isn't going to make any of this easy.
