clean_body: Hope you're ready, because I sure am! | = Peter, I've been thinking a lot about something lately. Washington has gotten awfully good at telling the American people what they CAN'T have. Can't afford to expand healthcare. Can't make housing more affordable. Can't ask billionaires and giant corporations to pay their fair share. Can't possibly find the political will to take on the special interests pulling the strings. Funny how there's always an excuse when working families need something, but somehow Washington manages to find a way when the wealthy and well-connected come calling. Well, I'm tired of the excuses. And I have a feeling you are, too. Last week, I asked you what your biggest priorities were for the new Congress. What you wanted us to fight for. What changes you were hoping to see. And I want to tell you something. I'm taking this responsibility VERY seriously. Because for the first time since I was elected, Democrats are preparing to take the House majority. And after four years of watching Republicans bend over backward for Donald Trump, give away Congress's power, and put corporate interests ahead of everyday Americans, we've got some serious work to do. And I don't intend to waste a single minute of this opportunity. Here's something I believe with every fiber of my being: The power we hold in Congress belongs to the PEOPLE. It belongs to the parent working two jobs and still struggling to pay rent. The senior choosing between groceries and prescription drugs. The young person wondering whether they'll ever be able to afford a home. It belongs to YOU. And somewhere along the way, too many people in Washington seem to have forgotten that. They've gotten comfortable letting corporations write the rules, billionaires buy influence, and politicians treat public office like their own personal investment portfolio. I mean, for crying out loud, can we PLEASE start by banning members of Congress from trading stocks? That seems like a pretty reasonable place to start! And while we're at it, let's take on the corporate monopolies driving up costs, fight to make healthcare affordable, protect our democracy, and make sure Congress actually does its job holding those in power accountable. Because the American people gave us an opportunity to change the direction of this country. And we owe it to them to DELIVER. Now, I know what you're probably thinking. Becca, that sounds like a pretty ambitious to-do list. You're darn right it is! But I didn't run for Congress because I thought the work would be easy. I ran because I believe deeply in what government can accomplish when we have the courage to stand up for people. And after four years in the minority, you better believe I've got some pent-up energy. So, Peter, I want to ask you one more thing: Are you ready to help us make the most of this moment? = I know we're going to face resistance. I know the corporate lobbyists aren't going to suddenly pack up their bags and head home. And I know Donald Trump isn't going to make any of this easy. But I also know what happens when ordinary people come together, refuse to give up, and demand something better. We just saw it happen at the ballot box. Now comes the part where we turn all that hope into action. And I am so, SO ready to get to work for you. subject: Are you upset about 2026?
body:
Non-citizens on the rolls, ballots counted days late, machines that won't work. We can fix this

I'll be honest with you. I'm frustrated with how the 2026 midterms turned out, and if you're reading this, I'd guess you are too.Look at what we watched happen this cycle. On Election Day, ballot scanners failed across Westchester County, **New York** , in one of the closest House races in the country, held by a Republican incumbent, and poll workers stuffed completed ballots into emergency bags saying they would just be counted later. In **California** , federal officials flagged roughly 20,000 likely non-citizens who had been mailed ballots, and an appeals court let the state count them anyway.**New Jersey** admitted it found 6,600 non-citizens on its own voter rolls. And in one **California** county, election staff opened a locked drop box and found nearly 600 sealed ballots that had sat there uncounted for five months after the election was certified.On top of all that, the Supreme Court ruled this summer that 14 states and D.C. can keep counting mail ballots that arrive after Election Day. **_Election Day is supposed to mean one day._** After a night like this, it's tempting to tune out and wait for things to cool down. I _understand that feeling._ But these problems don't fix themselves between elections. If we look away now, every one of them will be bigger in 2028, and liberals will do everything they can to steal the presidential election. _**[If you're upset about how 2026 turned out and you want to make sure 2028 is decided by honest votes, I need your help right now.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkTmP2zAQhX8N1UkQD10FiwCGgRQbBEiRkhiTI3sQiWR4eOF_HzBXv80U73t4c31_M29AB_n7FzhRU84mZQMJX6HWmLHALdQiRjGbVnrOe74YsIWeaBR0Tk-Cr_vaoebLprZJrFJ1D41OWYVcLbvblZwnt9pln7kS-2211m4d6ZbHOV-EGEexDXKcuZtufJajQ7HtTI01Oig4kM_kMNsQYgwHFbJ5COneHfpRSsxMfmLiysQ1o60Jh3fyCd1gw9k0eGKPB9pCwfcOXkxcAfsYcvmvgv3J5LWW05zoqJ5MXvAEOpiYm5hDTRaZvDwgOcg_TPP_QRbOCHT3TF4yOuPDs8FKmVrw74v9cwZf0BcmL5-_feXTumzqLymYWscuaRff6TgozwtT471N0Jboyse_8tTiVwAAAP__2nedUQ)**_

I serve on the board of **Save Election Day**. We're a team of volunteer election lawyers who have worked Election Days, early voting, and recounts, so we've seen these problems up close. We're a 501(c)4 non-profit founded for one purpose: **to carry President Trump 's election reforms into the states and turn them into law.**Here's why the states matter. Washington, D.C. keeps introducing election bills that stall, and even when Congress acts, elections are still run under state law. So we write the bills, push them through statehouses, and take the fight straight to voters with ballot measures where legislatures won't move. Our goals are simple:
---
* Photo voter ID for every voter
* One national Election Day, with results on Election Night
* No more ballots counted days after the polls close
* Shorter mail-in and early voting windows
* Only American citizens voting in American elections

---

Across the country, Democratic pro-choice women flipped seats, shattered expectations, and made history — and supporters like you helped make it possible. But the blue wave didn't happen overnight. It took years of organizing, early investments, and a millions-strong community of people committed to electing Democratic pro-choice women. Now, we're asking you to help us grow that community even bigger. Will you forward this email to TWO friends who might want to become official 2027 EMILYs List members and help build the next blue wave? And to celebrate this year's historic victories, everyone who joins or renews during our Early Bird Membership Drive will receive an exclusive, limited-edition Blue Wave membership card in the mail! | | | That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer -- a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow officers moved in.The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be seriously injured -- maybe even killed.So my husband made a split-second decision. He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too late.Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit. But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible that someone died.But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers safe.And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his own. He was the one who joined a violent street gang...He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general. **You see, Letitia James is bankrolled by George Soros. And she’s filled her office with prosecutors who hate cops as much as she does.** And five months after that fateful day......she charged Erik with Manslaughter.She didn’t just charge Erik. She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case into a media circus.They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant parents.What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle? Things only got worse at the trial.But not only did the judge find Erik guilty......he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a “general deterrent” to other police officers!This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about “deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in this day and age.But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream for Erik. He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the area.Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad to our three children.Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing I’ve ever done.Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he go to jail?After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in awful conditions.He spent his days in solitary confinement in a dark, filthy cell with blood all over the walls.**This is how Letitia James and Judge Guy Mitchell repaid my husband for 15 years of protecting his neighborhood.** It’s disgusting.It’s unjust.And it’s just plain wrong.Thankfully, Erik’s lawyers told us he has a good chance at an appeal. And after we filed the appeal, the court set Erik free on bond.But as you know, the appeals process is incredibly expensive.I had almost given up hope.But thank the Lord, Erik is a godly man. Through it all, his faith has never wavered -- not once.On his way home from prison, he stopped at our local church to pray and ask God for help. clean_body: You’ve heard about Erik on the news. He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer. | | | | Dear Friend,I know you and I have never met. But I’m writing to you today because I’m desperate. | | | This is Erik, me, and our three children in the family photo.I wish I didn’t have to blur our faces. But with the death threats we’ve been getting, I couldn’t afford to take any chances.I should explain...You’ve heard about Erik on the news.He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer who was speeding a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk. | | | | | That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer -- a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow officers moved in.The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be seriously injured -- maybe even killed.So my husband made a split-second decision. He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too late.Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit. But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible that someone died.But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers safe.And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his own. He was the one who joined a violent street gang...He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general. You see, Letitia James is bankrolled by George Soros. And she’s filled her office with prosecutors who hate cops as much as she does. And five months after that fateful day......she charged Erik with Manslaughter.She didn’t just charge Erik. She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case into a media circus.They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant parents.What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle? Things only got worse at the trial.But not only did the judge find Erik guilty......he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a “general deterrent” to other police officers!This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about “deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in this day and age.But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream for Erik. He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the area.Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad to our three children.Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing I’ve ever done.Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he go to jail?After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in awful conditions.He spent his days in solitary confinement in a dark, filthy cell with blood all over the walls.This is how Letitia James and Judge Guy Mitchell repaid my husband for 15 years of protecting his neighborhood. It’s disgusting.It’s unjust.And it’s just plain wrong.Thankfully, Erik’s lawyers told us he has a good chance at an appeal. And after we filed the appeal, the court set Erik free on bond.But as you know, the appeals process is incredibly expensive.I had almost given up hope.But thank the Lord, Erik is a godly man. Through it all, his faith has never wavered -- not once.On his way home from prison, he stopped at our local church to pray and ask God for help. You know that LELDF helps innocent law enforcement officers -- and their families -- fight for justice when there’s nowhere else to turn. Thanks to kind-hearted people like you, they get these officers the lawyers and expert witnesses they need to fight back against activist prosecutors and judges......and win.Friend, you’ve already read my email this far, so I’m going to come right out and ask: I know it’s strange to ask for your support in the very first email I’ve ever written you.But we have nowhere else to turn.Erik and I come from working-class families.We’re not wealthy.And with Erik being found guilty, we lost his salary and our medical benefits. We’re barely getting by as it is. because LELDF is a nonprofit, your gift is tax-deductible too.But whatever God is prompting you to give, please act quickly.Erik’s legal team needs to be working around the clock on this appeal.Because if we don’t fight this injustice, Erik will be imprisoned. And you know how police officers are treated in prison. And when you access the secure donation page, you’ll see there is a box where you can type a message— If you’re a believer like Erik, maybe you could write a short prayer. I know it will mean the world to him. Friend, for the past three years Erik told me something over and over again: “It’s not about the hardships. It’s about the people God sends into your life during difficult times to help you.” I pray that today you’ll be one of those people God uses to help our family.Thank you, and God bless you.Sincerely, Cynthia Duran P.S. My husband doesn’t deserve this. He’s a decorated police officer who spent his entire career serving and protecting his city. That day in the park, he saved lives. And for that, Letitia James wants him locked up for NINE YEARS.Please don’t let the cop-haters destroy another good man. | | | | More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. Team,
Big Tech can afford to pay its own bills.
If a corporation wants to build a massive data center in our community, the people who live here deserve answers. What would it mean for our water? Our electricity bills? And how much would taxpayers be expected to cover?
Those decisions should be made in public, with the people affected having a say.
That’s why I support a pause on new data center construction so communities have time to understand the costs and put protections in place. I also support a national ban on data center nondisclosure agreements that keep the public in the dark.
**The companies building these facilities should cover their full costs, protect our water, use clean energy, and meet strong environmental standards.**
I’m taking that fight to Congress. When a corporation asks for special treatment, I’ll be asking what it means for the people who sent me there.
Your support helped us win this seat. Now we have to keep organizing around the commitments we made, including holding powerful corporations accountable.
[**Will you chip in $10, $25, or whatever works for you to help us keep taking on Big Tech and building support for a government that answers to working people?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143619131/660816399/-1502190644?refcode=body&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc4MzkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWM2NjdiNmItZDZlMi1mMTExLTkxZjMtMDAwZDNhNTMzOTc4IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=wkhUyaCsqkh8qINQrigreRK54RlwiFIhU9qeuiT7BS8=)

**November 17, 2026**
October 5, 2026, was the final day to register to vote in Florida's November 3 General Election. It provides an interesting point of comparison.
## The Registration Numbers
Between August 31 and October 5, Florida's active voter rolls increased by **124,371** over 35 days. In the 26 days between October 5 and October 31, they increased by another **133,768**.
That is **9,397 more net growth in nine fewer days.** Another point of interest: the average daily net increase was approximately 3,553 before the deadline and 5,145 afterward--about 45% higher in the shorter, post-deadline period.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2e44c49b-e5c0-473d-a8e3-199b82cbe19b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The increase was not confined to one registration category. All four grew during both periods. Democrats recorded the largest numerical increase in each period, while Republican, No Party Affiliation, and minor-party registrations also continued to rise.
Across the full two-month period, Florida's active voter rolls increased by **258,139** , bringing the October 31 total to **13,838,263**.
## Two Important Distinctions
So what does this tell us? There are two important nuances to understand.
**First** , October 31 is a post-deadline snapshot, not the registration count used for the November 3 election. The October 5 deadline established the cutoff for that election. Applications received afterward could be processed for future elections, but did not make those applicants eligible to vote on November 3.
**Second** , these figures represent net changes in active registration, not counts of new registrations. At the statewide level, net change reflects the balance between new voters added and active voters removed, including removals resulting from changes in voter status. At the party-category level, changes in affiliation can also shift totals from one category to another without changing the statewide total. The reports show how the numbers changed, but not every transaction behind those changes.
## The Unanswered Question
What accounts for the faster average daily growth in Florida's active voter rolls after the October 5 registration deadline?
How much of the increase came from new registration applications? How much reflected changes in party affiliation, voter status, or other record adjustments? And why did the four registration categories continue to grow at different rates?
The monthly totals reveal a pattern, but not the activity behind it. To understand what happened, we need to look beyond the net changes and examine the underlying registration activity.
The numbers give us something worth examining. They do not yet give us the explanation.
Registration tells us who is on the rolls. Understanding how those rolls change is another part of understanding our elections.

Folks, it’s Chuck Hubbard. If we haven’t met before, I’m a native of northwestern North Carolina who's spent forty years of my career working in local journalism, and I'm also the Democrat who is currently up by 335 votes against Virginia Foxx, the second most-powerful Republican in the House.
_**This is the closest House race in the entire country, and it could also be one of the most important.**_
As Chair of the Rules Committee, Virginia Foxx directly **blocked the House from voting on Trump’s tariffs and the release of the Epstein files.** When Elon Musk and DOGE ransacked our federal government last year, she stood by and cheered them on. She’s made a name for herself yelling at reporters to shut up and screaming at staff for using the wrong elevator. And for twenty years, she’s stepped on the backs of working people in order to climb the ladder in Washington, DC, all while making millions playing the stock market.
Meanwhile, I spent my career reporting the truth at the local newspaper my grandfather started after WWI. I always made an effort to bring my readers just the facts without any bias. In that same spirit, my team and I are working around the clock to make sure every legal ballot in this race counts, because no matter who they voted for, all of our neighbors deserve to be heard.
For the first time in decades, North Carolina’s Fifth District will be represented by a Democrat. I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work to lower costs and fight corruption in Washington – but Republicans are going to do all they can to ensure this doesn’t happen. They’re going to challenge every single vote.
[**Just 335 votes could end Virginia Foxx’s political career and the decades of nastiness – but this week will be the most critical of the campaign. I need your help now to ensure we have the resources required to defend this seat and make sure our neighbors are heard. Can I count on you to chip in a few dollars today? Even just $5, $10, or $25 can help us and Equal Opportunity Now to defend this seat.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143619711/660818411/-1898432515?refcode=261117_hubbard_335&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiZGRkNWFlZi1kOWUyLWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wvN0xI3TWXVGarVqgltQOB3hGbTV6DawxBYWsu8rTE8=)

Last Friday afternoon, every departing flight in the United States was held on the ground during a nationwide ground stop lasting more than four hours, the longest since September 11, 2001.
By the end of the day, more than 9,100 flights had been canceled and more than 24,500 delayed. Mine was one of them. It was canceled again, and again. After the second cancellation, I stopped waiting for an airline to get me home. I got in a car in Fort Lauderdale and drove 22 hours to Washington, D.C.
I was lucky. I got a car and could drive.
Thousands of travelers were stuck in terminals with no clear answer about when they would get out. I saw a mother of small children breaking down, crying in the corner of the airport. A father of 3, waiting in the rental car pickup line with me, said his wife and kids were exhausted and huddled together upstairs, praying he could book one of the last rental cars to drive to Boston that night... from freaking Florida!
The cause of all this turned out to be painfully ordinary, according to the admin. The FAA said that legacy equipment on its telecommunications network became unstable when it was flooded with connection requests, roughly a thousand attempts every few seconds, disrupting radar feeds and aircraft communications. Investigators are looking at a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio site in Arkansas where the FAA's network contractor had been installing a new router.
[| | | | | Benny Johnson

| 2:37 PM * Nov 17, 2026 * 55.3K Views166 Replies * 90 Reposts * 543 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/b43a68a2-66ec-4820-86ef-26afebe6d81d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The agency says it has no indication of a cyberattack. In other words, the most advanced economy on earth lost control of its departures for an afternoon because old equipment could not handle a network hiccup.
This was not a fluke.
In September, flights into New York, Philadelphia, Boston and Washington were halted for eight hours after a Philadelphia facility's primary and backup data links both failed. Before that, repeated telecom failures at the same facility disrupted Newark for weeks. Our air traffic system is, as the president himself put it nearly a decade ago, "stuck, painfully, in the past."

## Trump saw this coming
On June 5, 2017, President Trump stood in the East Room and **[signed a letter to Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/fac0fd36-9379-4353-9028-063e51eef44a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** laying out principles for air traffic control reform. He warned that controllers were working with 1960s technology in outdated facilities, and that air traffic was only going to grow.
His fix was bold: move air traffic control out of the FAA into an independent, nonprofit corporation funded by user fees, as Canada had done, and leave the FAA to focus on safety oversight.
"Efficient operation of our airspace requires significant investments in rapidly evolving technology," Trump wrote in the letter. "In this environment, bureaucratic efforts are unlikely to succeed. That is why all other industrialized countries, with the exceptions of the United States and France, have separated their ATC functions from government. By taking that critical step, those countries have accelerated modernization, maintained or improved safety, and lowered operating costs."
Whatever you think of that model, the diagnosis was right. Republicans controlled the House, the Senate and the White House. It should have been the right moment to make a move.
## Why it died
It was not. Rep. Bill Shuster's 21st Century AIRR Act cleared the House Transportation Committee on a 32-25 vote but never reached the floor. Rural Republicans worried that a board shaped by the big airlines would raise costs and neglect small airports. **[More than 120 aviation groups](https://substack.com/redirect/c1a6a070-766b-4b66-a3e6-ac18baf8753f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , led by general and business aviation, lobbied against it. FAA unions opposed it. Democrats opposed it. The Senate never took it up.
In February 2018, **[Shuster gave up](https://substack.com/redirect/98d30adb-6d3f-4223-9fe0-00b590bce3b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , and Congress passed a routine FAA reauthorization instead. As Southwest's CEO put it at the time, the problem the day before was the lack of modernization, and the problem the day after still existed.
The real lesson of 2017 is that Washington let a fight over who should run air traffic control crowd out the one thing everyone agreed on: the equipment is failing and must be replaced.

## Why wasn't the job done in Trump's second term thus far?
To his credit, President Trump came back to the issue. After the deadly midair collision near Reagan National in January 2025, his administration announced a "Brand New Air Traffic Control System," and Congress **[included $12.5 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/15ca4254-6aa4-4135-b30b-41e987fc236c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for it in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that July. New radios, radars and fiber are going in.
But the administration itself calls that money a down payment. The FAA administrator has acknowledged that the first phase alone will **[cost about $16 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/0d535eba-b2f2-4183-a0ed-e04e59fbb038?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , and the full price tag is **[now estimated at $42.5 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/438f89e2-f798-40a7-9033-902c12f000bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. The remaining $30 billion, in Sen. Eric Schmitt's Modern Skies Act, was introduced only at the end of September and is sitting in committee. Federal auditors warn the FAA still lacks a reliable cost estimate or integrated schedule.
Air traffic control got a slice of a massive tax bill rather than becoming the president's signature fight, and the hardest part, the software and automation at the heart of the system, is still unfunded. That is not neglect. But it is not the urgency last Friday demands.
## Mr. President, finish the job
We know that some of President Trump's closest allies and operators read PolitiBrawl. If you are seeing this, please urge him to do the following.
President Trump, you diagnosed this problem in 2017. Today you have the bully pulpit and a Congress your party controls. Make the Modern Skies Act a top priority, demand a credible budget and timeline from the FAA, and do not let up until the job is done.
Also, you need to level with the American people.
On Friday, the FAA first cited "extraordinary circumstances," then a "temporary telecommunications outage," while the Department of Homeland Security blamed an outdated system. A fuller explanation came two days later. The same week, a Microsoft outage disrupted businesses, and the FBI, the NSA, the Pentagon and the nation's cyber-defense agency got on a call to compare notes.
Americans are anxious, and rumors fill silence fast. Say what you know, when you know it, and what you do not know yet. Transparency will build and maintain trust with the American people. Mixed messages and information voids will destroy it.

The Democrats are quick to blame Trump, but here is what they're not mentioning... | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? Who is really to blame for Friday's national crisis? The Democrats are quick to blame Trump, but here is what they're not mentioning... | | | Nov 17 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Help us beat and replace the mainstream media! Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today: Last Friday afternoon, every departing flight in the United States was held on the ground during a nationwide ground stop lasting more than four hours, the longest since September 11, 2001. By the end of the day, more than 9,100 flights had been canceled and more than 24,500 delayed. Mine was one of them. It was canceled again, and again. After the second cancellation, I stopped waiting for an airline to get me home. I got in a car in Fort Lauderdale and drove 22 hours to Washington, D.C. I was lucky. I got a car and could drive. Thousands of travelers were stuck in terminals with no clear answer about when they would get out. I saw a mother of small children breaking down, crying in the corner of the airport. A father of 3, waiting in the rental car pickup line with me, said his wife and kids were exhausted and huddled together upstairs, praying he could book one of the last rental cars to drive to Boston that night... from freaking Florida! The cause of all this turned out to be painfully ordinary, according to the admin. The FAA said that legacy equipment on its telecommunications network became unstable when it was flooded with connection requests, roughly a thousand attempts every few seconds, disrupting radar feeds and aircraft communications. Investigators are looking at a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio site in Arkansas where the FAA's network contractor had been installing a new router. The agency says it has no indication of a cyberattack. In other words, the most advanced economy on earth lost control of its departures for an afternoon because old equipment could not handle a network hiccup. This was not a fluke. In September, flights into New York, Philadelphia, Boston and Washington were halted for eight hours after a Philadelphia facility's primary and backup data links both failed. Before that, repeated telecom failures at the same facility disrupted Newark for weeks. Our air traffic system is, as the president himself put it nearly a decade ago, "stuck, painfully, in the past." PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. Trump saw this coming On June 5, 2017, President Trump stood in the East Room and laying out principles for air traffic control reform. He warned that controllers were working with 1960s technology in outdated facilities, and that air traffic was only going to grow. His fix was bold: move air traffic control out of the FAA into an independent, nonprofit corporation funded by user fees, as Canada had done, and leave the FAA to focus on safety oversight. "Efficient operation of our airspace requires significant investments in rapidly evolving technology," Trump wrote in the letter. "In this environment, bureaucratic efforts are unlikely to succeed. That is why all other industrialized countries, with the exceptions of the United States and France, have separated their ATC functions from government. By taking that critical step, those countries have accelerated modernization, maintained or improved safety, and lowered operating costs." Whatever you think of that model, the diagnosis was right. Republicans controlled the House, the Senate and the White House. It should have been the right moment to make a move. Why it died It was not. Rep. Bill Shuster's 21st Century AIRR Act cleared the House Transportation Committee on a 32-25 vote but never reached the floor. Rural Republicans worried that a board shaped by the big airlines would raise costs and neglect small airports. , led by general and business aviation, lobbied against it. FAA unions opposed it. Democrats opposed it. The Senate never took it up. In February 2018, , and Congress passed a routine FAA reauthorization instead. As Southwest's CEO put it at the time, the problem the day before was the lack of modernization, and the problem the day after still existed. The real lesson of 2017 is that Washington let a fight over who should run air traffic control crowd out the one thing everyone agreed on: the equipment is failing and must be replaced. (Piece continues below) We 're not giving up this fight, and neither should you The midterms were a wake up call to all American patriots... | | ---|---|--- The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington. They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain. This is what we believe in. We must fight for our nation with everything we've got, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did. PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news. We appreciate your readership and support. Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day. -The PolitiBrawl Editors (Piece continues): Why wasn't the job done in Trump's second term thus far? To his credit, President Trump came back to the issue. After the deadly midair collision near Reagan National in January 2025, his administration announced a "Brand New Air Traffic Control System," and Congress for it in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that July. New radios, radars and fiber are going in. But the administration itself calls that money a down payment. The FAA administrator has acknowledged that the first phase alone will , and the full price tag is . The remaining $30 billion, in Sen. Eric Schmitt's Modern Skies Act, was introduced only at the end of September and is sitting in committee. Federal auditors warn the FAA still lacks a reliable cost estimate or integrated schedule. Air traffic control got a slice of a massive tax bill rather than becoming the president's signature fight, and the hardest part, the software and automation at the heart of the system, is still unfunded. That is not neglect. But it is not the urgency last Friday demands. Mr. President, finish the job We know that some of President Trump's closest allies and operators read PolitiBrawl. If you are seeing this, please urge him to do the following. President Trump, you diagnosed this problem in 2017. Today you have the bully pulpit and a Congress your party controls. Make the Modern Skies Act a top priority, demand a credible budget and timeline from the FAA, and do not let up until the job is done. Also, you need to level with the American people. On Friday, the FAA first cited "extraordinary circumstances," then a "temporary telecommunications outage," while the Department of Homeland Security blamed an outdated system. A fuller explanation came two days later. The same week, a Microsoft outage disrupted businesses, and the FBI, the NSA, the Pentagon and the nation's cyber-defense agency got on a call to compare notes. Americans are anxious, and rumors fill silence fast. Say what you know, when you know it, and what you do not know yet. Transparency will build and maintain trust with the American people. Mixed messages and information voids will destroy it. | | POLL Were you affected by Friday's ground stop? | ? ? * You're currently a free subscriber to . 3rd, voters rejected Trump’s corruption. So why is Chuck Schumer already
waffling?

Right after voters handed Democrats the Senate majority, Schumer said he’d
let Trump’s nominees onto the federal bench as long as they’re not
“crappy.”

Really? That’s his standard for a lifetime appointment?

For years, Trump has run an assembly line for loyalist judges: he picks
them, and Senate Republicans rubber-stamp them. Next Congress, Democrats
will finally have the power to shut it down. Every nominee they block is
one fewer Trump pick shaping the law for decades.

And look at who Trump is nominating. His picks are so loyal to Trump, they
refuse to say he lost the 2020 election. They won’t even say January 6th
was an attack on the Capitol. They rule for corporations and Trump’s
billionaire friends. Again and again, they’ve shown they answer to Trump,
not to the Constitution or the people.

There is no such thing as a Trump judge who isn’t “crappy.” A standard
that loose leaves the door open for backroom deals on every single
nominee.

Trading away seats on the federal bench was always morally wrong. Now,
it’s politically toxic, too. Enough. Voters didn’t hand Democrats this
majority to wave Trump’s nominees through.

Demand Justice PAC is drawing a hard line for Chuck Schumer and every

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: [Petition] Medicare for All
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Healthcare is a human right. Let’s start treating it like one.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261117-6966-footer&t=1&akid=6966%2E420207%2Ea3hJqH)
Peter,
Trump’s Big Bad Betrayal Bill slashed Medicare and Medicaid, leaving Americans with sky high health insurance bills — or without healthcare altogether. And the real kicker? The bulk of these cuts haven’t even taken effect yet.
Our new Congress _must_ do everything in its power to repeal these cuts.
Voters showed up on Election Day and demanded change. Now, it’s time to deliver. We’re closer than ever to a healthcare system that guarantees every American gets the care they deserve. Without jumping through insurance company hoops. Without taking on unnecessary debt. Without skipping care or rationing prescriptions to make ends meet.
94% of Democrats, 60% of Independents, and 1 in 5 Republicans support Medicare for All. Our current ‘sick care’ system is not working. Insurance companies and Big Pharma continue to exploit working people, all while slashing coverage and increasing prices.
Americans are sick and tired of the rising costs. Americans are frustrated with the worsening care. Americans are ready for Medicare For All.
I have introduced Medicare For All in every legislative session of Congress. I am the lead sponsor of Medicare For All in the House. And I won’t stop until everyone has access to the healthcare they deserve.

Earlier this month, voters handed Donald Trump and the Republican Party a resounding rebuke.
#
Hi there,
**Quick reminder: Swing Left’s post-election Inside Update call is this Thursday, November 19th from 8-9pm EST.[Will you join us to hear about what’s next?](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3284?t=1&akid=3450%2E1562180%2EfsGIp0)**
**[RSVP »](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3284?t=2&akid=3450%2E1562180%2EfsGIp0)**
Earlier this month, voters handed Donald Trump and the Republican Party a resounding rebuke, flipping districts and states blue that Democrats haven’t won in a generation.
This community helped make that happen. Now we turn to the task of holding these majorities—because it’s far from guaranteed. After big wins in 2018 and 2020, Democrats lost the House in 2022 and then the Senate and White House in 2024. To ensure Democrats can deliver consistently and materially for the American people, we can’t let that happen again.
On Thursday’s virtual call, we’ll:
* Celebrate what we accomplished together in 2026
* Share what we learned from Ground Truth conversations with voters
* Give you a first look at Swing Left’s strategy for 2027 and 2028

**The work starts now, and we need you with us.[So RSVP for Thursday’s call today and get ready to talk about what’s next!](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3284?t=3&akid=3450%2E1562180%2EfsGIp0)**
We hope to see you there,
The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261117-1&t=4&refcode2=3450_1562180_fsGIp0&akid=3450%2E1562180%2EfsGIp0)
